sessions.title: 100 Million Bugs Later: A Field Report From the Agentic Era (sponsored by CodeRabbit)
sessions.abstract:
CodeRabbit reviews code generated by major coding agents: 30M+ pull requests and 200K+ independent code reviews each day across open source and enterprises. As agentic development accelerated, PR volume grew 4x while review rounds per PR fell 20%. AI-co-authored PRs carry about 1.7x more issues and up to 2.74x more security issues than human-written code.
David Loker, CodeRabbit VP of Applied AI, shares 12 months of review telemetry behind 100M caught bugs—and the enterprise pattern it reveals: heterogeneous coding-agent stacks are the end state. He introduces Agentic Change Management: an independent, agent-agnostic quality gate that assesses every change, surfaces what needs human attention, and explains what it approves. Leave with a vendor-neutral framework for scaling an agentic SDLC without sacrificing quality, security, or control. This presentation is brought to you by CodeRabbit, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: 10x Faster Vector Indexes: GPU Acceleration in Amazon OpenSearch with NVIDIA cuVS (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.abstract: At billion-vector scale, vector index construction can become a performance and cost bottleneck for retrieval, RAG, and AI workloads. Amazon OpenSearch Service Vector Acceleration uses NVIDIA cuVS to accelerate index construction, delivering up to 10x faster builds at a quarter of the indexing cost while preserving the OpenSearch experience. This 300-level session goes under the hood of the architecture: how eligible builds are offloaded to managed GPU workers, how cuVS and CAGRA accelerate graph construction through the Faiss backend, and how the graph is converted into an HNSW index for CPU-based search. We will examine how segment size, quantization, and ingestion patterns affect GPU utilization, build speed, and efficiency. Attendees will leave with guidance for identifying good-fit workloads, optimizing ingestion, and modeling performance and cost benefits for their own deployments. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: 5 Amazon ECS features that prevent common production incidents
sessions.abstract: Five configuration mistakes cause the majority of Amazon ECS production incidents. All five are fixable in under a minute. In this lightning talk, see the incident each feature prevents, the specific attribute to verify, and the fix. Leave with a production-readiness checklist your team can use before every release.

sessions.title: A closer look at AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.abstract: Lambda durable functions let you write reliable, long-running workflows as sequential code. Finally, we cover observability, a decision framework to help you choose when to use durable functions versus AWS Step Functions, and operational considerations like concurrency, cost, and versioning.

sessions.abstract: In this session, discover recently developed resilience mechanisms for DynamoDB workloads and how existing, advanced resilience patterns have been evolving. We'll cover Athena's latest innovations including Amazon S3 Tables integration for fully managed Iceberg tables and enhanced Spark notebooks.

Learn to optimize your applications for specific performance requirements, from cost-effective general storage to ultra-low latency implementations. sessions.title: Advanced vaulting: Ransomware resilience with AWS Backup
sessions.abstract: Bad actors increasingly target backups alongside production data, and organizations need a vaulting strategy that puts them out of reach. Isolation, immutability, and encryption form the pillars of that strategy, and this session dives deep into how to implement all three with AWS Backup. We'll cover logically air-gapped vault architecture, including how backups are stored in isolated, immutable infrastructure by default, encryption with AWS-owned and customer-managed keys, and durable recovery pathways with Multi-party approval. We'll also cover how these vaulting patterns feed into recovery workflows so that what's protected stays recoverable.

sessions.title: Agentic Memory: Build AI Agents That Learn from Every Interaction
sessions.abstract: Today's AI agents forget everything after each conversation ends. A customer calls back about the same issue for the third time, and the agent starts from zero. In this chalk talk, we explore how to architect persistent memory systems for Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, enabling them to remember customer preferences, recall prior issue context, and adapt resolution strategies over time. We walk through three memory patterns: episodic (past interactions), semantic (customer knowledge graphs), and procedural (learned resolution paths). We whiteboard real architectures using Customer Profiles, Bedrock knowledge bases, and DynamoDB to build agents that reduce repeat contacts and deliver personalized experiences, without retraining models. Bring your memory challenge and we'll design the persistence layer on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Agents can delete your data lake. Can you recover it? (sponsored by Rubrik)
sessions.abstract:
AI is multiplying the identities and agents that can change your AWS data. One over-scoped role or runaway agent can delete or overwrite the data your models depend on, in an S3 lake or Iceberg lakehouse. Replication copies a bad write, versioning is often off. How do you recover without a valid backup?

Resilience spans your estate. Hear how TGS built a ransomware-resilient platform with Rubrik. This presentation is brought to you by Rubrik, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Agents need names too: Open standards for agent discovery
sessions.abstract: As AI agents proliferate, the internet needs a decentralized way to name, discover, and trust them. sessions.title: Agents run at the edge. The blast radius lives in the cloud (sponsored by Sysdig)
sessions.abstract: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. Bring your own agents. Ask us what they can reach. This presentation is brought to you by Sysdig, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: AI agents are crawling your website? Identify, optimize, rate-limit, & monetize them
sessions.abstract: AI agents are the new web visitors, but how do you protect your content while unlocking new revenue? In this code talk, we deploy a Single Page Application on CloudFront, S3, API Gateway, Lambda, and Bedrock, then progressively secure and monetize AI agent traffic. We integrate AWS WAF Bot Control to identify agents via the WBA protocol, implement intelligent routing in CloudFront Functions to serve optimized content per visitor type, and enforce rate limits by bot identity and actual resource consumption. Finally, we enable AI Traffic Monetization in WAF and demonstrate end-to-end paid content access using the x402 payment protocol with a Bedrock AgentCore.

Join Ralph Gootee, CTO of Lennar, and Ariel Assaraf, CEO of Coralogix, for a practical look at moving AI from experimentation into production. They’ll share how Lennar is building and scaling AI agents on Amazon Bedrock, using AWS inference services and open-source models, and how Coralogix helps teams understand adoption, performance, cost, and business impact. This presentation is brought to you by Coralogix, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

sessions.title: AI Didn't Wait for Security: Now What?
sessions.abstract: AI didn't wait for your security review. Developers already ship code with agentic AI, coding assistants, and MCP servers without governance; blocking them lowers efficiency and leaves you falling behind. This builder-focused session dissects the architecture of a governed AI platform. You'll learn how to build a centralized MCP broker with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and Runtime, and how agent requests gain identity and permissions. You'll build and distribute a curated agentic skills catalog and reusable agentic blueprints. Finally, you'll see how AI SDLC frameworks bring consistency and higher-quality artifacts, with DevOps and security agents woven into key stages.

sessions.title: AI discipline: UCLA's data foundation and framework for saying no
sessions.abstract: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) invested in their data foundation first. Their large-scale data modernization—Bruin Cloud and the campus Data Hub—created a unified, governed data environment across a sprawling research university, but it wasn't enough. As AI demand surged, Deputy CIO Veronica Garcia and her team built a disciplined product management approach to evaluate, prioritize, and scale AI use cases against UCLA's mission. Learn how UCLA’s technical architecture accelerated data modernization, the framework used to determine AI priorities, and the governance model that keeps it all aligned that launched high-impact use cases from increasing fundraising, advancing research, and supporting student safety and success.

You leave with a working application built entirely through the AI-DLC methodology.

sessions.abstract: Choosing the right HPC configuration often requires extensive benchmarking across instance types, MPI implementations, core counts, and application-specific settings. Learn how AWS uses AI to predict optimal HPC configurations from historical workload data, helping engineers make informed decisions before launching large-scale jobs. We’ll cover the models behind these recommendations and demonstrate how AI reduces trial and error while improving performance, cost efficiency, and time to solution.

sessions.title: AI-driven serverless development with Kiro
sessions.abstract: What if an AI assistant could apply serverless patterns and best practices to help you build production-ready code faster? In this workshop, use Kiro to create a serverless application with authentication, tests, observability, and an optional CI/CD pipeline. Along the way, your AI assistant reviews and explains code, looks up configuration settings, and generates tests—accelerating your development workflow while teaching you serverless fundamentals. Whether you're new to serverless or looking to boost productivity, you'll walk away with a working application and practical AI-assisted development techniques. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: AI-Enabled SRE: Empowering Incident Commanders at Riot Games
sessions.abstract: Learn how Riot Games built an AI-powered post-incident review workflow within its LiveOps Process & Analytics (P&A) team using AWS AgentCore. Integrated with Datadog, Slack, Jira, and version-control sources, the platform orchestrates modular AI agents that gather evidence, validate incident impact, and generate structured reviews and RCA drafts. With humans in the loop to review and approve outputs, it accelerates analysis, reduces toil, and improves consistency—helping teams identify root causes and prevent recurrence. Beyond post-incident response, this work establishes a reusable foundation for standardizing and scaling AI-assisted operational workflows across LiveOps, enabling teams to adopt intelligent automation while maintaining human oversight.

sessions.title: AI flight plan: How British Airways’ parent builds and measures AI ROI (sponsored by NTT DATA)
sessions.abstract: British Airways’ parent, International Airlines Group (IAG), has moved rapidly from AI experimentation to production deployments delivering measurable results. This session explores how IAG and its partner NTT DATA assess AI opportunities by giving business units ownership of value realization, build momentum by prioritizing high-impact use cases, and operationalize AI through scalable technology, operating models, governance and change management. Attendees will learn how to connect AI strategy to top- and bottom-line impact through real-world examples, including procurement optimization, contract leakage detection and citizen-developed agents that accelerate safe, responsible AI adoption across the enterprise. This presentation is brought to you by NTT DATA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: AI for Impact: Elevating human potential through inclusive innovation
sessions.abstract: Learn how California's Department of Developmental Services (DDS) is leveraging AWS to modernize legacy systems and unify data for half a million individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities across 21 regional centers and acute care hospitals. See how this aligns with HR.1 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) requirements for government modernization within CA Health and Human Services. Explore responsible AI agents with fairness scoring and bias detection that improve equitable service delivery. Discover how multi-agent architectures on Amazon Bedrock enable transparent, auditable decisions for vulnerable populations — a replicable blueprint for ethical AI at scale.

sessions.title: AI Governance: The Framework, The Pitfalls, The Playbook (sponsored by Vanta)
sessions.abstract: The AI revolution is upending organizations’ security and GRC programs. Shadow AI is exploding as employees adopt new agent harnesses, workflows, platforms, and plugins. Even sanctioned AI poses new challenges that don’t yet have standardized solutions. Meanwhile, developers are moving AI applications from experimentation to production, introducing new risks. This session will break down what AI Governance is all about, cover common concerns that it’s meant to resolve, and provide attendees with practical tips for solving some of their most pressing AI Governance challenges. What you’ll learn. What AI Governance entails, from practical policy to active protections. How to solve AI Governance concerns across different layers of the AI stack. This presentation is brought to you by Vanta, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

sessions.title: AI innovations across network monitoring and operations
sessions.abstract: Join us to explore how AI is transforming network monitoring and observability. This session dives into new capabilities for traffic analysis, network health monitoring, and faster issue resolution that shows how intelligent, automated tooling helps you move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive insight. Whether you want to cut time-to-resolution or get a clearer, real-time pulse on your network's health, come see what's new and what's on the horizon.

sessions.title: AI is Breaking Data Security… And Fixing It (sponsored by Concentric AI)
sessions.abstract: AI is rapidly becoming one of the biggest drivers of productivity and innovation in the enterprise — and one of the fastest-growing sources of data security risk. As copilots, assistants, and public AI tools become integrated into daily work, sensitive data is flowing into systems that most security teams can’t fully see, understand, or control. The problem is that traditional data security controls were never built for this. In fact, many organizations were already struggling to operationalize data security before AI accelerated the challenge. The good news? AI isn’t just creating the problem — it’s also enabling a smarter, more effective way to solve it. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how AI is reshaping data security — and how they can use that same technology to gain control, minimize exposure, and support safer AI adoption across the business. This presentation is brought to you by Concentric AI, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

sessions.title: AI Is Getting Smarter. AI-Generated Code Isn’t Getting Safer. (sponsored by Veracode, Inc.)
sessions.abstract: AI-generated code is scaling fast, but its security performance is not keeping up. Across more than 100 models tested since 2023, the average security pass rate remains stuck at 56%, even as syntax performance approaches perfection. For security leaders, this is no longer a developer tooling discussion. It is a verification, release-control, and accountability issue. In this session, Veracode leaders unpack the findings from the 2026 GenAI Code Security Report and turn them into practical actions for secure software delivery at scale. Whether you’re a developer, security lead, or business decision-maker, this session will help you navigate the real-world security implications of GenAI in your development workflow. This presentation is brought to you by Veracode, Inc., an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

sessions.title: AI Meets Production: The New Reliability Playbook for Financial Services (sponsored by Traversal)
sessions.abstract: Financial services depend on software that needs to be available around the clock. When that software fails, the consequences can affect millions of customers and create regulatory, financial, and reputational risk. This panel brings together technology leaders from some of the world’s largest financial institutions across banking, payments, and investment management for a conversation moderated by Anish Agrawal, CEO & Cofounder of Traversal, the AI SRE helping diagnose, fix, and prevent incidents across complex enterprise environments. Together, they’ll discuss how AI is changing production reliability across financial services, where it’s already being used, the emerging role of AI SREs, what teams look for when evaluating new approaches, and what it takes to deploy AI safely in highly regulated environments. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: AIOPs for cloud data infrastructure (sponsored by NetApp)
sessions.abstract: Cloud data infrastructure rarely stays optimal — workloads change, configurations drift, and data infrastructure expertise is scarce. AIOps applies AI-powered, agentic automation to cloud data storage operations: continuously assessing the environment, analyzing it against workload-specific best practices, recommending fixes, and applying them at the level of autonomy you choose. In this lightning talk, we’ll explore how NetApp Workload Factory does all this while providing customers with right-sized cost, on-target performance, stronger resilience and protection — without the need for deep data infrastructure expertise, and while always staying in control. This presentation is brought to you by NetApp, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: AIOps for SAP on AWS: Proactive Log Intelligence with Amazon Bedrock Agents
sessions.abstract: SAP operations teams spend hours sifting through thousands of log lines to diagnose outages, often only after business impact has occurred. In this workshop, learn how to implement AI-powered operations for SAP workloads on AWS, whether customer-managed or RISE with SAP. Ingest SAP system logs into Amazon CloudWatch using the CloudWatch Agent and SAP ECS LogServ, then apply Amazon Bedrock–powered agents for proactive analysis and reactive root-cause investigation. See how AWS DevOps Agent extends this with autonomous remediation. Leave with a deployable architecture, real customer examples, and guidance to get started in days.

sessions.title: AIOps strategy: foundations before firefighting
sessions.abstract: Most teams turn on AI-driven operations before deciding what they actually want it to handle, investment is racing ahead of maturity. This chalk talk works through an AIOps strategy at the whiteboard, using real support-case patterns showing that most critical failures are catchable before they reach production. We map the two halves that teams miss: using AI to run operations and the operational foundations that let AI scale safely, such as cost, security, and organizational readiness. We discuss what to automate, what stays human, and where agents earn autonomy. Leave with a foundational framework and a maturity checklist for your team.

This session covers the evolution of AWS Partner Programs, from transactional resell to outcome-driven partnerships, and reveals which programs, incentives, enablement, and tools deliver the highest ROI. Discover how AI-powered differentiation lowers your cost of sales, attracts high-value customers, deepens relationships, and enables innovation at scale. sessions.title: AI Spreadsheets and the Modern Data Stack: An AWS Story (sponsored by Row Zero)
sessions.abstract: AWS relies on spreadsheets for planning, forecasting, business intelligence, and self service analytics. To improve self-serve data analysis, AWS rolled out Row Zero, a cloud-based AI spreadsheet that can open billion row datasets, connect directly to data warehouses, and provide enterprise grade security controls. This session covers how AWS solved their legacy spreadsheet problems that are constrained by the compute and memory resources of employee laptops and a 1 million row limit. By adopting Row Zero, business users can derive insights and have secure access to governed data in Amazon S3, Redshift, or Athena at massive scale. This presentation is brought to you by Row Zero, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: AI Systems Performance Engineering on AWS: A practitioner's deep dive
sessions.abstract: Extracting useful throughput from GPU clusters is a discipline: profile kernels, tune collectives, feed the GPUs, and survive the failures that compound with scale. In this workshop, you walk the full stack on Slurm-managed NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances — compute, network, and storage; the ML software stack from drivers to distributed frameworks — and stand up the observability that ties them together, from GPU, EFA, and Lustre counters to training throughput and MFU. At each layer: measure, attribute, fix with the tool that sees inside. Leave with dashboards you built yourself and a goodput methodology for your training clusters.

sessions.abstract: Join PwC and four leading clients across industries to hear real examples of how Amazon Connect is transforming customer experience and delivering business outcomes. This session showcases cutting-edge omnichannel solutions across voice, chat, and messaging, along with agentic AI capabilities driving automation in areas like order management and real-time updates. Hear how organizations are deploying next-generation, AI-powered voice solutions in production, with new innovations continuing to emerge. Discover how these advancements deliver measurable business value, backed by PwC's outcome-based approach that ties technology investment directly to efficiency gains and improved customer and business performance. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

sessions.title: AI Threat Readiness: Securing AWS Workloads at Machine Speed (sponsored by Wiz)
sessions.abstract: As AI accelerates development in the cloud, it’s also increasingly expanding the cloud attack surface. With autonomous agents accelerating both software deployment and vulnerability exploitation, traditional security workflows can no longer keep pace. Organizations need a new operating model for AI Threat Readiness inside high-velocity AWS environments that builds agentic trust without slowing innovation. This session explores how combining full AWS visibility with agentic workflows, including Wiz Red, Green, and Blue Agents, transforms reactive cloud security into proactive, machine-speed defense across Amazon Bedrock, containers, and serverless architectures. This presentation is brought to you by Wiz, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: AI Transformation: Redesigning How Work Gets Done (sponsored by Lucid Software)
sessions.abstract: Every major technology shift starts the same way. We use new technology to do the old thing. Early factories replaced steam engines with electric motors, but real transformation came when they redesigned the factory around what electricity made possible. We’re doing the same thing with AI. AI transformation isn’t about adding agents to existing workflows. It’s about redesigning how work gets done. That starts with context. In this session, we’ll show how teams can make work visible, give humans and AI a shared understanding of it, redesign workflows around agents, and turn that understanding into action. This presentation is brought to you by Lucid Software, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Partner Advantage Theater

sessions.title: AI Under Fire: How to Stop AI-Powered Attacks and Secure AI Coding (sponsored by Palo Alto Networks)
sessions.abstract: Frontier AI is transforming cyber threats, acting as a force multiplier across the kill chain. Adversaries leverage AI to scale social engineering, accelerate vulnerability discovery, and iterate malicious code. In this session, we highlight Palo Alto Networks’ approach to securing the frontier, by combining AI-powered Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW) and Frontier Virtual Patching (FVP) to preemptively block zero days, alongside identity controls and Secure AI Coding to protect developer workflows. Attendees will learn how threat intelligence and proactive defense outpace machine scale adversaries. This presentation is brought to you by Palo Alto Networks, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

sessions.title: AI Writes the Code. Who Reviews the Reviewer?
sessions.abstract: AI coding assistants now write, refactor, and even review code at scale but who's actually accountable when something breaks in production? This session explores how AI has reshaped the code review process: faster first-pass reviews, AI-generated suggestions, and agentic tools running directly in CI/CD pipelines. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

sessions.title: A leader's guide to advanced teams models in an agentic world
sessions.abstract: Agents made execution cheap. The work did not disappear. It moved into deciding what should exist, checking what agents produce, and owning it when something breaks. Most team designs were not built for that. This session gives you four questions to ask of any piece of work: what is it for, what does it touch, how will we check it, and whose name is on it. Then we walk through the team models leaders reach for, what each gets wrong, and where the pager and the name should sit. You leave knowing who does what now.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
sessions.abstract: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

sessions.title: A leader’s guide to governing AI, on behalf of humans
sessions.abstract:
AI deployments can reason, problem-solve, and act with increasing agency. Leaving governance models built for deterministic software no longer sufficient.
AWS Executive in Residence Ryan Seaman and Dr. Bernadette Han, organizational psychologist at the American Psychological Association (APA), bring technology and human behavior into one governance conversation. As AI interacts with people, influences decisions, and takes actions, governance must address not only what AI can do, but how it behaves with people and what happens as a result.
Bernadette introduces the EEI-AI Behavioral Architecture™, translating psychological science into behavioral requirements organizations can design for, test, observe, and govern responsibly.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
sessions.abstract: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
sessions.abstract: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
sessions.abstract: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

speakers.name: Sree Ratnasinghe
speakers.title: Director, Customer Solutions, AWS Strategic Accounts

sessions.title: A leader's guide to moving from AI investment gridlock to acceleration
sessions.abstract: Fund the platform or the use case? Demand proof before investing, or invest to generate the proof? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and can't wait for the annual budget cycle. To move at the pace of AI, the CIO and CFO must be in lockstep. Two former operators share how the best pairs manage AI like a venture portfolio: bets in the face of uncertainty, recycling of wins into the next ones, and governance that scales across the portfolio rather than project by project — plus the key questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to predicting and proving AI value
sessions.abstract: Every organization faces the same AI questions: How do we predict and manage costs? How do we prove value when outcomes are hard to measure? How do we move fast without losing control? Two finance leaders, one advising enterprise executives and one managing AI economics at scale inside Amazon, share what is working, what is not, and where teams go wrong. Learn how to measure AI cost and value in terms finance and technology leaders agree on, which guardrails to set as investment grows, and how to make the case for AI value to your board.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
sessions.abstract: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

speakers.name: Romeo Romeo
speakers.title: VP, AI Ventures and Tech M&A

speakers.name: Simone Zucchet
speakers.title: Head of UKI SA - Advertising, Publishing and Information Services

sessions.title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
sessions.abstract: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.

speakers.name: Daniel Slater
speakers.title: Executive in Residence; Worldwide Head, Culture of Innovation

sessions.title: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
sessions.abstract: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
sessions.abstract: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
sessions.abstract: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
sessions.abstract: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
sessions.abstract: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

sessions.title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
sessions.abstract: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

sessions.title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.

sessions.title: Allocate shared AWS infrastructure costs to your business units
sessions.abstract: Shared Amazon S3 buckets, Amazon EKS clusters, and network resources improve efficiency but can obscure which applications and business units drive spend. In this session, learn how to attribute shared costs based on actual usage. Follow a practical example using AWS Split Cost Allocation Data for S3 and EKS and Flexible Cost Allocation for networking. Then use AWS Cost Categories and Data Exports to combine each business unit’s share of storage, compute, and networking spend into a unified view. Walk away with a repeatable approach to showback and chargeback across your shared AWS environment.

sessions.title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
sessions.abstract: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Amazon Aurora architecture patterns for open table format analytics
sessions.abstract: Modern analytics architectures increasingly rely on open table formats like Apache Iceberg but combining operational and analytical data remains complex. This session explores emerging patterns for bridging Amazon Aurora with open table format analytics. Learn architectural patterns for bidirectional data flow between databases and data lakes. Topics include design patterns for analytical workloads, performance optimization and reverse ETL, and deep dives into maintaining transactional consistency when streaming database changes to Amazon S3 Tables, delivery guarantees, and type mapping.

sessions.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL: A developer's perspective
sessions.abstract: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

sessions.title: Amazon Aurora HA and DR design patterns for global resilience
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.

sessions.title: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
sessions.abstract: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

sessions.title: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
sessions.abstract: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.

sessions.title: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
sessions.abstract: Amazon EC2 continues to push the boundaries of cloud compute. Join this session to explore the latest innovations — from new AWS Graviton processors to the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances built for demanding workloads. Hear how customers are using EC2 to accelerate application development, high-performance computing, and AI inference on the CPU. Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers strong isolation and performance, and leave with practical guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.

sessions.title: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

sessions.abstract: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

sessions.title: Amazon EVS: How to deploy & operate your VMware stack in the cloud
sessions.abstract: What if you could rapidly migrate your VMware-based workloads to the cloud without giving up control over how you build, configure, and operate your environment? Amazon EVS lets you run the latest VMware Cloud Foundation software within your Amazon VPC using EC2 bare-metal instances. Use the tools and processes your team already knows, now backed by AWS scale and flexibility. Retain control of your virtualization stack, from networking and storage to disaster recovery. We'll walk through deployment workflows and integration patterns with AWS Partners and native AWS services. Hear lessons from a customer who fast-tracked their migration with EVS.

sessions.abstract: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. In this session, learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals — wherever they are. Walk away with a clear understanding of Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide. This presentation is brought to you by Amazon Leo, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Amazon Linux: Securing and scaling your workloads on AWS
sessions.abstract: Amazon Linux powers the majority of workloads on AWS, from containers and AI/ML to enterprise applications and managed services. In this session, we introduce Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027), cover its security enhancements, optimizations, and key features. Learn how AL2027 addresses the needs of modern AI/ML and container workloads, and what the roadmap means for your infrastructure planning. Whether you are planning a migration or evaluating your OS strategy, this session is for you.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
sessions.abstract: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
sessions.abstract: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
sessions.abstract: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.

sessions.title: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
sessions.abstract: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.abstract: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.

sessions.title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
sessions.abstract: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

sessions.title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
sessions.abstract: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

sessions.title: An Epic Tale: Hyperscale Storage & Compute for the Fortnite Ecosystem
sessions.abstract: The metaverse will not be built by one studio. It will be built by thousands of teams shipping petabytes of content, running millions of build and render jobs across regions every day. The engineers behind Lore, Epic's distributed version control system for massive binary repositories, and Overmind, a multi-region ephemeral compute orchestrator, reveal the AWS architecture that makes it possible: self-managed scheduling on EC2, S3/DynamoDB/Keyspaces/Aurora for the data plane, EKS-hosted control planes running durable workflows, and MSK for replayable event streams. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and lessons on tenant isolation, regional sovereignty, and global platform scale.

sessions.title: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver single-digit millisecond performance at any scale - whether your application has tens of thousands or hundreds of millions of simultaneous users - for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn how some basic data structure decisions led to these characteristics. And how those same decisions provide immutable, point-in-time restore. Leave with a better understanding of why DynamoDB can operate at the scale it does, and a framework on how to use it for decisions in your own applications.

sessions.title: Answering CX questions 10x faster with Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Amazon Connect Customer generates a deep set of signals from every customer interaction. Sentiment, intent, conversation analytics, resolution outcomes. It's all there and Connect Customer gives you built-in tools to explore it. But we wanted to go further. We wanted anyone in the organization to ask questions about customer interactions in plain language and get answers instantly. So we paired Connect Customer's analytics data lake with Amazon Quick. In this session, we walk through how we did it, including how we handled cross-account Lake Formation access, and show how our broader team now asks questions and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster from question to action.

sessions.title: Aon: Turning raw exposure data into faster underwriting
sessions.abstract: Insurers and brokers process thousands of Statements of Values annually, complex unstructured documents that require manual extraction and validation and delay quoting and bind decisions. In this lightning talk, learn how Aon built an AI-powered exposure data ingestion platform on Amazon Bedrock using Anthropic Claude, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. See how the platform transforms unstructured data into standardized, risk-ready information with improved address quality, geocoding precision, and hazard identification, reducing document processing from days to minutes and feeding higher-quality inputs to catastrophe models.

sessions.title: Apache Iceberg V3 on AWS: Lower Costs, Better Lakehouse Performance
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg V3  is now production-ready, and adopting deletion vectors, row lineage, and new  data types across your lakehouse requires careful planning. In this session,  explore implementation patterns using Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, Amazon Athena,  and Amazon S3 Tables. Learn when deletion vectors outperform copy-on-write,  how row lineage enables compliance without extra pipelines, and how V3  incremental processing cuts batch costs. Leave with a practical migration strategy for your Iceberg upgrade.

sessions.title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg V4 is the biggest architectural evolution of the format, shifting from batch-first to real-time ready. Explore how single-file commits eliminate metadata bottlenecks for streaming ingestion, how Parquet-based metadata and redesigned content statistics accelerate query planning, and how relative paths make tables portable across regions and clouds without costly rewrites. We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

sessions.abstract: Aperf is an open-source project created by AWS to accelerate the performance debugging process by enabling experienced users to deep dive into extensive data and less experienced users to identify issues without specialized knowledge. sessions.abstract: Every organization bleeds knowledge when people leave. For mission-driven teams, a single departure can erase years of context from codebases, runbooks, and integrations. Configure steering files that encode your team's conventions, connect MCP servers to pull context from docs and APIs, and deploy subagents that generate living architecture diagrams and knowledge bases as your code evolves. This chalk talk provides hands-on guidance for implementing essential safeguards through S3 Versioning, Replication, Object Lock, and Resource Control Policy guardrails, plus techniques for recovering from unwanted changes across large datasets. We also cover how GuardDuty Malware Protection for AWS Backup lets you verify data is malware-free before restoring. Whether you’re meeting compliance requirements or ensuring business continuity, leave with actionable steps from basic backup policies to advanced immutability and malware-scanning controls.

Beyond the mechanics, you'll implement real-world migration strategies and learn how to choose among them based on downtime tolerance, writer constraints, and data volume. You'll leave with a repeatable playbook for migrating your data lake to Iceberg with minimal risk and zero data loss.

sessions.title: A practitioner’s guide to data for agentic AI
sessions.abstract: In this session, gain the skills needed to deploy end-to-end agentic AI applications using your most valuable data. This session focuses on data management using processes like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and provides concepts that apply to other methods of customizing agentic AI applications. Discover best practice architectures using AWS database services like Amazon Aurora, DynamoDB, and Neptune, along with analytical, data processing and streaming experiences found in SageMaker. Learn data lake, governance, and data quality concepts and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, and other features tie solution components together.

sessions.title: A practitioner’s guide to migrating from 3rd-party CDN and WAF to AWS
sessions.abstract: Considering migrating from a third-party CDN/WAF provider to AWS services? In this chalk talk, we’ll walk through the migration phases together: defining success criteria, running low-risk proof of concepts, designing your target architecture with Amazon Route 53, Amazon CloudFront, AWS WAF, and edge compute, executing the DNS cutover, and managing post-migration operations. Most of this session is open discussion: you bring your questions and stories, and we’ll share what we’ve learned running these migrations in production.

sessions.title: Architect AI-powered analytics with Amazon Quick across your data platforms
sessions.abstract: As organizations adopt AI-powered analytics, they need architectures that connect BI and conversational AI experiences to their existing data platforms. In this session we'll diagram architectural patterns for connecting Amazon Quick to structured data sources and integrating with third-party catalogs and semantic layers. We'll compare the available connectivity approaches, including data sources and MCP-based action connectors, and discuss when to use each. Considerations will span production use cases like BI dashboards, embedded analytics, text-to-SQL Q&A, and agentic workflows. Together we'll tackle real-world integration challenges including authentication, performance optimization, and governance. This session is ideal for architects and technical leaders looking to build AI-powered analytics across their data platforms.

sessions.title: Architect and optimize your VMware environment on Amazon EVS
sessions.abstract: Dive deep into the architectural decisions that shape a resilient, high-performing VMware environment on Amazon EVS. Explore VCF 9 support, Windows Server license-included entitlements, networking designs, storage configurations tuned for performance and cost, and operational patterns for backup, patching, and disaster recovery. Hear from a customer running production workloads on EVS and leave with actionable architectures tailored to your VMware workloads.

sessions.title: Architect for production AI: A decision framework that scales
sessions.abstract: Organizations deploying AI face a critical decision at every step. Which service handles which job, and will those decisions hold up as you scale? This chalk talk delivers an opinionated decision framework for choosing between Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI, and when to combine both for unified security, governance, and models that move between services without rearchitecting. We cover model access patterns (API, custom model import, marketplace), deployment trade-offs between self-managed and fully managed inference, and cost-performance optimization at production scale.

sessions.title: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
sessions.abstract: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios, such as credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse. We'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.

sessions.title: Architecting Enterprise Agents on Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.

sessions.title: Architecting firewalls on AWS: a layered defense strategy
sessions.abstract: With automated traffic now more than half of the web, a single firewall layer can't separate good bots from L7 attacks. This chalk talk covers how AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall work together. We cover deployment patterns for internet-facing apps, outbound controls, and workload segmentation, including firewall patterns attached to AWS Transit Gateway. Then we dig into the tradeoffs, including centralized versus distributed inspection, cost versus latency, and when one service can carry the load and when you need both. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we whiteboard a design for your environment.

sessions.title: Architecting for digital sovereignty: Choosing your AWS hybrid cloud infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Digital sovereignty requirements vary widely across government, defense, healthcare, and financial services. This session uses real-world case studies to compare the architectures of AWS Dedicated Local Zones and AWS Outposts, whether deployed in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud or in AWS Regions. It examines how data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and cryptographic key management differ across these options. It then shows how to configure account access, data residency controls, and network ingress and egress policies for strict and moderate requirements. Finally, it covers how to detect and prevent unauthorized data flows between hybrid infrastructure, the parent Region, and on-premises environments.

sessions.title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
sessions.abstract: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

sessions.title: Architecting for resilience and data residency
sessions.abstract: Your data can't leave the jurisdiction, but your workload still has to survive a Region degradation. This chalk talk explores architecture patterns that address both resilience and data residency together. We break the challenge into practical layers: where data lives, how workloads recover, what isolation looks like, and how to maintain business continuity across geographic boundaries. We map each layer to AWS capabilities including Dedicated Local Zones, Outposts, and policy controls, then work through real scenarios together. Bring your architecture challenges and we will whiteboard design patterns and tradeoffs with you.

sessions.title: Architecting for six nines with multi-region hedging (sponsored by Capital One)
sessions.abstract: Traditional disaster recovery assumes you can afford a recovery window. At six nines, your entire annual downtime budget is 31 seconds, a single failover event can consume it all. In this session, learn how to eliminate recovery windows entirely and make regional impairments invisible to customers without operational intervention. Explore a decision framework for selecting multi-region topologies based on simultaneous failure tolerance, data consistency, and cost tradeoffs. See how cell-based architecture limits blast radius and continuous fault injection proves resilience before incidents occur. Walk away with a pattern selection model you can apply to your own mission-critical workloads to move beyond failover toward true continuous availability. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Architecting for ultra-low latency on AWS Outposts with accelerated networking
sessions.abstract: This session covers networking on second-generation AWS Outposts, from scalable multi-site topologies to ultra-low-latency bare-metal deployments for financial trading. It starts with the second-generation dedicated network rack, local gateway routing domains for segmentation, and intra-VPC and inter-VPC communication. It then expands to multi-site interconnections spanning Outposts and AWS Local Zones, extended VPC designs, and resilient architectures grounded in AWS Well-Architected principles. It closes with bare-metal instances using high-throughput accelerated networking, kernel bypass, network interface card (NIC) selection, and rack topology for co-located workloads where every microsecond matters.

sessions.title: Architecting vector-driven AI applications with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Vector search is the engine behind intelligent AI, transforming data into meaning-driven insights that power smarter search, recommendations, and generative experiences. In this session, discover how to combine cost-optimized, fully elastic vector storage delivered by Amazon S3 Vectors with multimodal embedding models in Amazon Bedrock to extract and index text and image semantics at scale. Learn how to leverage S3 Vectors with popular AWS AI services to power AI-driven applications that can efficiently search through large vector datasets. Whether you’re building media search applications or search-enabled AI, you’ll learn how to optimize your use of S3 Vectors.

sessions.title: Architecting video search at trillion scale with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Storing and querying 1.5 trillion vectors demands rethinking traditional vector database architecture. Join this talk to learn how Bright Data built its video search retrieval layer on Amazon S3 Vectors, covering index partitioning across massive collections, embedding storage layout for sub-second nearest-neighbor queries, and cost/latency trade-offs versus dedicated vector databases at this scale. Bright Data walks through its approach to sharding, metadata filtering, and query routing, with benchmarks comparing throughput and cost per million queries. You'll leave with concrete architectural patterns for evaluating S3 Vectors in large-scale search, RAG, or embedding retrieval systems.

Connect directly with AWS Marketplace subject-matter experts to evaluate approaches for your business, validate your listing strategy, and identify opportunities to simplify the customer experience. sessions.title: Architect Oracle Database@AWS for resiliency and scale
sessions.abstract: Dedicated Exadata infrastructure inside AWS data centers gives Oracle workloads full feature compatibility alongside cloud native flexibility, but architecting for resiliency at scale demands deliberate design choices. In this session, explore architecture patterns for primary and disaster recovery deployments on Oracle Database@AWS, including strategies for multi-terabyte migration and managing petabyte-scale Oracle estates. Join a live whiteboarding discussion where AWS experts cover ODB@AWS deployment options, DR configurations, and operational design choices. Architect with validated best practices drawn from real customer deployments.

sessions.title: Architect production MCP servers on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Your MCP server works perfectly on a single Amazon ECS task. Then agents multiply, sessions collide, and scaling breaks everything. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the infrastructure patterns that make MCP servers production-ready on Amazon ECS. We'll cover horizontal scaling with externalized session state, request routing, fine-grained authentication, and autoscaling based on agent request patterns. We'll discuss multi-service topologies where different tool categories run as independent ECS services behind a shared ingress layer. Bring your current MCP architecture, and we'll design the production upgrade together.

sessions.title: Architect resilient agentic systems: Patterns beyond the happy path
sessions.abstract:
Every agentic system works on the happy path. The real test is what happens when your AI agent times out mid-reasoning, returns a malformed action, or cascades a single failure across an entire chain. In this session, you implement four resilience patterns built for non-deterministic agents: circuit breakers that trip on semantic failure, fallback hierarchies from AI to rules to human, bulkhead isolation between agents, and timeout budgets for chain-of-thought latency. Leave with a decision framework mapping failure modes to pattern combinations you can implement immediately.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Architect resilient, multi-region workforce access on AWS
sessions.abstract: Most AWS workforce access hinges on a single Region and a single identity provider. When either one goes down, everyone who signs in is affected—developers can't ship, DevOps engineers can't deploy, and administrators may be locked out just when they need access most. This session applies defense in depth across four layers: IAM Identity Center multi-Region replication, direct IAM federation through AD FS, Regional AWS STS endpoints, and break-glass IAM users. You learn how to decide which layers your environment needs, the order to fail over in, and how to test the full path without disrupting production.

sessions.title: Architectural patterns for predictable multi-agent costs at scale
sessions.abstract: Agents consume several times more tokens than chat interactions, and multi-agent coordination pushes that higher. Monitoring alone isn't enough to manage costs, token economics must be considered when building agents. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard architectural patterns that improve token economics for multi-agent applications, covering orchestration design decisions (orchestrator-subagent, generator-verifier, shared state) and how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's temporal policies and cost optimization features improve cost-determinism. We'll illustrate these patterns with practical examples, then open the whiteboard for attendees to share their challenges and solutions.

sessions.title: Architect your metadata hub with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.abstract: Your data is scattered across warehouses, lakes, databases, and streams. In this session, learn how AWS Glue Data Catalog serves as a single metadata hub that connects all of your data, enforces consistent governance across it, and makes it discoverable across engines and teams. See how to enrich, curate, and share metadata at scale, and give AI agents the context they need to get work done accurately and efficiently. Ideal for data engineers, architects, and platform teams.

sessions.title: A responsible AI challenge: Audit your agentic AI before the regulator does
sessions.abstract: Accuracy is necessary, but it isn't enough for agentic systems. Your agents can handle most requests correctly and still fail when someone asks how a decision was made, who approved it, or how to override it. In this hands-on workshop, you inherit a multi-agent claims system seeded with responsible AI gaps. Using the Well-Architected Responsible AI governance skill in your IDE, you audit the code against responsible AI dimensions like fairness, transparency, and accountability, investigate what you find, fix it, and generate an evidence-backed report. Walk away with a repeatable audit workflow you can run on your own agentic systems.

sessions.title: Ask the News: Making Decades of Publisher Content Instantly Searchable (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.abstract: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. Featuring ArcXP, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Assess your workloads with SELinux compatibility on Amazon Linux 2027
sessions.abstract: AL2027 preview enforces SELinux by default. In this session, deploy an application that hits SELinux denials, learn to read audit logs, diagnose the root cause, and write a custom policy that resolves it. You will leave with the practical skills to adopt AL2027's security defaults.

sessions.title: Assume breach, prove recovery: A ransomware resilience workshop
sessions.abstract: Most organizations have backups. Few can prove clean recovery after ransomware, and regulators now demand exactly that proof. In this hands-on workshop, you configure a resilient backup architecture on AWS using vaults and immutable storage. You then experience a simulated ransomware event, validate that your recovery infrastructure held, restore to an isolated clean room environment, and scan recovered resources for attacker persistence using GuardDuty Malware Protection. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.

sessions.abstract: Can an AI system move beyond answering questions to actually conducting research alongside you? We built one. AtoZ AI Co-Scientist is a multi-agent orchestration platform where specialized agents collaborate through a unified interface to discover literature, synthesize knowledge via graph-routed retrieval, generate hypotheses, implement baselines from papers, and run experiments autonomously. In this chalk talk, we dissect the compositional architecture, the graph-routed retrieval system achieving <200ms with structural signals flat search cannot capture, and Co-Scientist Bench—our agent-agnostic evaluation framework. Bring hard questions about reliability, memory, and human oversight.

Join The Access Group CTO Thad Széll and Coralogix CEO Ariel Assaraf to learn how unified telemetry is moving the business from reactive troubleshooting to continuous product improvement. Hear how it is sharpening decisions, focusing teams on what matters most, and creating the trusted data foundation needed to advance The Access Group’s AI ambitions. sessions.title: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
sessions.abstract: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.
