AT&T shares how they're deploying Interconnect last-mile to expand their connectivity portfolio. They'll also share how they're working with Amazon Leo to bring broadband satellite connectivity to underserved locations. Leave with a clear model for extending your own connectivity offerings.

We'll diagram a reference architecture covering control, data, and governance planes, walk through real-world authentication flows and discuss how to design policies that control which workloads can access which external credentials.

You leave ready to apply these patterns to your own agentic AI systems.

sessions.title: Automate AI governance and risk management with John Deere
sessions.abstract: Governance frameworks designed for static deployments struggle to keep pace with AI systems that learn, adapt, and act autonomously. sessions.abstract: Every minute of downtime is a minute your customers notice. What if an agent could correlate your logs, metrics, and change history the moment an application fails? In this hands-on lab, use AWS DevOps Agent to autonomously investigate operational issues across your AWS environment. Trigger investigations from simulated application failures, observe the agent correlate logs, metrics, and change history in real time, and review root cause analyses with actionable mitigation plans.

By the end, you'll know how to turn raw patch data into audit-ready answers on demand.

sessions.abstract: Security testing shouldn't require weeks of manual effort anymore. In this hands-on lab, configure and execute automated penetration tests using AWS Security Agent. Analyze findings with CVSS scores and reproduction steps, then generate actionable reports for your development teams.

sessions.abstract: Managing Savings Plans well is a continuous job. In this chalk talk, we discuss approaches to making commitment purchases more intelligent and less manual. We will cover how you can build a purchasing cadence that incorporates your organization's demand patterns through automation and the right level of human oversight. We'll also cover Automation, a feature within AWS Compute Optimizer that enables you to apply optimization recommendations to your AWS resources, which can help you reduce costs and improve performance. sessions.title: Automate threat detection and response across your logs
sessions.abstract: Security teams cannot manually hunt through every log for the one event that matters, and threats move faster than analysts can query. In this hands-on builders session, you will build automated detection and response on your security telemetry: metric filters and anomaly detectors that flag suspicious activity, findings routed to alarms that page the right people, and automated remediation that acts before an analyst logs in. After tuning detections to cut false positives, walk away with a pipeline that watches your logs so your team does not have to.

sessions.title: Automate your AWS partnership with a unified agentic operating model
sessions.abstract: Getting the most from your AWS partnership requires thoughtful and sustained engagement from both sides. Instead of heavy manual lifts, an agentic partner operating model supports this engagement at scale through strategic automation, delivering the right guidance, insight, and capabilities to team members who need them most. In this workshop, build a unified agentic operating model that connects pipeline, co-sell coordination, and AWS consumption measurement into a single orchestration layer using your CRM, AWS Partner Central, and Amazon Quick, enabling all team members to easily leverage AWS tools, insights, and investments from one agentic surface to increase your AWS engagement.

sessions.title: Automate your business processes with workflow agents on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: The agents with the clearest ROI don't wait for a prompt. They wake on an event and run a process to completion. A new lead triggers a prospecting agent, a filed ticket triggers IT resolution, a spend threshold triggers a campaign adjustment. This session covers best practices for building workflow agents on AgentCore: triggering agents from event sources, running long tasks asynchronously on Runtime, connecting to systems of record through gateway, holding state with memory, adding human-in-the-loop approvals, and enforcing actions with policies the agent cannot bypass.

sessions.title: Automate your landing zone and network migration with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Designing landing zones and translating on-premises networks into cloud-native architectures is complex and time-consuming. AWS Transform automates both. In this workshop, you'll see the landing zone agent analyze your requirements and deploy AWS Control Tower, organizational units, service control policies, and workload accounts as infrastructure as code. Then the network agent translates VMware networking components or firewall configurations into VPCs, subnets, security groups, and transit gateways with hub-and-spoke or isolated topologies, ready for deployment in CDK or Terraform modules. Laptop required.

times.room: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano IV

sessions.title: Automating data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg
sessions.abstract: Join this session to experience the power of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive in to an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline - governed end-to-end through AWS Glue Data Catalog - where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint on how to unify DataOps, MLOps, and FinOps for their data pipelines, with Glue Data Catalog as the metadata backbone tying governance, lineage, and discovery together across the pipeline.

sessions.title: Automating macOS at scale: AMI build, TCC, and provisioning on EC2 Mac
sessions.abstract: Automating macOS in the cloud brings challenges Linux and Windows don't. Going from a fresh EC2 Mac instance to a production-ready fleet means clearing non-obvious hurdles: building AMIs with EC2 Image Builder and Packer, pre-approving TCC permissions, bootstrapping Systems Manager, and working with Apple's security model. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through the real friction points teams hit: image pipelines, the TCC dialog problem, remote access, MDM enrollment, and fleet provisioning. Bring your toughest macOS automation questions; most of the session is open Q&A.

sessions.title: Automating Serverless migrations at scale with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Runtime deprecations pile up. API migrations stall. Legacy code sits untouched because manual upgrades across hundreds of functions take weeks your team doesn't have. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to assess, plan, and execute Lambda runtime upgrades and API migrations at scale. Working hands-on, you'll run the full agentic loop: codebase assessment, transformation planning, incremental code changes committed to Git, and self-validating test execution. You'll scale transformations across hundreds of functions in parallel using AWS Batch and Fargate. Walk away with patterns for automated, large-scale modernization. Bring your laptop.

See how New Relic's Intelligent Observability Platform integrates with AWS DevOps Agent to: Autonomously triage incidents, pinpoint root cause, and deliver actionable remediation with no custom tooling required. Investigate incidents agentically correlating telemetry, code, and deployments across AWS, multi cloud, and on-prem environments. Demonstrate how this innovation proactively prevents future incidents by analyzing patterns and recommending improvements. Learn how customers are cutting MTTR by 75% and shifting from firefighting to prevention, and walk away ready to get started. This presentation is brought to you by New Relic, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: Maintaining performance for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS often requires manual effort, such as tuning queries, managing indexes, and handling alerts. sessions.abstract: To achieve the operational agility markets require, manufacturers are turning to AI agents that can reason and act autonomously across the product lifecycle. This session demonstrates how to rapidly build autonomous multi-agent systems using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Kiro that connect CMMS, MES, and ERP systems through Model Context Protocol (MCP). Watch a live demo where we use Kiro to develop specialized manufacturing agents that detect anomalies, diagnose root causes, and orchestrate corrective actions autonomously. Leave with proven architecture patterns that you can apply to transform your production planning, supply chain optimization, and anomaly management processes.

sessions.abstract: Operations teams face a growing volume of production incidents, but investigating root cause manually is slow and doesn't scale. At Banco BMG, one of Brazil's most established financial institutions with more than 9 million customers, roughly 350 operational events occurred daily, each investigation taking hours. In this lightning talk, see how AWS DevOps Agent began investigating these events autonomously, reducing root cause identification from hours to minutes. Learn to integrate the agent with your observability tools, correlate telemetry, logs, and code, and turn every investigation into compounding efficiency that lowers MTTR.

sessions.title: Autonomous Remediation with OpenTelemetry and DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: You instrumented everything. You have metrics, logs, and traces. And when production breaks a human still has to piece it together, tab by tab, signal by signal, under pressure. That is not an observability problem, it’s an automation problem. We'll show you an architecture on AWS that closes it. OpenTelemetry captures signals across EKS, ECS, and Lambda. AWS DevOps Agent runs the investigation, finds the root cause, and prepares the fix. By the time a human looks at it, the pull request is ready. Come learn the triggers, investigation loop, and guardrails you need before letting an agent touch production.

sessions.abstract: The legacy ERP system that once gave you a competitive edge may now be limiting your ability to innovate. Modernizing SAP can be complex, expensive, risky, and every delay is a missed opportunity to innovate. In this Chalk Talk, you will learn how AI Agents can make it possible to upgrade to SAP's Cloud ERP safely and cost-effectively in weeks, not months. Whether you're running SAP ECC, moving to RISE with SAP, modernizing ABAP and PI/PO, or migrating SAP Business Warehouse (BW), discover how AI-powered agents can take on the heavy lifting for you

sessions.title: AWS AI Factories: Bring production scale AI to your data center
sessions.abstract: Data sovereignty, data gravity, and latency requirements prevent many organizations from running all AI workloads in the public cloud. AWS AI Factories bring AWS and NVIDIA AI infrastructure directly into your data center, fully operated, maintained, and continuously updated by AWS. Run leading foundation models on premises for training and inference without building and managing AI infrastructure yourself or negotiating separate agreements with model providers. In this session, learn how organizations are accelerating AI adoption, reducing time to value, and maintaining full control of their data while benefiting from the AWS experience in their own facilities.

sessions.title: AWS AI from chips to agents: The end-to-end production AI foundation
sessions.abstract: The AI experiment is over. Now it has to work. This session walks through the AWS AI Platform end-to-end, starting at the chip layer with AWS Trainium and AWS Graviton delivering up to 40% better price performance. From there, model inference and customization through Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker AI. Then production agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Every layer co-designed so workloads move across the stack without rearchitecting. You will leave knowing which service handles which job, where the layers connect to accelerate production timelines, and how to keep your architecture open as your AI strategy evolves.

sessions.title: AWS AI League: Build agents with AgentCore (Agentic Football Cup)
sessions.abstract: Coordinating agents is where multi agent systems break. They duplicate work, drop handoffs, and burn tokens. In this workshop, build and deploy five autonomous agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Kiro and the Strands Agents SDK, then field them five versus five in live Agentic Football matches. Write the tools your agents call, orchestrate multi turn reasoning across a maze like arena, and solve coordination problems that decide the match. Tune prompts, roles, and tactics between rounds and watch your score climb a live leaderboard. Leave with working code, production ready multi agent patterns, and a shot at the Finale.

sessions.title: AWS AI League: Build domain specific AI with Forge
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop you’ll compete head-to-head with other builders to build your own domain specific AI. You’ll tackle real-world challenges as you generate synthetic datasets, experiment with model customization, and fine-tune models to improve accuracy, clarity, and relevance. You’ll learn just how accessible and cost-effective AI customization can be. Whether you’re chasing the championship or simply sharpening your AI expertise, this session delivers practical techniques you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate

sessions.title: AWS AI League Championship Grand Finale: Agentic Football Cup
sessions.abstract:
Experience the ultimate AI showdown from your theater seat as fifty finalists from the AWS AI League season battle head-to-head in real time for the $50,000 championship prize.

This electrifying viewing experience offers ML practitioners, developers, and AI enthusiasts unique insights into agent orchestration, model customization, and multi-agent coordination at scale, as five-versus-five AI agent squads face off live in Agentic Football, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK.

sessions.title: AWS AI League: Train with RLVR on SageMaker, deploy in AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Turn a generic model into one that wins on your task, and prove it with data. In this hands-on workshop, you customize a foundation model on Amazon SageMaker AI using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), with no infrastructure to manage. Then you build an agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that orchestrates the model end to end: preparing datasets, triggering training, registering models, evaluating with LLM-as-a-Judge, and deploying to a real-time endpoint. Your score posts to a live leaderboard, and you tune between rounds to climb it. You walk away knowing when customization beats a strong prompt.

sessions.title: AWS Backup: Architecture deep dive
sessions.abstract: Dive into AWS Backup architecture with AWS experts, including how new capabilities fit into your design. We work through deployment strategies, backup storage options, restore scenarios, and security posture. Bring your questions, leave with a plan.

sessions.title: AWS Backup at scale: centralizing enterprise data protection
sessions.abstract: Protecting a single workload is straightforward. But when every team owns their own accounts, organizations need a centralized approach to enforce consistent data protection across all of them. We'll dig into how to build backup architectures that scale across your entire AWS estate, covering Organizations backup policies to enforce protection standards across accounts, cross-account and cross-region copy strategies, and Backup Audit Manager for compliance monitoring and audit evidence. Whether you're onboarding new accounts or tightening controls on existing ones, we'll walk through patterns for centralized data protection you can prove.

sessions.title: AWS Backup: Centralized data protection for your cloud environment
sessions.abstract: Managing data protection across a growing cloud environment requires a centralized strategy. AWS Backup was designed around this principle, giving more than 150,000 organizations a fully managed service to automate backup operations, enforce protection policies at scale, and safeguard 20+ AWS services from a single console. From human error to infrastructure failures to targeted attacks, AWS Backup helps ensure you can recover the right data, at the right time, with confidence. In this session, learn how AWS Backup works, how you can use it to protect mission-critical workloads, and hear directly from customers about their implementation strategies and operational outcomes.

times.room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

sessions.title: AWS Backup clean room recovery: Comprehensive resilience framework
sessions.abstract: Having an isolated vault is only half the battle. When a cyber event hits, you need confidence your backups are clean and recoverable. In this chalk talk, learn how to design an Isolated Recovery Environment using AWS Backup that validates and restores data in a secure space separate from production: reducing blast radius, breaking the kill chain, and proving recoverability on demand. We'll cover immutable air-gapped copies, automated restore testing with malware scanning, and Multi-party approval to control recovery access during account compromise. Leave with a framework for building recovery confidence into your backup strategy.

sessions.title: AWS CDK - Contributing AI safety tooling to the IaC ecosystem
sessions.abstract: AI agents generate infrastructure-as-code that looks correct but fails 38% of the time at deployment. The open source Agent Toolkit for AWS provides skills for validation, linting, and security checks that any MCP-compatible AI tool can consume before deploying. This chalk talk covers how we contributed these capabilities as open source tooling that works across cfn-lint, Checkov, and cdk-nag, improving first-deploy success from 62% to 82%. Attendees discuss how to build similar validation layers for their own IaC tools and the tradeoffs between blocking vs advisory checks in agent workflows.

Certifications still validate expertise, but practitioners now need to demonstrate they can design, build, and optimize AI-powered systems alongside traditional cloud architecture. This lightning talk explains how AWS Training and Certification developed exam content, hands-on labs, and simulation-based assessments for agentic AI domains. You will also see how our team validated new competency frameworks, mapped learning paths to job roles, and built assessment experiences that measure real-world readiness rather than knowledge recall alone.

sessions.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs: Strong isolation for agents & beyond
sessions.abstract: Agents running generated code, multi-tenant platforms, and untrusted workloads all need strong isolation, but each traditional compute option forces a tradeoff. VMs isolate well but start slowly. Containers are fast but share a kernel. Functions scale to zero but limit state. Teams close the gaps with isolation logic they build and maintain themselves. Lambda MicroVMs offer sandboxes with VM-level isolation for each agent, tenant, or task: state that persists across invocations, automatic suspend on idle, resume on demand. This session covers how MicroVMs work, the security and isolation model, lifecycle management, and patterns for agentic sandboxing and untrusted code execution.

In this hands-on session, we'll explore best practices for modernizing .NET Framework applications with AWS Transform. You'll learn how to work alongside the agent to reach a desired outcome. Together, we will apply plan customizations, steering documents, checkpoints, and iteration. Come ready to share your use cases and leave with practical steps to efficient, cost-effective modernization. Bring your laptop with Visual Studio and an AWS account onboarded to AWS Transform.

sessions.title: Best practices for operating an Apache Iceberg lakehouse at scale
sessions.abstract: Operating an Iceberg lakehouse at scale means taming the operational overhead that grows with your data. In this chalk talk, we dive into table maintenance strategies—compaction, snapshot expiration, and orphan file cleanup—and discuss how Amazon S3 Tables automates these tasks. We'll whiteboard patterns for metadata management with AWS Glue Data Catalog, storage cost optimization through lifecycle-aware file pruning, and partition evolution without rewriting data. You will leave with battle-tested operational patterns for production Iceberg workloads.

sessions.title: Best practices for scaling self-managed GPU workstations
sessions.abstract: Artists, engineers, and scientists need GPU-powered virtual workstations, but managing VDI at scale means navigating instance selection, capacity, and cost. In this chalk talk, learn how to match EC2 G instances to user personas, from fractional GPU for task workers to full GPU for power users running 3D modeling, compositing, or subsurface visualization. Explore the decision framework covering instance types, DCV streaming, storage, security, and fleet orchestration with Research and Engineering Studio (RES). Whether supporting a VFX render farm's artist desktops, an oil company's subsurface workstations, or an automotive design studio, leave with guidance balancing performance, cost, and simplicity.

sessions.abstract: The session covers best practices, architectural guidance and lessons learned for successful multiplayer game launches at scale. It's based on experience from helping hundreds of game customers from indie studios to AAA titles launch their games on AWS.

sessions.title: Best practices for working with shared coding agents on your team
sessions.abstract: Software development happens through teamwork, but agent work is often trapped in individual sessions. The developer who starts the work becomes the coordinator who needs to relay feedback, reconstruct decisions, or keep agents moving. Working with agents as a team has many paper cuts, but there are best practices you can implement. Follow an issue from investigation through implementation, testing, and review, with requests, decisions, and approvals attributed along the way as work progresses. Learn how team-scoped knowledge, reusable practices, and clear permission boundaries let agents take on ongoing responsibilities while people keep control of what ships.

sessions.title: Best practices to build, connect and optimize agents on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Ship agents fast. Connect to anything. Optimize continuously. In this session, learn best practices for the full agent lifecycle on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Build: go from local to production with microVM isolation, persistent memory, and any framework. Connect: access MCP servers, knowledge bases, and APIs through Gateway with automatic authentication. Optimize: trace every model call with OpenTelemetry-compatible observability and run continuous evaluations. Walk away with architectural patterns and implementation strategies to ship your first agent in minutes, not months.

sessions.title: Better, faster, cheaper: How Valkey is revolutionizing caching
sessions.abstract: Discover how the powerful combination of open source Valkey and Amazon ElastiCache is transforming the landscape of distributed caching. In this session, explore recent innovations including advanced search capabilities such as full-text search, a memory-efficient dictionary that reduces memory usage by up to 40%, and a multi-threaded architecture that enables instantaneous scaling by up to 230%. Learn about the infrastructure that enables ElastiCache to patch hundreds of thousands of customers while maintaining high availability, even for extreme workloads like Prime Day's trillion requests per minute.

sessions.title: Beyond AIOps: Operating safely in the age of agent sprawl
sessions.abstract: As organisations move from a small number of AI assistants to a distributed ecosystem of agents that can discover tools, make decisions, and act, operational excellence must evolve. Drawing on HMRC’s work to develop a governed platform model for agentic systems, this session explores a practical maturity model spanning inventory, ownership, identity, delegated authority, observability, blast-radius controls, evaluation, and human accountability. Learn how existing platform engineering, SRE, security and service-management practices can be extended across cloud and SaaS ecosystems without creating a separate governance regime for every agent or vendor. Designed for platform leaders, SREs and architects preparing to scale agents safely in complex, regulated environments.

sessions.title: Beyond Batch: Modernize with Event-Driven Architecture & Serverless
sessions.abstract: In this builders' session, transform a batch-oriented data processing pipeline into a real-time, event-driven architecture using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AWS Step Functions. Working hands-on in small groups, you'll decompose a monolithic batch process into discrete event-driven steps, implement file-processing triggers, and design fan-out patterns for parallel execution. Learn when to keep batch and when to go event-driven, and leave with a working modernization pattern. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
sessions.abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.

sessions.title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
sessions.abstract: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.

sessions.title: Beyond code generation: accelerating the entire SDLC on AWS
sessions.abstract: Teams pour AI into code generation and wonder why they're not shipping faster. In reality, accelerating one stage just moves the bottleneck downstream. This session follows a single task across its entire lifecycle and shows where AI compounds. We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent), ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. Come see our vision for an SDLC where every stage moves at the same speed.

sessions.title: Beyond English: Architecture Patterns for Multilingual AI Voice Agents
sessions.abstract: Deploying AI voice agents beyond English introduces unique challenges: accent handling, language detection, code-switching between languages mid-conversation, and cultural nuances in conversation flow. In this chalk talk, we share architecture patterns for building multilingual voice agents using Amazon Connect Agentic Voice. We cover real-world scenarios from deployments like Spanish and English coexistence, German with regional dialects, and Italian conversational AI. We discuss when speech-to-speech models work natively, when to fall back to TTS pipelines, how to handle polyglot but non-native accent scenarios, and practical approaches to knowledge base localization. Bring your language challenge and we'll design your multilingual architecture on the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Beyond fine-tuning: RL for reasoning agents with AWS Trainium
sessions.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning enables your model to follow instructions, but teaching it to reason requires reinforcement learning. RL workflows demand iterative loops that multiply compute costs — making AWS Trainium's purpose-built price performance critical. In this chalk talk, we explore what techniques like RLHF and GRPO bring to the table and how to run them on Trainium with the AWS Neuron software stack, Torchtitan, HuggingFace TRL, vLLM, and native PyTorch. We compare co-located vs. disaggregated RL architectures. You'll leave ready to implement cost-effective RL loops that train agents to reason.

See how a leading US mortgage lender is rebuilding origination and servicing with agentic AI on AWS, cutting cycle times while keeping controls and auditability intact. We will also show how the same agent patterns reach IT operations, resolving incidents before customers feel them. Tata Consultancy Services shares the reference architecture, guardrails, and adoption model behind both. Built for financial services business and operations leaders, CIOs and IT operations heads, and data and AI leaders, this session gives you a practical path from promising pilots to production at enterprise scale. sessions.title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Optimize the Agent Harness
sessions.abstract: An agent’s performance depends on far more than its model or system prompt. Tools, instructions, context management, memory, orchestration, and runtime policies form an agent harness that can determine whether the same model succeeds or fails. This session introduces harness optimization: a systematic, evaluation-driven approach to improving the complete agent system. Learn how to identify high-leverage changes, design controlled experiments, optimize for quality, latency, and cost, and avoid overfitting to benchmarks. Leave with a repeatable method for turning agent development into an engineering discipline.

sessions.title: Beyond Prompts: Crafting Production GenAI from Scratch
sessions.abstract:
Building reliable GenAI applications requires deliberate systems engineering, not just prompt engineering. 
After collaborating with AWS Professional Services on an enterprise client, I learned how to build production-grade web apps the official AWS way. 

Bypassing basic buzzwords, we map a compound serverless conversational assistant engineered from scratch using AWS CDK, CloudFront, Cognito, API Gateway, and ⁠Amazon Bedrock. 

Examine how to handle real-world token streaming failures, manage state in DynamoDB, and implement strict Infrastructure as Code. Leave with complete source code and a concrete approach to balancing model performance against infrastructure cost in highly concurrent production environments.

sessions.title: Beyond RSA: Post-quantum data encryption using ML-KEM in AWS KMS
sessions.abstract: RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography secure nearly every application today, and both are vulnerable to future cryptographically relevant quantum computers. Data captured now can be decrypted later, so applications needing long-term confidentiality should adopt post-quantum encryption well before those computers arrive. AWS KMS now offers ML-KEM, the NIST-standardized replacement for RSA and ECDH key establishment and ultimately encryption under asymmetric keys. It protects the private keys in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. In this session, learn about ML-KEM and how to use it as a building block for quantum-safe encryption using Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE).

sessions.abstract: As enterprises move from experimenting with AI agents to deploying them at scale, the challenge is no longer just how to build agents, it’s how to maintain visibility, performance, and control across the growing agent ecosystem. This session will explore how Amazon Bedrock and Dataiku Agent Management support the agent lifecycle from creation through enterprise-wide management. Attendees will see how organizations can build and deploy agents with AWS while using Dataiku to discover agents, monitor performance, and identify risk across environments, helping teams scale agentic AI with greater confidence and governance. sessions.title: Beyond the Docs: Operating Scoped VPC Endpoints in Real Environments
sessions.abstract: Scoped VPC endpoint policies look simple, until production traffic proves otherwise. In this interactive chalk talk, we'll walk through real-world failures we've encountered while deploying account- and org-scoped endpoint policies and trace the identity flows, auth chains, and hidden dependencies behind them. Together, we'll explore a key lesson: endpoint policies evaluate the request that's actually made, not the request you think you're making. Bring your questions and experiences as we whiteboard the assumptions that lead to outages and learn how to spot them before they impact production.

sessions.title: Beyond the GPU count: Engineering inference at scale
sessions.abstract: You have enough GPUs in your server to cover your software requirements. But is that all you need to consider? In a world where everyone is fighting for GPUs, picking the wrong server type is one of the most expensive mistakes an engineering team makes at scale. This session shares lessons running GPU inference across AWS and bare metal connected privately. You'll see how EKS Hybrid Nodes provides a single scheduling plane, failure modes, and how to use AI to accelerate decisions without replacing engineering judgement. Leave with a cloud and bare metal architectural pattern and a GPU selection framework covering workload fit and server tradeoffs.

sessions.title: Beyond the GPU: Optimizing AI performance with storage architecture
sessions.abstract: When AI workloads need scale or speed, the instinct is to add more compute, but GPU speed only pays off when the data keeps pace. From training to inference, storage architecture shapes performance at every stage: optimizing checkpoints for uninterrupted training, reducing model load times, extending context windows beyond GPU memory, and accelerating retrieval for RAG and inference workloads. Learn how Amazon FSx for Lustre, FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon S3 Express One Zone give you those levers.

In this session, hear how Booking.com dissolved organizational silos, broke through bottlenecks, and compressed timelines to fundamentally change how they build, operate, and innovate. You'll learn the architectural decisions, migration frameworks, and repeatable patterns that scaled cloud adoption across the enterprise, and how embedding AI from the ground up now powers next-generation customer experiences. sessions.abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore best practices for building high-performing, cost-efficient Spark applications using AWS analytics data processing services. We'll discuss the AWS performance-optimized runtime for Apache Spark—delivering up to 4.5x faster execution across Amazon EMR, Amazon Athena, and AWS Glue—meaning faster jobs and lower compute spend. Explore flexible deployment models—long-running clusters, on-demand elasticity with EMR Serverless, Kubernetes integration with EMR on EKS, and Graviton instances for up to 30% cost reduction. We'll also highlight how Glue's auto scaling, Flex execution class, and Iceberg integrations simplify pipelines while optimizing costs.

sessions.abstract: Disconnected systems slow teams down. See how Agentforce, Slack and AgentCore Bedrock enable your Headless agentic strategy to unlock seamless collaboration and boost productivity across teams in real time. This presentation is brought to you by Salesforce, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: Deploying an application to Kubernetes is straightforward. Provisioning its AWS resources, IAM roles, policies, and supporting infrastructure is more complex. Separate infrastructure and application toolchains create fragmented workflows and increase the risk of drift. In this session, we'll build a GitOps platform using EKS Capabilities, Argo CD, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes (ACK), and kro. See how kro packages Kubernetes workloads and their AWS dependencies behind a single, self-service custom resource. Learn how Argo CD continuously reconciles the entire application stack from one Git repository. Finally, watch several microservices deploy, with their cloud resources provisioned and continuously managed alongside their workloads.

sessions.abstract: Oracle modernization promises freedom from licensing, lock-in, and operational overhead, yet projects stall on PL/SQL packages, schema quirks, and application logic that resists automated translation. In this workshop, you'll migrate a live Oracle workload to open-source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL end-to-end and tackle the hardest schema conversion challenges that derail real-world projects. sessions.abstract: Batch inference is more than running a model over a large dataset. In this interactive chalk talk, we build an end-to-end batch inference architecture on Amazon EKS one component at a time. We examine when to use Spark with Ray Serve and when Ray Data can unify preprocessing and inference. Along the way, we address data sharding, storage and data movement, GPU scheduling, autoscaling, batch sizing, checkpointing, retries, observability, security, isolation, and cost. Attendees will leave with a practical decision framework and a production architecture for operating reliable, scalable batch inference with Ray Data and the KubeRay Operator.

sessions.title: Break it to prove It: Fault-isolated architecture built to recover
sessions.abstract:
Your recovery plan is only as good as the architecture backing it. This workshop presents single-Region and multi-Region resilience patterns built along fault isolation boundaries, where failure scope dictates which recovery mechanism to engage. Using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC), you architect for discrete blast radii, then validate each boundary through fault injection with AWS Fault Injection Service. Observability surfaces the failure, alarms classify scope, and automated recovery executes without intervention. The result: proof that your architecture recovers the way you designed it to.
Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Bring your S3 data to your compute with S3 Files
sessions.abstract: S3 Files makes the data in your S3 buckets available to your compute as a high-performance file system, so any POSIX-based tool or workload can work with S3 objects in place. We will work through the two ways customers use it: giving established file-based applications direct access to data already in S3, and giving agents and other short-lived compute a durable, isolated file workspace they can leave behind. We'll whiteboard the decisions that matter: connecting compute to S3 Files across VPCs, accounts, and on-prem; tuning for price and performance; and securing access with IAM, POSIX permissions, and encryption.

sessions.title: Bring your tech debt: build a custom transformation that fixes it
sessions.abstract: Every codebase has that annoying pattern: the deprecated internal library, the logging convention nobody follows, the framework migration that keeps getting deferred. In this small-group builder session, you'll tackle yours. Bring a real modernization problem from your own code and build a custom transformation in AWS Transform custom that solves it—defining the transformation in natural language, running it against a repository, and refining it until it holds up. No fixed curriculum and no slides: this is open-ended, hands-on time. Stuck for an idea? We'll have a few ready-made problems on hand. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.abstract: You have hundreds of services stuck on aging infrastructure, and your engineers are spending more time maintaining them than building new experiences. British Airways faced the same challenge with 590 Github repositories and 200 business services on EC2. Using AWS Transform custom, they built an agentic AI platform that autonomously migrates services to ECS Fargate on Graviton, cutting costs by 48% without compromising business logic. They also extended it to improve test coverage and patch security vulnerabilities continuously. In this session, you'll learn how to build a repeatable transformation engine and give your engineers time back.

sessions.title: Brownfield development across large codebases with AI agents
sessions.abstract: Most production code has no spec. It was written by teams that moved on, and its docs went stale long ago. When you inherit a service, prepare a migration, or chase an incident, you spend days reconstructing what the system does, and your AI agent rediscovers the same behavior in every new chat. We'll first sketch how to generate a structured model of an existing system from its code: its invariants, dependencies, and hidden assumptions. Then it's your turn. Bring your questions and your hardest brownfield problems, and we'll work through them together at the whiteboard.

sessions.title: Build a backend before your coffee gets cold with AWS Blocks
sessions.abstract: What if you could stand up a full application backend—database, auth, real-time messaging, file storage, even an AI agent—in TypeScript, running locally, with no AWS account required? AWS Blocks is an open-source framework where each "Block" bundles your app code, a local dev implementation, and production AWS infrastructure. Compose the Blocks you need, run one command to develop locally, then deploy the same code to AWS unchanged. Built for a world where AI agents write the code, Blocks ships steering files that guide agents to correct architecture from the start. In this lightning talk, see how fast full-stack can be.

sessions.title: Build a brand knowledge graph for retail and CPG AI
sessions.abstract: Retail and CPG brands invest years building product expertise, from visual styling rules to ingredient pairing and formulation knowledge, that generic AI simply cannot replicate. In this builder session, you'll construct a Graph RAG solution that encodes brand-specific curatorial knowledge into an Amazon Neptune Analytics knowledge graph with multimodal vector embeddings. Using a CPG product catalog, you'll build graph schemas capturing formulation relationships, brand hierarchies, and cross-category pairing rules. Then see how vector similarity search combined with graph traversal enriches retrieval context before grounding Amazon Bedrock LLM responses. Leave with a working deployed architecture adaptable across retail and CPG.

See how to build a voice agent that answers common citizen inquiries about permits, utilities, parks, and city services, routes callers to the right department, and seamlessly escalates to live agents with full conversation context when needed. Walk away with a production-ready reference architecture that operations team can configure, deploy, and manage independently.

sessions.title: Build a container pipeline that blocks tampered images at the gate
sessions.abstract: What if you want to prove cryptographically that every container in your environment is untampered and fully inventoried? In this builders' session, you build exactly that. Dive deep into the AWS Signer cryptographic model: KMS-backed keys, ECDSA P-256, COSE_Sign1 envelopes, and notation trust policies. Implement ECR managed signing, generate SBOMs with Amazon Inspector, slim images to reduce attack surface, and enforce admission on EKS with Kyverno. Then stress test it with attack simulations against the pipeline you just built.

sessions.title: Build a cost-optimized multi-agent system on Amazon EC2 CPUs and GPU
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, you build a production-ready multi-agent system that splits workloads between CPU and GPU EC2 instances — the best of both worlds. Starting with an autonomous customer-support pipeline, you deploy reasoning agents on GPU and orchestration, tool-calling, and retrieval agents on CPUs. You profile each stage, measure latency and cost per agent call, and implement routing policies that dynamically assign tasks to the optimal compute tier. By the end, you have a hybrid deployment with a live cost dashboard showing 30–45% savings vs. GPU-only baselines.

sessions.title: Build a digital asset tokenization issuance solution
sessions.abstract: The emergence of digital assets and stablecoins requires bridging traditional message-based finance protocols such as SWIFT and ISO 20022 to programmable settlement rails while preserving institutional security, auditability, and governance. In this session, learn how to build a production-ready end-to-end hybrid settlement architecture on AWS that ingests financial messages, normalizes them into canonical settlement instructions, and executes tokenized asset transfers on-chain. Explore hardware-backed signing with AWS KMS, on-chain signer governance, and three settlement patterns: issuance, redemption, and transfer, with full audit trails, idempotent transaction handling, and EIP-712 typed signing. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build a fully managed data lake with Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Data lakes have evolved from raw Parquet files with Hive-style partitioning to fully managed Apache Iceberg tables. In this hands-on workshop, you'll understand that evolution, then build a working analytics data lake with Amazon S3 Tables in under two hours. You'll create an S3 table bucket, ingest real-world data, migrate data into the bucket, and query it with Amazon Athena. You'll also learn how to connect third-party tools like DuckDB for interactive exploration. Along the way we’ll cover the benefits of fully managed Iceberg tables and when to use Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation for open data architectures.

sessions.title: Build agentic fraud detection with a transaction foundation model
sessions.abstract: Organized fraud rings exploit the gaps between siloed detection systems, making them invisible to traditional rules-based approaches. In this workshop, you’ll construct a fraud detection optimization system that tackles them at scale. Load 24M transactions into Apache Iceberg, build a knowledge graph with Amazon Neptune to reveal hidden fraud networks, and train an ensemble combining transaction foundation model embeddings with graph embeddings for measurable score improvement. Then deploy a multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that autonomously investigates patterns, expands fraud rings, and creates validated detection rules. Leave with an end-to-end working system you can replicate in your own environment.

You will transform unstructured and semi-structured data into a catalog of domain-specific GraphRAG tools to enable agents to answer multi-faceted questions that require context from multiple distinct knowledge sources to provide a contextually complete answer. sessions.title: Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.abstract: What if your agent's most convincing answer rests on the wrong evidence? Build agentic hybrid retrieval with Aurora PostgreSQL across more than 500,000 product listings in three connected hands-on labs. Debug SQL combining full-text search, pg_trgm fuzzy matching, and pgvector semantic search under shared filters. Repair reciprocal rank fusion, inspect Amazon Bedrock reranking, and compare retrieval settings against judged queries. Then build a Strands agent, connect its retrieval tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway, and deploy it to AgentCore Runtime. Trace its searches to cited specifications and reviews, and test what happens when requirements change. Leave with reusable retrieval SQL and working agent code.

sessions.title: Build agentic payment investigators on Aurora PostgreSQL & AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Payment dispute resolution and ledger reconciliation require agents that reason over transactional history, retrieve precedent with precision, and write through idempotent workflows. In this session, learn how to build two production-grade payment agents on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: a dispute investigator that classifies cardholder disputes and drafts representment narratives, and a reconciliation agent that resolves breaks between internal ledgers and bank statements. Both share one investigator pattern: an agent reasoning over structured records, retrieving precedent with pgvector, and writing through an idempotent ledger. Go deep on SERIALIZABLE state machines, hybrid retrieval that knows when a trigram index beats an embedding, confidence-scored human-in-the-loop routing, and trace-to-row observability with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

sessions.title: Build a grounded AI support assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: You want to build an AI assistant: where do you even start? A model alone is not the answer. The hard part is grounding it in your own data so it gives real answers, remembers the conversation, and holds up as that data grows, and grounding is a search problem. In this hands-on workshop, you build a customer support assistant grounded in Amazon OpenSearch Service. Starting from a pre-deployed base, you create an OpenSearch Serverless collection, add hybrid search for relevance, and add agentic memory so your assistant retains context across the conversation. You connect your tools and data with the OpenSearch MCP server, the AWS Knowledge MCP, and the AWS MCP. You leave with working code, an architecture that scales itself, and a clear path from a blank page to an assistant that answers from real data.

sessions.title: Build AI agents on Amazon S3 Files
sessions.abstract: S3 Files is the first cloud object store with fully-featured, high-performance file system access to your data. In this hands-on session, you'll create an S3 file system, attach it to an Amazon EKS cluster, and build an AI agent that loads model weights and processes data directly from S3 via standard file I/O. No SDK rewrites, no data duplication, just native POSIX access. You'll fine-tune synchronization behavior between S3 and the file system, controlling how data flows between object and file interfaces. Finally, you'll configure cross-Region replication to establish a disaster recovery strategy for your production workloads.

sessions.abstract: Chatbots answer questions. Your best reps remember context, pull up the right data, take action, and resolve the issue in one conversation. This session shows how to build conversational agents on AgentCore that work the same way: low-latency streaming on Runtime, multi-turn and cross-session context with Memory, Gateway-connected tools so the agent checks orders, modifies accounts, and triggers workflows mid-conversation, guardrails that keep every interaction on-policy, and human handoff when needed.

sessions.title: Build AI agents to operate desktop and mainframe apps on WorkSpaces
sessions.abstract: You rely on desktop and mainframe applications for critical workflows, but these interfaces remain inaccessible to AI agents. Your Robotic Process Automation efforts have struggled to keep pace as applications and configurations constantly change. Amazon WorkSpaces lets AI agents securely operate the same desktop and mainframe applications your employees use, without any application modernization. WorkSpaces supports Model Context Protocol (MCP), so it works with any agent framework. In this workshop, connect to a pre-provisioned WorkSpace, build a custom agent, run agents that complete desktop workflows, and monitor agent sessions with CloudWatch and CloudTrail. Bring laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build AI photo discovery with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Learn how S3 Vectors turns millions of untagged images into a semantically searchable collection without standing up a separate vector database. In this builders' session, you will generate multi-modal embeddings from photo assets, store and index them in S3 Vectors with metadata predicates for filtered search, and wire an AI agent that discovers images using natural language queries. You will explore index configuration, batch ingestion throughput, and cost patterns at scale. You will leave with a working prototype and production patterns for building vector-native search directly on S3.

sessions.title: Build AI-Powered Analytics with Conversational BI on Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Construct a complete AI-powered analytics pipeline, from data ingestion to conversational consumption. Use Amazon Quick's Data Catalog to discover data, query it live without moving it into SPICE, then enrich and import metadata with semantics inherited to build natural-language Q&A. In this hands-on workshop, you start with seven raw banking tables: no catalog, no definitions. An agent inspects the data and builds the catalog for you. You ask questions in plain English and get answers. An agent generates a dashboard showing which top customers are slipping. Another agent, aware of the bank's compliance rules, checks every offer before it ships. Then you automate the full response as a Quick Flow and wrap it in a custom app your team can use. You leave with a working banking command center that agents built, and that you can rebuild in your own account using conversational analytics.

sessions.title: Build a knowledge graph-based agent guardrail with Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: AI agents assert relationships such as compatible products, cleared counterparties, or approved suppliers, derived from LLM reasoning rather than verified data. When these assertions are wrong, downstream business decisions fail. In this session, explore how to implement Amazon Neptune as a post-generation verification layer. Before the agent responds, a graph traversal confirms or contradicts the assertion against a live knowledge graph. Learn how to build the verification tool, the override pattern when Neptune contradicts the model, and the graph data model for storing authoritative relationship data that constrains agent behavior. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.abstract: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. No repo setup, no infrastructure work. You'll touch the full stack, generation, database, and deployment, and walk away with a functional prototype. Then we open up the system behind it: planning, safety checks, a durable job queue, containerized workers on Amazon EC2, automated testing, targeted repairs, and deployment. We'll unpack what makes it repeatable, like isolating generated code, keeping credentials at trusted boundaries, and preserving state across restarts with Atlas. A MongoDB Build Lab workshop, with AWS. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build a multi-agent system for hyper-personalized customer journeys
sessions.abstract: Delivering personalized experiences across complex customer journeys requires agents that understand intent, maintain context, and coordinate across systems. In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI personal banker using a home buying scenario as the example. Your agents extract intent from natural conversation, build dynamic customer profiles, and orchestrate workflows across internal banking systems and external ecosystem APIs. Implement multi-agent patterns for shared memory, readiness signals, and coordinated decisioning using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents Framework, and MCP. Walk away with reusable orchestration patterns you can apply to any personalized customer experience.

sessions.abstract: In this session, get hands-on experience with Amazon Aurora DSQL, a serverless distributed SQL database that delivers active-active high availability. Learn how to build a retail rewards points application with active-active resiliency across multiple Availability Zones and two Regions. Explore how ACID transactions and active-active replication work in Aurora DSQL. Discover best practices for data model and application design and more. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build an Agentic AI Marketing Engine Powered by Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on builder session, construct a multi-agent AI system that automates campaign planning, activation, and optimization. Build four specialized agents on Amazon Bedrock including a planner, media buyer, analyst, and creative generator that turns campaign parameters into audience targeting, budget allocation, performance forecasts, and localized creative grounded in your brand guidelines and historical data. Activate campaigns through Amazon Ads DSP, then add an optimizer agent with human-in-the-loop approvals that reallocates budget across channels as performance shifts. You'll build a running multi-agent workflow and take away the Bedrock agent definitions to adapt for your own campaigns.

sessions.title: Build an agentic AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that serves every model on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: a fine-tuned intent router and a fine-tuned embedding model for vector search (both ONNX, trained on CPU), a cross-encoder re-ranker for retrieval quality, and a quantized generative analyst served with llama.cpp and grounded by RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock generates the synthetic training data, judges every answer through a faithfulness gate, and answers the edge cases the small models cannot. You'll finish by running the control test that puts a frontier LLM in the same seat, so you know whether the small model is good enough on your workload. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

sessions.title: Build an agentic context layer with ontologies on Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: Most knowledge graphs answer questions but never close the loop with operational systems. In this session, explore how to build an ontology-driven context layer that transforms a knowledge graph into an active control plane for AI agents. The session covers RDF ontology design, SHACL constraint validation, synchronization patterns, agent integration, and write-back mechanisms that propagate decisions to systems of record. Hear how Lockheed Martin applied these patterns in production, enabling agents to reason across supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering domains. Leave with a concrete architectural blueprint and lessons learned from building context layers that act while increasing your trust.

sessions.title: Build an AI agent that understands customer intent
sessions.abstract: Today's AI agents start every session cold. They don't know what the customer was just browsing, whether they're frustrated or exploring, or whether this is a service moment or a buying moment. So they waste the first few turns asking what your data already knows. In this hands-on builders' session, you close that gap. You unify customer data into Profiles, then turn it into real-time signals about what each customer needs. You wire those signals into an AI agent with calculated attributes and event triggers, so when the customer makes contact the agent already understands why they're there and responds with the right answer and the right offer. You leave with a working prototype ready for your own environment.

sessions.title: Build an AI navigator that makes every frontline worker an expert
sessions.abstract: A member is on the line, a regulation changed last week, and the answer isn't in any manual yet. Frontline staff don't need a search box — they need a guide that surfaces the next right action in the moment. In this builder session, build a self-improving frontline navigator on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Harness: ground it in your policies with a Managed Knowledge Base, keep it current with live rule changes via AgentCore Web Search, and close the loop with AgentCore Optimization so it measurably improves from every real interaction. Unlike a static knowledge base, this agent recommends actions, adapts as policies shift, and learns on the job. Whether you serve members, patients, or beneficiaries, leave with a deployed self-improving navigator and the architecture behind it.

In this builders' session, you'll construct a multi-agent system that analyzes your AWS Backup environment across four dimensions: coverage gaps, ransomware resilience scoring, vault security, and cost optimization. You'll build an MCP server exposing backup APIs as agent tools, wire specialist subagents into an orchestration graph, and deploy a remediation agent with human-in-the-loop approval to AgentCore Gateway. sessions.title: Build an AI-powered student services with Connect Customer
sessions.abstract: Education institutions field thousands of student inquiries each semester across enrollment, financial aid, and academic support. In this chalk talk, we architect agentic AI-powered student services using Amazon Connect Customer. You’ll configure a knowledge base with university content and connect it to Connect Customer for real-time AI-generated recommendations during live calls, then deploy a self-service experience that resolves common inquiries over voice and chat. We'll cover when to use deterministic intent handling vs. agentic reasoning, MCP tool integration with student systems, and guardrails for FERPA compliance. By the end, you'll have a working prototype that boosts advisor productivity and reduces student wait times.

sessions.title: Build an AI Student Advisor: Agents for Education
sessions.abstract: Universities lose students to inadequate academic advising often because a single advisor carries unsustainable caseloads and response times stretch to days. In this chalk talk, we explore the architecture of an AI student advising agent built with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands, connected to student record systems via MCP, with guardrails for sensitive student welfare queries, and embedded in an existing LMS through Amazon Quick. We'll whiteboard real-world advising scenarios (Course selection and degree planning) and discuss when the agent should hand off to a human advisor and how to design that escalation path.

sessions.title: Build an AI testing safety net before you modernize
sessions.abstract: Modernizing applications is risky without comprehensive test coverage, and most apps that need modernization don't have it. In this workshop, you'll build an AI-powered testing safety net before touching a line of production code. Starting with a deployed insurance application, you'll use Kiro to generate spec-driven tests from source code and Nova Act to discover UI tests through autonomous exploration. Then you'll apply AWS Transform to modernize the codebase and re-run your AI-generated test suite to prove functional equivalence. You'll leave knowing how to de-risk modernization by letting GenAI build your safety net first. Laptop required.

sessions.abstract: Multi-tenant ISVs need per-tenant observability that traditional dashboards can't deliver — aggregated metrics hide the tenant causing the problem, and shared traces don't tell you whose agent misbehaved. sessions.title: Build a Physical AI Model Factory on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Physical AI teams in robotics and autonomous vehicles can't collect enough real data for the rare edge cases that dominate risk. The answer is a continuous data flywheel: generate synthetic scenarios, post-train policies, evaluate, repeat. Running that at scale is GPU-hungry and orchestration-heavy. This chalk talk shows how to run the full Physical AI model factory on SageMaker HyperPod with EKS: provision heterogeneous GPU pools, schedule multi-stage jobs, and leverage auto-healing infrastructure.

You will create an agentic system that is capable of decomposing complex tasks and delegating sub-tasks to specialized worker agents. These agents will manage shared state and memory across boundaries, gracefully handle failures, and enforce quality guardrails. Subsequently, these agents will be deployed to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for production scaling and observability, featuring harness capabilities for checkpointing and long-running multi-agent workflow capabilities. Upon completion, you will be equipped with reusable design patterns and industry best practices to construct production-grade multi-agent systems utilizing the Strands Agent SDK.

Configure service-to-service networking with Service Connect, implement per-tier autoscaling policies, deploy updates with automated rollback, and observe your application using CloudWatch Container Insights. Walk away with a working architecture you can use as a reference for your own workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build a real-time data lakehouse with CDC streams on S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Learn how to build a real-time transactional data lakehouse using Amazon S3 Tables with Apache Iceberg. In this hands-on session, you will ingest CDC streams from Amazon MSK into a medallion architecture, transform batch and streaming data into business-ready gold layer tables with Amazon SageMaker, and query the results through Amazon Quick. You'll configure S3 Tables maintenance policies per layer and compare binpack, sort, and z-order compaction strategies to optimize query performance. You will leave with production patterns for continuous ingestion, incremental processing, and low-latency analytics at scale.

sessions.abstract: Learn how to build your own co-scientist with Amazon Quick. In this builder session, you'll gain hands-on experience with loading life sciences domain skills directly into Amazon Quick, and work through your own scientific questions with guidance from AWS's life sciences experts. sessions.abstract: A SaaS control plane - tenant onboarding, billing, configuration management, agent provisioning  is the most repeatable software every software vendor builds from scratch. In this builder's session, use Kiro specs to define the control plane requirements and let Kiro implement the scaffolding, then wire multi-tenant agent capabilities using Strands' open-source constructs. You'll build a working onboarding flow, a tenant configuration store, and a simple agent provisioning endpoint -  all from a spec, not from scratch. Leave with a reusable starting point for your own control plane and a pattern for using Kiro and Strands together to accelerate platform development.

sessions.title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
sessions.abstract: Teams deploying AI agents inherit two exposures. Any client reaching the endpoint can invoke the agent, and it can reach any destination its tools name. In this builders' session, learn to close both gaps with AWS managed controls. Put AWS WAF Bot Control in front of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to classify callers and admit only the classes you choose, then route the agent through AWS Network Firewall and use domain category filtering to decide which destination categories it may reach. Run each control in count or alert mode, then enforce it and verify the allowed and the refused path. Leave with a two-boundary pattern you can apply to your own agent deployments.

sessions.title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
sessions.abstract: AI agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore accept untrusted input and make outbound API calls, creating both ingress and egress attack surfaces. In this session, learn how to defend both paths using AWS WAF and AWS Network Firewall. See how WAF authenticates callers, enforces rate limits, and blocks prompt-injection payloads before they reach your agent, while Network Firewall applies managed threat-intelligence categories to drop egress traffic to malicious destinations without maintaining custom deny lists. Walk away with a deployable defense-in-depth boundary pattern for your agentic AI workloads.

sessions.title: Build a team shared agent workflow from issue to tested PR
sessions.abstract: How do you let agents carry development work across teammates without handing over control? In this code talk, build an issue-to-review workflow that you can share with your team. Follow the code and configuration for setting up guardrails, permissions, shared workflows, logging, and best practices, so teammates can steer the implementation or review who requested or approved each action alongside the evidence the agent produced. Bring questions and follow along as we explain why each boundary exists and how to adapt the pattern to your toolchain and approval process.

sessions.title: Build at scale real-time ingestion pipelines for Apache Iceberg tables
sessions.abstract: Landing streaming data into Apache  Iceberg at scale is a complex undertaking. In this chalk talk, we dissect practical reference architectures for real-time ingestion into Iceberg tables, covering  Kafka to Flink, Kinesis to Firehose, and managed pipelines through Amazon S3  Tables. Learn which architecture fits your latency and cost requirements, how  to keep Iceberg tables query-ready under continuous writes, and how these  pipelines feed downstream analytics and AI workloads.

sessions.title: Build a unified student insight platform on Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: From advisors triaging at-risk students to deans auditing course difficulty to executives tracking retention trends, every role in a university needs student-success insights, but today they use disconnected tools. In this session, learn how Amazon Quick connects to your institutional data and delivers explainable, persona-aware insights through one unified architecture. Chat Agents explain early-warning signals with cited data, automated Flows trigger interventions, and Stories generate executive-ready narratives. Explore the architecture and take away patterns for explainable, natural-language analytics on AWS.

sessions.title: Build Autonomous Agents and Run AI-Powered AppSec on Bedrock (sponsored by OpenAI)
sessions.abstract: Go hands-on with OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock across two builder tracks. First, stand up a fully managed autonomous agent with Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents: define instructions and tools, wire action groups for API access, and ground responses in your own data through knowledge bases. Then shift to code security, using OpenAI's Codex Security to review a real vulnerable app by running scans, threat modeling, triaging findings, and fixing one with verified remediation. Throughout, inference runs securely on Bedrock under your account's controls. You'll leave with repeatable blueprints for building agentic OpenAI applications and for AI-assisted application security on AWS. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed. Labs are 30-60 min. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build a Video Semantic Layer for Media Agent and Agent Harness on AWS
sessions.abstract: This workshop tackles a question most media organizations have yet to ask: your video pipeline extracts rich metadata for human search and discovery, but is it actually optimized for agents? In this hands-on session, you will build the semantic infrastructure that bridges that gap: multimodal embeddings tuned for machine recall, hybrid search that combines vector similarity with keyword precision, and an entity graph that maps content relationships into structures agents can reason over. By the end of this workshop, you will have a media agent harness that queries, enriches, and continuously improves their video understanding, making video content not just searchable by people but optimized at scale for agents.

sessions.title: Build a well-governed natural language-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift
sessions.abstract: The Amazon Redshift MCP Server enables AI agents to generate and execute SQL using natural language, but going from demo to production means answering critical security questions on preventing query hallucination, prompt injection, unbounded scans, and inadvertent PII exposure by the LLM. In this session, you will build a well-governed text-to-SQL agentic solution for Amazon Redshift with security gates that validate every AI-generated query before execution including schema allow-listing to constraining LLM context, authorized tables, columns and rows, SQL AST validation and enforced read-only access.

sessions.title: Build better agent retrieval with OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents and assistants are only as good as the answers they retrieve. Out-of-the-box frameworks get you started, but production-ready AI applications demand more from their search layer including higher relevance on complex queries, persistent memory across sessions, and tools the model can invoke reliably. Amazon OpenSearch Service delivers these capabilities natively. In this chalk talk, we dig into how to make OpenSearch Service the backbone of your AI agents and assistants, covering hybrid retrieval for better accuracy, MCP-based access to your data, and built-in conversation and long-term memory so your applications maintain context across interactions. Bring your architecture questions. Whether you're optimizing retrieval accuracy, adding persistent context, or connecting your agent to search via MCP, we work through it together and leave you with patterns you can apply.

sessions.abstract: Periodic reviews can't keep pace with infrastructure that changes daily. In this hands-on workshop, deploy an AI-powered agent for continuous, goal-driven architecture reviews across a multi-account environment. Configure agent profiles, cross-account role chaining, and business goals that prioritize across Cost Optimization, Security, Resilience, and Performance pillars. See how the agent enriches Trusted Advisor, Compute Optimizer, and Resilience Hub signals with cross-pillar trade-off analysis. Run pre-deployment reviews against CloudFormation, CDK, and Terraform, then remediate through AI-generated SOPs. Wire recommendations into CI/CD via API. For architects, platform engineers, and operations leads who want always-on architectural governance in their delivery lifecycle.

sessions.title: Build Bidstream Agents and Simulate Auction with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, build Agentic Real-Time Framework (ARTF)-compliant agents that operate inside the bidstream, using the Agents for Advertising framework on Amazon Bedrock. You'll construct an agent container that accepts bid requests and returns pricing decisions to the ARTF specification, then orchestrate a multi-agent pipeline that simulates adversarial auction scenarios and scores your bidding strategy against the outcomes. Run interactive simulations that generate learning signals, and plug in your own bidding model to see how it performs. You'll leave with a working ARTF container and auction-simulation harness you can point at your own models.

sessions.title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
sessions.abstract: Every organisation's modernization journey is unique — we whiteboard how to build, deploy, and share custom transformation agents using the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit — from orchestrator architectures and MCP patterns to one-command Bedrock AgentCore deployment. Bring your challenges.

sessions.title: Build Composable Agents with the AWS Transform Agent Builder Toolkit
sessions.abstract: Partners spent years building their modernization tooling. AWS Transform now meets them where they are, ATX agents exposed via MCP, callable from any partner-native orchestrator. We'll cover the integration pattern, agent-card model, and field-tested wins from GSI and ISV partners already in production.

sessions.title: Build conversational AI agents for query federation with Amazon Athena
sessions.abstract: Stop copying data just to query it. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll use MCP server integration with Amazon Athena for faster conversational analytics where agents translate natural language to federated SQL queries across custom databases and multi-cloud data stores – without moving or copying data. You’ll learn how federated queries eliminate complex ETL pipelines, enable cross-source joins in a single SQL statement, and integrate with your lakehouse on AWS for unified governance.

sessions.title: Build deeper into AWS with a traffic layer you own (sponsored by HAProxy Technologies)
sessions.abstract: Most teams on AWS accumulate separate systems for load balancing, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and Kubernetes routing. Each brings its own config model and failure domain, another hop in the request path, and a configuration that does not travel. This session makes the case for one layer, on Graviton, benchmarked at over 2 million HTTPS requests per second, with no traffic leaving your VPC for inspection, managed and observed from one control plane. Because that layer runs unchanged in every environment you add, it becomes the one part of your architecture that never has to move. This presentation is brought to you by HAProxy Technologies, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build durable AI agents with AgentCore and Temporal (sponsored by Temporal)
sessions.abstract: An AI agent completes five steps, waits for approval, and then its runtime is replaced. How does it recover without repeating costly tool calls or losing the business process? In this session, learn how Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and Temporal combine AWS-native agent infrastructure with durable execution. We’ll build a production agent that preserves progress across failures, coordinates tools, agents, and people, and safely evolves while work is still running. You'll see how Temporal natively supports serverless compute infrastructure, complementing AgentCore Runtime with durable execution, preserving workflow progress across failures, approvals, runtime changes, and scale to zero, without pushing recovery and coordination logic into application code. This presentation is brought to you by Temporal, an AWS Partner.
