sessions.title: Build End-to-End AI Pipelines on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Modern AI pipelines demand unified frameworks for petabyte-scale data prep, large-model training, and low-latency serving. In this hands-on workshop, build a complete data processing → distributed training → model serving pipeline on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, fine-tuning and serving an LLM end-to-end. Experience HyperPod's native distributed computing integration with managed orchestration, embedded observability, tiered checkpointing, hung-job detection, and managed KV cache for inference. Simulate a node failure and watch training auto-resume in seconds. Leave with a working serving endpoint, production patterns, and a resilient platform that eliminates the infrastructure toil of running distributed AI workloads at scale.

sessions.title: Build End-to-End Testing & Self-Healing Framework for Agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Organizations are accelerating their deployment of AI agents, yet the critical gap remains: proving they work reliably and responding when they don't. This workshop delivers a hands-on framework for the complete testing and operational lifecycle of agentic AI on Amazon Connect Customer. First, build a layered testing strategy using native Testing & Simulation — functional, integration, and regression tests for flows and bots, wired to dashboard-driven observability. Then, implement automated operational responses such as threshold-based alerting triggers pre-approved remediations. You will leave with a reusable testing playbook and an implementable pattern for closed-loop operational automation — reducing manual validation effort and moving toward self-managing AI agents at scale.

sessions.title: Build eval-driven skills for Aurora PostgreSQL operations

Complete and refine skills that cover pre-flight checks, execution, validation and rollback. Freeze a grading rubric, then compare the same agent, hosted on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, without and with your skill. Write Python recovery checks that reject incomplete fixes, perform the repairs yourself, and verify customer recovery using independent database and business records.

sessions.title: Build event-driven applications with AWS Streaming and Messaging

Learn to architect sophisticated event-driven systems using Amazon SQS, SNS, MSK, and Amazon MQ. Through guided exercises, implement critical features including fan-out architectures, FIFO queues, and hybrid patterns while optimizing for security, cost, and performance. Gain practical insights into how architectural decisions impact scalability, latency, and operational complexity in production systems.

sessions.title: Build explainable AI agent observability with DynamoDB and Neptune
sessions.abstract: Unintended agent actions and incorrect outputs are difficult to investigate without a structured provenance layer. In this session, learn how to design an agent observability system using Amazon DynamoDB to capture the operational audit log and Amazon Neptune to model causal dependencies between retrieved facts and agent decisions. Explore the data model, instrumentation patterns, and graph query techniques that answer what data an agent retrieved, what it concluded, and how those conclusions shaped the final output, making every agent decision traceable and explainable. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Build full-stack observability for agents and apps
sessions.abstract: When your applications include AI agents that reason, plan, and act autonomously, observability has to evolve too. Disconnected tools and siloed signals slow teams down right when speed matters most. In this chalk talk, we walk through real scenarios and trace an agent's chain of thought across services, correlating agent failures with infrastructure, and using natural-language investigation to cut resolution time. We diagram how service discovery, dependency mapping, evaluations, and IDE-native telemetry come together so you can ship agents with confidence.

sessions.title: Build GenAI-Powered Workflows with AWS Serverless and AWS AI Services
sessions.abstract: In this builders' session, design and deploy a workflow that chains AI service calls—document analysis, content generation, and decision routing—using AWS Step Functions and Lambda durable functions for checkpoint and recovery. sessions.title: Build governed agentic AI search with Aurora, RDS, & Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Build an agentic retail assistant that answers from business facts under explicit controls. Across four connected labs, combine Aurora PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector with reciprocal rank fusion and Cohere Rerank on Amazon Bedrock. Connect search and inventory tools to specialists built with the Strands Agents SDK, then deploy them to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with Runtime, Memory, Gateway, and Policy. Approve a store credit, query the audit records, and verify denied calls don't execute and retries don't duplicate credits. Patterns are reusable across Aurora and RDS for PostgreSQL.

sessions.abstract: AI-powered database intelligence can surface recommendations for slow queries, vacuum issues, index changes, and parameter tuning, but acting on those recommendations safely in production requires governance. In this session, build a governed recommendation-to-remediation workflow for Aurora PostgreSQL. Starting with a performance troubleshooting recommendation, learn to classify operational risk, validate the proposed change, apply policy-based approval gates, execute with scoped permissions, and capture an auditable trail from insight to action. Explore custom security controls, blast-radius reduction, human-in-the-loop governance, rollback planning, post-change verification across development, staging, and production environments, and integration with signals from your own agents. In this hands-on workshop you'll wire Strands SDK agents to inference on Amazon Bedrock and NVIDIA NIM-on-AWS, sandbox tool execution with OpenShell (Landlock, seccomp, eBPF, cgroups), and install signed skills, connectors, and runbooks from an open, versioned registry that federates with AWS AgentCore. You'll watch a five-layer enforcement spine crystallize in a run-DAG where every prompt, model call, tool call, and delegation becomes a visible, proven step. Then you'll graduate the same governance from laptop to AWS unchanged, with SPIFFE/SPIRE attesting which instance ran each step. You'll leave with a working reference deployment in your own AWS account and reusable patterns you can adapt to real agents. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build hybrid data planes for government GenAI pipelines
sessions.abstract: Strict national security mandates block government agencies from adopting cloud GenAI. To resolve this, architects deploy a decoupled edge-to-cloud tokenization pattern. In this workshop, use AWS CDK to build a three-phase data plane that isolates sensitive citizen data in a simulated edge environment. You will deploy local data tokenization, route masked payloads to Amazon Bedrock for stateless inference, and reconcile state on-premises. Leave with an infrastructure-as-code blueprint to unlock frontier AI and satisfy federal localization mandates.

sessions.title: Build hybrid quantum-classical solutions for science and engineering on Amazon Braket
sessions.abstract: Take the next step into hybrid quantum computing. This expert-level workshop combines Amazon Braket and AWS Parallel Computing Service to build hybrid quantum-classical resources that enable scientific and engineering research in fields like  physics. You learn how to structure hybrid programs, manage classical resources, and interpret results from real quantum devices. Expect hands-on exercises, detailed guidance, and examples you can use as a foundation for you own projects

sessions.title: Building 10x Organizations - Using Modern Productivity Metrics (sponsored by Atlassian)
sessions.abstract: 10x developers may be a myth, but 10x organizations are very real, as proven by the influential study performed in the 1980s, ‘The Coding War Games.’ In this keynote-style session, teams will take a detailed, granular look at the barriers to productivity developers face today and modern approaches for removing them. You’ll learn about the history of productivity theory, and how previous practices have influenced our current understanding. DevOps and Platform Engineering philosophy is clearly converging on developer experience. But which of these approaches works? DORA? SPACE? DevEx? What should we invest in and create urgency behind today so we don’t have the same discussion again in a decade? This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building a Cost Governance framework for AI that scales
sessions.abstract: AI spend starts with model tokens but often misses costs from agent runtimes, memory, data, and supporting services. Using AWS FinOps Agent as an example, we'll examine how its architecture creates costs across Amazon Bedrock and supporting services, and how to govern those costs. Bring your AI cost challenge and leave with a model that helps FinOps and engineering teams assign ownership, find waste, and set effective controls.

sessions.title: Building agentic apps with serverless: Lambda as your agent's toolbox
sessions.abstract: Agents need tools—functions they can call to retrieve data, take actions, and interact with external systems. Lambda is well-suited for this, but designing functions as agent tools requires different thinking than traditional API backends. In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

sessions.title: Building a governed AI ready data foundation on AWS (sponsored by Fivetran)
sessions.abstract: Most data stacks were built for dashboards, not AI. Duplicated pipelines, competing definitions, and slow reporting make it difficult to deliver the fresh, trusted, governed data AI demands. Learn how a fast growing organization replaced engineering heavy operations with a self serve model built on AWS, Fivetran, and dbt. Understand how to standardize ingestion, apply governed transformations and semantic definitions, and cut pipeline development from months to days. You'll walk away with a practical approach to freeing engineering time, providing business teams with trusted access to data, and building a governed foundation that scales AI from experiments to production. This presentation is brought to you by Fivetran, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building AI Agents with Vercel and AWS (sponsored by Vercel)
sessions.abstract: This session explores how Vercel and AWS work together to support the development and deployment of AI agents. You’ll learn about first party connectivity to AWS databases and services through the Vercel Marketplace, along with the backend capabilities agents need, including APIs, durable workflows, queues, cron jobs, and MCP servers. You’ll see how these building blocks, together with the EVE framework, can simplify agent development, followed by a live demo showing how to build an agent using Vercel and AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building a Knowledge & Context Engineering Foundation for AI Agents
sessions.abstract: Every enterprise building agentic AI hits the same wall: AI agents can't deliver trusted guidance without governed knowledge behind them. In this session, learn how AWS solved this internally with an agentic specialist teammate for Amazon Connect powered by a structured knowledge governance framework. We'll show how specialist reasoning is captured, validated, and scaled across 92 domains to 30K+ field members, and demonstrate the live workflow from governed knowledge delivery to human escalation. Walk away with a repeatable reference architecture for making your own AI agents production-ready and trustworthy.

sessions.title: Building an AI Travel Assistant with AgentCore Gateway
sessions.abstract: Your agent handles conversations well, but to search for flights or check weather it needs access to external tools and APIs. In this SimuLearn session, you create an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway and register Lambda functions as MCP-compatible tool targets. You then deploy a travel planning agent using the Strands Agents SDK that connects to the Gateway, sequentially invokes flight search and weather tools, and synthesizes results into a trip recommendation through one secure MCP endpoint.

sessions.abstract: Kubernetes has become the platform of choice for production gen AI inference at scale. This builders' session covers deploying and scaling large language models on Amazon EKS with NVIDIA GPUs - from cluster setup optimized for GPU workloads to efficient model serving with vLLM, distributed inference with Ray, and observability using Prometheus and Grafana. Real-world patterns address cost optimization and enterprise-grade reliability for teams moving beyond experimentation. Attendees leave with hands-on experience and best practices for running production-grade gen AI infrastructure on Kubernetes. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building and scaling low latency web apps with AWS Serverless
sessions.abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this code talk, build a full-stack web application entirely on AWS serverless services, live in code: API endpoints, business logic, data persistence, and authentication. We walk through architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and show how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with patterns you can apply to your own projects.

sessions.title: Building and securing AI agents on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: AI agents now generate and run their own code at runtime, turning secure agent execution into a platform engineering problem. Containers alone were not built to run untrusted, autonomous code safely at scale. In this hands-on workshop, you will build an agent on Amazon EKS using the Strands Agent SDK, MCP, and Amazon Bedrock, then progressively harden and operate it: run it with stronger workload isolation, apply controls over what it can access, establish scoped identity for secure communication, and manage its lifecycle in production. You will leave able to architect, deploy, secure, and operate production-ready agentic workloads on Kubernetes.

That's because every card swipe has to be evaluated before it's cleared to keep fraud from slipping through. Join Sivakumar Palanasami, Mastercard's EVP of Data Platforms, to learn how his team's real-time fraud decisioning model built with Redis on AWS and for a sneak peek of what they're doing next. sessions.abstract: Amazon Lightsail is a simple, low-cost cloud platform designed for small and medium business workloads. In this chalk talk, we start with an overview of what Lightsail offers and common use cases partners are delivering today. We then introduce the Lightsail Partner Program and the benefits available to partners who build their practice on Lightsail. Bring your scenarios. We'll work through partner economics, discuss real use cases, and how Lightsail helps partners tackle onboarding and scaling challenges. You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how to leverage Lightsail to build your partner business.

sessions.title: Building a private service fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
sessions.abstract: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts, whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities, creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don't cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. Bidirectional sharing doubles the problem. In this session, build a private service fabric, a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

sessions.title: Building a semantic layer with AWS Glue Data Catalog and AWS Context
sessions.abstract: In this chalk talk, we dive into how AWS Context assembles semantic data from multiple semantic stores to create a semantic layer, which is then turned into a unified context layer through a knowledge graph. This enables AI agents and analytics engines to understand business meaning, relationships, and intent — not just schema and location. We'll work through architecture patterns for defining semantic data annotations, propagating semantics across lakehouse tables, and exposing discoverable, agent-ready metadata at query time.

sessions.title: Building a Zero Trust for Agentic AI Practice: A Partner Framework
sessions.abstract: AI agents create identity, authorization, governance, and tenant-isolation challenges that map directly to partner revenue streams. In this builders' session, you'll work hands-on with the Zero Trust Agent Maturity (ZAM) Framework and configure Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Gateway to enforce verifiable agent identities, auditable interaction chains, and centralized policy authorization that scopes every agent action to its tenant boundary. You'll run a live ZAM assessment on a sample multi-tenant deployment, revealing security gaps that become partner opportunities: red-teaming engagements, MCP security proxies, multi-tenant isolation reviews, and compliance automation. Leave with a repeatable assessment methodology to secure multi-tenant agent deployments.

sessions.title: Building better quantum computers with digital twins
sessions.abstract: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. To design better error-correction strategies, simulating how real quantum hardware operates is essential, yet computationally intractable. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

sessions.title: Building Context-Aware Agents with AgentCore Memory
sessions.abstract: Customers expect personalized service and context retention without repeating themselves every session. In this lab, you build a customer service agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that remembers each client across conversations. You create a Memory resource with Semantic, Summary, and User Preference strategies, deploy a Lambda-based agent backed by Amazon Nova Lite, and seed multi-turn conversations. The agent retrieves preferences and facts from long-term memory to personalize responses and recommend products from a DynamoDB catalog.

sessions.title: Building Cross-Enterprise AI Agents with MCP and A2A on AWS
sessions.abstract: Enterprises run hundreds of applications from ERP, CRM, supply chain, and beyond and yet orchestrating intelligent actions across these systems remains a challenge. We explore how Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enable AI agents to seamlessly interact across application boundaries through a single, unified chat interface. Walk away with practical architecture patterns for connecting SAP and adjacent enterprise systems like SalesForce, ServicesNow etc into a cohesive, AI-powered automation layer

sessions.title: Building enterprise agent platform on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: As agents multiply across teams, platform owners need control without becoming a bottleneck. In this session, learn best practices for building a governance foundation for your agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Use gateway as a central control point for all agent-to-tool traffic, enforce authorization with policies at the infrastructure layer that agents cannot bypass, and propagate identity end to end for a complete audit trail. Use the Agent Registry to catalog, discover, and approve agents and tools across the organization, and end-to-end tracing for fleet-wide visibility. Includes a demo. Leave with a governance blueprint teams can adopt.

sessions.title: Building eval-driven observability for AI agents
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent systems fail in ways your dashboards cannot show: one agent hands off bad context, another retries, and the API still returns 200. In this live coding session, start with a multi-agent app on LangGraph, Strands, and CrewAI, and instrument it with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference. Trace it from the first prototype run, evaluate agents on demand with LLM-as-judge evaluators, A/B test prompt and model variants before promoting to production, pull production traces into a versioned dataset, reproduce the failure locally, and ship the fix. All from your IDE, without switching tools.

sessions.abstract: Event-driven architectures help development teams operate more independently, release features faster, and build more scalable applications. In this workshop, learn the fundamentals of event-driven design using Amazon SNS, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon EventBridge, and more. Through hands-on exercises, discover how to choose the right AWS messaging and eventing service for your use case, design loosely coupled systems that scale independently, and optimize for both cost and performance. Whether you're starting your event-driven journey or refining existing patterns, you'll leave with practical skills you can apply immediately. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.abstract: Event-driven architectures have powered serverless applications for a decade. Now AI agents bring non-deterministic producers, multi-step reasoning chains, and agent-to-agent coordination via events. Learn how the patterns you already know, such as queues, events, and retries, evolve when your consumers are autonomous agents rather than just microservices.

sessions.title: Building event-driven, multi-agent swarms on serverless
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent AI systems need communication that is decoupled, observable, and scalable. In this chalk talk, we show how to coordinate swarms of independent agents through event choreography on Amazon EventBridge. Each agent reacts to events and emits new ones rather than being told what to do by a central controller. We discuss how to handle multi-agent failure modes like cascading hallucinations and runaway event loops (circular delegation), and how to prevent independent agents from taking conflicting actions.

sessions.title: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
sessions.abstract: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.

sessions.title: Building for Always-On: Resilient Trading to Agentic AI on Modern Data Foundation (sponsored by Cognizant)
sessions.abstract: Learn how LPL Financial built an always-on trading platform on AWS that supports 32,000+ financial advisors with resilient, multi-region architecture for mission-critical, latency-sensitive workloads. Discover how a unified data foundation across trading, brokerage, and custodial systems creates a trusted layer for innovation, and learn the realities of deploying agentic AI in a regulated broker-dealer environment. Gain practical insights into architecture patterns, governance, real-time data access, key tradeoffs, and lessons learned that can help accelerate your own modernization and AI initiatives. This presentation is brought to you by Cognizant, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building globally distributed applications with DynamoDB global tables
sessions.abstract: Failures happen. Regions degrade, Availability Zones go offline, and networks partition. In this session, learn how to architect Amazon DynamoDB applications that maintain availability and data integrity across a spectrum of failure modes, from single-AZ impairments to full-Region disruptions. Explore the DynamoDB primitives that underpin resilience, including global tables, multi-Region strong consistency, backup and restore, snapshots, and streaming, and how to compose them into patterns that meet strict RTO and RPO objectives. Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.

Whether you're looking to improve coverage for distributed operations or exploring new connectivity options, come learn how satellite networking fits into your cloud network strategy.

Ontologies address this by giving AI systems a formal structure for knowledge: a graph defining what exists, how entities relate, and what questions are meaningful. In this workshop, build an ontology-driven semantic layer using Amazon Neptune to power accurate, trustworthy agentic workloads across diverse data sources. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building optimized enterprise HPC systems for CAE and CFD
sessions.abstract: High-fidelity Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations require significant compute infrastructure. We’ll discuss how organizations are migrating CAE and CFD workloads from on premises to AWS, combining scalable HPC infrastructure with cloud-native engineering applications to accelerate product development. Learn how to architect your enterprise HPC system to optimize cost, queue wait times, and throughput with Amazon EC2 HPC-optimized instances, Savings Plans, and Amazon FSx.

sessions.title: Building Production Graph Pipelines with Nodestream and Amazon Neptune
sessions.abstract: Nodestream is an open source declarative framework for building, maintaining, and analyzing graph data, built collaboratively by engineers at Intuit and AWS. In this chalk talk, we'll explore how Nodestream connects data sources like Apache Kafka, APIs, and files to graph databases with automatic schema migrations and zero database-specific code. We'll dive into the Amazon Neptune plugin, discuss how declarative pipelines eliminate brittle ETL, and share lessons learned from real world customer scenarios. Bring your graph data challenges and we'll solve them live.

sessions.title: Building production-ready agents securely: lessons from AWS at scale
sessions.abstract: Most AI agent demos work on stage but break in production. Real enterprise agents need multi-layer guardrails, tenant identity isolation, graceful degradation, and continuous evaluation. In this code talk, we share patterns from shipping two production security agent systems on AWS: one that investigates incidents across customer accounts, and one that helps security practitioners author threat detections. We cover practices that any team can adopt such as prompt injection defense, tenant-scoped sessions, circuit breakers, observability, and eval-driven improvement.

sessions.title: Building Proprietary Multi-Agentic AI Workflows for Low Latency and High Reliability (sponsored by Capital One)
sessions.abstract: Enterprise AI requires scalable, multi-agentic workflows capable of handling complex reasoning without sacrificing real-time speed. This session explores how Capital One designs proprietary multi-agent systems on AWS, optimized for governance, performance, and reliability. You’ll hear how state-of-the-art serving frameworks like vLLM, efficient distributed serving platforms like llm-d, and advanced agentic inference optimization techniques can enhance latency and boost throughput. We’ll showcase these principles through real-world applications, including complex real employee- and customer-facing banking use cases while meeting rigorous business standards around accuracy, reliability, and risk management. This presentation is brought to you by Capital One, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building resilience against ransomware using AWS Backup
sessions.abstract: To counter evolving cyber threats, organizations must fortify their backup infrastructure for recovery resilience. This session applies threat modeling to design a multi-account AWS Backup architecture across three pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and guaranteed accessibility. Walk through a phased reference architecture using logically air-gapped vaults for tamper-proof backups, restore testing and GuardDuty malware scanning for integrity assurance, and multi-party approval for secure recovery during account compromise. Learn how to define your minimum viable company to sequence recovery priorities, distinguish cyber RPO from operational RPO, and align your strategy to NIST CSF 2.0 for recovery resilience and business continuity.

sessions.title: Building resilient Amazon ECS applications: a multi-layer approach
sessions.abstract: In this interactive chalk talk, we explore how to build resilient Amazon ECS architectures by examining failure modes across multiple layers of the stack. We walk through specific scenarios such as deployment failures, Availability Zone impairments, and dependency cascades that cycle tasks faster than you can debug them. We discuss architectural patterns, ECS capabilities for resilience, and common mistakes to avoid that turn minor issues into incidents. You'll leave with a concrete mental model for hardening your ECS services and a checklist you can apply to your own workloads.

sessions.title: Building resilient authentication with Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication
sessions.abstract: Authentication is the front door to your app, and if that's unavailable, everything is unreachable. Amazon Cognito is the managed CIAM service that handles sign-up, sign-in, federation, and threat protection at scale. In this chalk talk, learn how Cognito's new multi-Region replication (MRR) unlocks resilient authentication across Regions. We'll whiteboard reference architectures for B2C, B2B, and M2M workloads, cover implementation considerations like customer managed keys and in-Region dependencies, and walk through failover strategies. Leave ready to architect authentication that keeps customers connected.

sessions.title: Building resilient deployment pipelines with Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Every application has a different risk profile when you ship a new version. A payments API needs different safeguards than a marketing page. In this workshop, learn how to match Amazon ECS deployment strategies to your workload requirements. Configure blue/green deployments for services requiring instant failback, canary deployments for APIs where you validate with real traffic before full cutover, and linear deployments for gradual migrations that build confidence at each step. Integrate pause hooks for manual approvals and external validation, and set alarm-based triggers that automatically revert bad releases before customers notice. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Building searchable live sports with AWS Elemental and Amazon CloudFront
sessions.abstract: Live sports fans no longer watch one feed and wait for the recap. They expect every angle live and every key play instantly findable. In this session, see how you turn live sports into searchable fan moments on AWS. Using AWS Elemental inference, the platform generates highlight clips in real time and pairs them with conversational AI powered by Amazon Bedrock, so fans can ask for "the catch in the third quarter" and get it in seconds instead of hours. Then go deeper into the delivery workflow: composing multi-view experiences so viewers follow simultaneous matches and camera angles, enriching clips with AI-generated titles and captions, and delivering live feeds and clips globally through a single Amazon CloudFront architecture.

sessions.title: Building Serverless AI agents
sessions.abstract: AI agents need more than an LLM and a prompt. Production agents require tool execution with least-privilege isolation, orchestration that recovers from partial failures, and observability that tracks token spend alongside function duration. In this chalk talk, we discuss architectural patterns for Serverless AI agents: model routing across providers and cost tiers, fault-tolerant orchestration with Step Functions and Lambda durable functions, isolated code execution using MicroVMs, and state management for long-running multi-step workflows. We whiteboard the decisions that matter for your workload shape and where each pattern introduces complexity you may not need.

sessions.title: Building the data architecture that survives agentic analytics (sponsored by Edelbyte)
sessions.abstract: Human queries are bounded, repeatable, and predictable, so techniques like caching, sampling, and precomputation keep them fast and affordable. AI agents are none of those. One prompt becomes dozens of novel, complex queries at machine speed, so caching an agent's curiosity is nearly impossible. At a leading automotive R&D group, 1,400 engineers and their agents query 200 petabytes of vehicle telemetry, with 600 terabytes ingested daily, to engineer higher-quality, more reliable vehicles and reach production faster. This session shows the AWS architecture behind it and how it delivers real-time analytics with full retention at the scale agents have made standard. This presentation is brought to you by Edelbyte, an AWS Partner.

On AWS that means a unified data foundation across electornic health records, claims, images, devices, and genomics; real-time AI at the point of decision; agentic workflows that absorb entire categories of administrative burden; and governance that holds up to audit at scale. Chief Information, Digital, and AI Officers building this now share what worked and what they would do differently. Attendees leave with a practical sequence, from data foundation to agentic deployment. This presentation is brought to you by PwC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building the semantic intelligence layer for enterprise AI agents
sessions.abstract: Every AI agent in the enterprise reasons better when it shares a common semantic understanding of the business. In this chalk talk, we show you how to build an Agentic Intelligence Layer that resolves meaning across every system and makes it innately consumable by any agent. We break down how to combine semantic embeddings, knowledge graph relationships, and natural-language memories into a single, governed layer that every agent reads from and writes back to. We take product and customer intelligence as the first domains and show how the same architecture extends to supply chain, operations, finance, and workforce. The result is a semantic intelligence layer that compounds learning across the business and transforms everything from demand forecasting to conversational commerce to enterprise decision-making.

In this session, we'll show how Check Point's AI security intelligence integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to enforce real-time guardrails at the agent runtime layer inspecting intent, validating actions, and preventing policy violations before they execute. Walk away with a practical framework for securing agentic AI on AWS with Check Point. This presentation is brought to you by Check Point, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Building your first event-driven application
sessions.abstract: A customer places an order. Inventory updates. Payment processes. Notifications fire. In a monolith, one failure cascades through everything. In this builders' session, build a retail order system where each step runs independently using Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. Through guided exercises, you'll publish and subscribe to events, handle failures in one service without breaking others, and trace event flows across your system. No prior event-driven experience required—you'll leave with a working application and the core patterns for decomposing synchronous workflows into resilient, asynchronous systems. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Building zero-trust personal AI with EC2 confidential computing
sessions.abstract: Learn how Bee built a personal AI assistant where privacy is cryptographically guaranteed - not policy-promised. Bee processes user data exclusively within hardware-isolated EC2 Confidential VMs powered by AWS Nitro, where no one - including Amazon - can access unencrypted data. We'll dive into NitroTPM attestation that lets devices verify server integrity before sharing keys, Sigstore transparency logs for auditability, mutual TLS with embedded attestation proofs, and key lifecycle management within encrypted VM memory. A practical blueprint for building zero-trust AI on Amazon EC2.

sessions.title: Build interactive web apps with AWS Lambda
sessions.abstract: Web applications need persistent connections, session state, and native HTTP handling - capabilities that don't map obviously to Lambda's request-response model. In this session, see how to run web frameworks like Express, Hono, and Next.js directly on Lambda using runtime adapters that preserve the framework's native patterns. If you're running containerized web apps today, we walk through practical migration paths that move your existing framework code to Lambda with minimal changes.

sessions.title: Build It, Govern It, Ship It: A Hands-On Multi-Agent System with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.abstract: Building an AI agent is easy. Building one you can trust, safe, affordable, and contained, is the hard part. In this session we build a working agent end to end on AWS using the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit: Nemotron reasoning models served as NIM microservices on AWS GPUs, NeMo Guardrails screening every prompt and response at the inference boundary, NeMo Switchyard routing easy requests to smaller models and hard ones to larger models to cut inference cost, and OpenShell sandboxing tool execution at the kernel with Landlock, seccomp, and eBPF. You will see each layer added live, then watch a side-by-side cost and latency comparison of routed versus un-routed traffic. Everything runs on open foundations, on Amazon Bedrock and NIM-on-AWS. Leave knowing how to assemble safe, cost-aware agents from open components you can adopt one piece at a time. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

We demonstrate both, then whiteboard how they fit together architecturally. Come ready to challenge the design and share where you would use each.

sessions.title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
sessions.abstract: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.

sessions.title: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.

Deploy and test your multi-agent workflow end-to-end. Walk away with working code and reusable patterns for orchestrating collaborative AI agents using open source tooling.

sessions.title: Build nanochat models with PyTorch and Trainium-Easier than you think
sessions.abstract: Can you train an LLM on AWS Trainium, our purpose built AI chip for better price performance, using PyTorch with minimal code changes? We'll show you with nanochat, a 560M-parameter GPT you can train in about two hours on a single Trainium instance using familiar PyTorch workflows. We cover end-to-end training from data preparation through distributed configuration to model test practices with interactive chat — showing what works out of the box and what few changes are required. Walk away ready to train your own LLM on Trainium with PyTorch.

sessions.abstract: AI is moving beyond the cloud, requiring developers to deploy intelligent workloads across data centers, edge infrastructure, vehicles, industrial systems, PCs, and mobile devices. The challenge is scaling AI efficiently across diverse hardware environments. In this session, learn how Qualcomm and AWS enable developers to build agentic AI applications across the compute continuum, from cloud training to real-time edge and on-device inference. Discover how open frameworks, portable AI runtimes, and streamlined workflows accelerate development and deployment. Through examples spanning automotive, IoT, industrial edge, mobile, datacenter, and cloud use cases, explore how a unified developer experience reduces complexity, increases flexibility, and helps deliver scalable AI applications anywhere. This presentation is brought to you by Qualcomm, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build on top of large codebases without breaking your code
sessions.abstract: Your AI agent writes code fast, but when you unleash it on a large codebase, context can fill up quickly and the agent can make questionable implementation choices. Learn how Kiro uses neurosymbolic techniques to understand what you want to build, removing ambiguity, contradictions, and gaps in your requirements before any code is generated. Then, learn simple practices you can use to keep your agent implementation surgical, and detect drift before it spreads all over your codebase.

sessions.title: Build optimized, resilient inference endpoints on Amazon SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: Deploy, optimize, and monitor an LLM inference endpoint end to end on Amazon SageMaker AI. In this hands on workshop, use GenAI Inference Recommender to discover optimal configurations, cutting model deployment time to days instead of weeks, learn how to train EAGLE speculative decoding heads on your own data for up to 2.5× throughput gains, and benchmark results. Then, configure capacity aware instance pools with priority based GPU fallback and weighted autoscaling for production resilience. Throughout, interact with endpoints via OpenAI compatible APIs. You keep the working notebooks to reuse on your own endpoints.

Using MCP servers, your agent will reason job configurations, construct parameters, execute transformations, interact with the Glue Data Catalog, handle retries on failure, and surface results—all from a single conversational prompt.

In this Chalk Talk, we architect a production-ready solution using open building blocks: retrieval, reranking, and generation models working together in real time. We diagram how to fine-tune for your domain, orchestrate multi-model pipelines, and serve thousands of concurrent users cost-efficiently. Walk away understanding how Native Hugging Face models and libraries on AWS Trainium let you own your AI stack and scale.

See how to keep agent behavior measurable, access secure, and actions aligned with organizational policies. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Build provable AI agents with Automated Reasoning checks
sessions.abstract: Neurosymbolic AI pairs the language understanding of LLMs with the mathematical rigor of automated reasoning, enabling agent decisions that are provably correct, not just statistically likely. In this hands-on workshop, you'll take real-world business rules (e.g. insurance eligibility or financial compliance) and formalize them into Automated Reasoning policies that agents invoke at decision time. Starting from natural-language documents, you'll translate requirements into verifiable logic, then integrate your policies with agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validating outputs at inference time. Leave able to build Automated Reasoning policies that guarantee correctness, where every decision is logically grounded, traceable, and auditable.

sessions.title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults
sessions.abstract: When ransomware compromises your account, your backups are the last line of defense. The question is whether they're isolated, verified, and accessible when you need them most. In this workshop, you'll work through a simulated account compromise using AWS Backup logically air-gapped vaults. You'll configure vault isolation policies to put backups out of reach, validate their integrity through restore testing, and orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised. Backup Audit Manager ties it together with compliance monitoring to prove your posture holds. You'll finish with a tested recovery playbook built against a live compromise scenario. Participants must bring a laptop.

Configure vault isolation policies, validate backup integrity, orchestrate recovery when primary credentials are compromised, and walk away with a tested recovery playbook. Connect your frontend to a serverless backend powered by AWS AppSync WebSockets. You must bring your laptop to participate.

In this hands-on lab, build reliable AI agents by fine-tuning an LLM on Amazon SageMaker AI for valid tool-call output and consistent persona, and connect it to Amazon Bedrock RAG to ground responses in your latest policies and customer data.

sessions.abstract: Building AI agents is easy, but securing enterprise data access without slowing development is hard. Teams often rely on static, over-privileged credentials, creating major security risks. But there’s a solution. This session explores how to secure agentic workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Okta. We’ll introduce the Blueprint Alliance, of which AWS and Okta are founding members, and cover how standards like Cross App Access (XAA) and SCIM for Agents transform AI identity. You'll learn how replacing static keys with dynamic, delegated permissions enables real-time policy evaluation at every tool call, empowering developers to build scalable, trusted AI agents that operate strictly within verified boundaries. Leave with a working reference implementation you can adapt to your financial services or enterprise environment.

You'll tune detection sensitivity, set approval gates for automated actions, and evaluate where autonomous remediation is safe versus where human oversight is required. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Build the full agent optimization loop on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: How do you know your agent is still performing? Stop guessing. sessions.title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
sessions.abstract: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

sessions.abstract:
AI agents behave (and fail) in unpredictable and nuanced ways that erode customer trust before engineering teams know anything is wrong. Teams want to deploy agents into critical business workflows, but it's hard to know if agents are behaving as intended or returning wrong answers.​

​

In this talk, you’ll learn how to observe the entire AI stack,
optimize tokenomics, and see a demo on how to evaluate

or inaccurate outputs. All of this can be done in near real-

sessions.title: Build your AI data pipeline to Amazon S3 and Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI applications are only as good as the data supporting them, and that data often lives across on-premises systems, other clouds, and distributed AWS storage. In this workshop, you'll build an end-to-end pipeline that moves data from these sources into Amazon S3 and connects it to Amazon Bedrock to build agentic applications. You'll configure data movement services including Storage Gateway, DataSync, and Transfer Family, establish secure transfer patterns, and integrate your migrated data into a gen AI workflow. Leave with a working architecture pattern for scalable data lakes that feed AI applications, grounded in real-world migration and processing scenarios.

sessions.title: Build your controls strategy org-wide to accelerate innovation
sessions.abstract: AWS Organizations policies drive governance through native service integrations. In this session, explore service control policies and resource control policies for data perimeters. Use declarative policies to enforce resource configurations, such as Amazon S3 public access restrictions, and centralize AWS Security Hub settings org-wide. Deploy AWS Config organizational rules and conformance packs for continuous compliance, leverage multi-party approval, enforce best practices via the AWS Control Tower controls catalog, and explore automated compliance assessments. Leave with a governance architecture driven by policy integrations.

As broadly available cyber models help threat actors find decade-old vulnerabilities, this session focuses on how defenders can put continuous defense into practice. This presentation is brought to you by OpenAI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal)
sessions.abstract: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
sessions.abstract: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

sessions.abstract: When AI agents and automated pipelines ship changes across AWS, Azure, and other providers in minutes, governance that runs on separate toolchains can't keep pace. You end up with disparate security findings along with mis-aligned operational metrics, and a team that spends its time reconciling dashboards instead of actually reducing risk. In this session, see how to collapse multicloud governance into a single operating model across AWS and Azure, leveraging Amazon CloudWatch unified telemetry for centralized observability and AWS Security Hub for aggregated findings into a single surface.You'll walk through a deployable architecture that gives one analyst a unified view across clouds, so your governance moves at the same speed your engineering teams already do.

sessions.title: Champagne AI on a beer budget: Cost-optimized AI architectures live
sessions.abstract: A surprise cloud bill can wipe out a nonprofit's budget, but running frontier-quality generative AI doesn't have to cost frontier prices. In this code talk, we build an architecture that gets premium model output on a fraction of the spend. Starting with a naïve workload where every request hits the same large model, we layer in routing to send requests to the lowest-cost model meeting the quality bar, caching to reduce token counts, and token budgets with kill switches that gracefully degrade. You'll leave with working code your engineers can implement, and your finance team won't panic over.

sessions.title: Chaos engineering: Network fault injection with Gateway Load Balancer
sessions.abstract: Your application works perfectly in the lab, but what happens with 45ms latency and 0.1% packet loss? In this session, deploy a transparent network fault simulator using AWS Gateway Load Balancer and Linux Traffic Control (TC) on Amazon EC2. Inject delay, jitter, packet loss, and bandwidth constraints into live traffic, then observe how a tightly coupled application degrades in real time. Use the results to set SLA thresholds, validate AWS Direct Connect failover behavior, and justify architectural decisions. Leave with a reusable, parameterized emulator pattern deployable via AWS Systems Manager.

sessions.title: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
sessions.abstract: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.

sessions.title: Choosing a game server instance without guessing
sessions.abstract: Most game studios pick server instances by vibes. This chalk talk replaces that with a number you measure on your game: cost per player at your tick rate. At the whiteboard we answer three questions: what does one tick cost, how many players fit, and what does a player cost? You’ll see how to time the whole tick in Unreal Engine and Unity, load a server with bots or thin clients against a failure rule set up front, and repeat across instances. Then we share what we measured on modern Amazon EC2 instances across AWS Graviton, AMD, and Intel: where clock speed pays, and where price decides.

sessions.title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
sessions.abstract: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. In this chalk talk, we break down the decision framework for selecting low-latency storage across common workload types. Bring your architecture questions as we compare directory buckets, parallel file systems, and caching strategies side by side. Leave with a clear mental model for matching your performance requirements to the right AWS storage tier.

sessions.title: Choosing the right AWS storage service
sessions.abstract: AWS storage spans block, file, and object services alongside purpose-built storage for vectors, tables, and migration, each optimized for distinct access patterns, latency requirements, and cost profiles. Choosing the most efficient option can help you reduce complexity, over-provisioning, or rearchitecting later. In this chalk talk, AWS storage experts walk you through a decision framework based on workload characteristics, not product names. Bring your architecture questions and work through real scenarios interactively. You will leave with a clear mental model for matching workloads to storage services and the confidence to make the right decision as your requirements evolve.

sessions.title: Choosing the right hybrid deployment for your AI workloads
sessions.abstract: Organizations are running AI workloads, including training, inference, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning, across an expanding set of environments, spanning AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, AWS Outposts, AWS Dedicated Local Zones, and AWS AI Factories. The right deployment option depends on latency, data sovereignty, compute density, and scale. Explore how customers deploy GPU-accelerated AI across the full hybrid spectrum: NVIDIA GPU-based and AWS Trainium-powered instances in Local Zones, purpose-built AWS AI Factories for large-scale training and model serving, and edge deployments for real-time inference. Hear how customers navigate these decisions and learn which environment fits each AI workload, without compromising performance or compliance.

sessions.title: Close the gap between code and production
sessions.abstract: Why is it so hard to connect a production alert to the code change that caused it? Metrics and traces reveal something is wrong but stop short of the function responsible. Developers guess which deployment introduced the regression, manually correlating dashboards with recent commits. Meanwhile, AI coding agents that could help write fixes are blind to runtime behavior. In this code talk, we'll explore how to close the gap between observability signals and the code your team owns, what new signals make that connection possible, how developers and AI agents can consume them, and what changes when observability reaches the code level.

sessions.title: Close the loop: From guardrail blocks into layered defense
sessions.abstract:
Guardrails block malicious prompts. Every blocked attempt is a signal: proof of what your defenses caught and a clue toward what will be attempted next. Capture that signal instead of discarding it. In this session, you design and deploy a layered enforcement architecture that closes the loop. A stateful detection tier identifies repeated probing across sessions and propagates block decisions to the network edge. You evaluate signals from guardrail violations and apply policies to classify and block the threat. You leave with a deployed pattern applicable to any AI agent workload.

Bring your laptop to participate.

You'll build auto-remediation with SSM Automation, package it into a Conformance Pack for org-wide reach, and use Resource Timeline to trace drift. You leave able to keep compliance closed however fast change arrives.

In this code talk, we build an AI agent from scratch using Lambda Durable Functions. You'll see how to implement a tool-use loop, add retries with exponential backoff, pause for human approval without paying for idle time, and recover cleanly from a mid-execution failure. We'll experiment with agent suspend and resume live, and watch it resume from a checkpoint deterministically. Leave with production-ready patterns for building stateful AI agents using familiar programming constructs.

sessions.title: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
sessions.abstract: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.

T-Mobile closes that gap with agent memory: session context pre-populated before the call starts, enriched turn by turn as it unfolds, with real-time graph traversal connecting customer, device, and issue so the rep sees the full picture. MongoDB Atlas runs it all, from vector search over T-Mobile's knowledge corpus to in-call graph traversal to the live session-memory documents. Afterward, AWS Neptune turns that history into a graph shaping future routing and retention. Walk away with an architecture pattern for building agent memory in real time, and a way to decide what belongs in short-term memory versus what should persist. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. sessions.title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect (sponsored by Deloitte)
sessions.abstract: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

sessions.title: Crossing the kill chain: IR when attackers pivot between clouds
sessions.abstract: When a threat actor compromises credentials in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool can follow. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the detection and response patterns for cross-cloud lateral movement using Security Hub, Inspector, and multicloud telemetry sources.

sessions.title: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
sessions.abstract: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Crypto escape room: race to migrate to quantum resistance
sessions.abstract: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway and here's a chance to hone your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, ML-DSA key for code signing, quantum ready PKI, and an audit of your PQ posture. Teams complete quests using the AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Private Certificate Authority, and AWS Secrets Manager services. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence to build quantum-resistant cryptographic infrastructure.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

sessions.title: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
sessions.abstract: What if your customers' data needs to stay invisible even to you? Cryptographic computing makes computation on encrypted data without decrypting it possible. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) has become practical for ML inference. In this session, learn what FHE is, why it now works at scale on AWS, and how to get started. We will walk through two examples: encrypted ML inference on medical images and financial transactions, and encrypted ETL that aggregates records without exposing individual values. Leave with a deployment blueprint built for regulated industries.

sessions.abstract: Ctrl+Alt+Ship is a choose-your-own-adventure experience with self-paced labs spanning Kiro, Amazon Quick, and Amazon Connect Customer. Start with the Kiro IDE for AI-native development, or level up to multi-agent workflows. Solve an escape-room-style corporate crisis using Quick, your AI work assistant, choosing between a guided investigation or an advanced multi-step operation to plan, execute, and automate your way to cracking the case. With Connect Customer, see how AI resolves customer issues, gives agents context, and helps supervisors improve service—or go hands-on with the agentic CX designer, a no-code visual canvas, to build conversational AI. AWS facilitators from each product team will be available to answer questions. Labs are 30-60 min. Workstations are provided; no reservation needed.

sessions.title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

sessions.title: Customize open models for accuracy, cost, and latency on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: An off-the-shelf model may not meet the accuracy, cost, or latency requirements of your specialized business task. Across businesses from retail to financial services, organizations are customizing open-weight models to unlock higher value. In this session, learn how to customize open-weight models with Amazon SageMaker AI, including for domain-specific workflows and agents. Intuit shares how it is using SageMaker AI with features such as serverless model customization and reinforcement learning, on its proprietary data to unlock business value and cut costs.

sessions.title: Customize workspaces and build guided workflows using AI in Connect Customer
sessions.abstract: In this workshop, you build the complete agent and business user experience in Amazon Connect Customer. First, you create persona-specific workspaces using the no-code UI builder, customizing page layouts, applications, and views so frontline agents, back-office workers, and supervisors each see only the information, tools, and guidance they need. Then, you create AI-powered guided workflows using natural language: describe the experience you want, and AI generates the step-by-step workflow automatically. You test and validate end-to-end in the Agent Workspace, seeing how custom layouts and AI-built guides work together to accelerate resolution. Walk away with persona-tailored workspaces and working guided workflows built in minutes instead of days.

sessions.title: Cut cost migrating agentic AI workloads to Graviton5 on EKS AutoMode
sessions.abstract: Learn how to cut agentic AI infrastructure costs by migrating to AWS Graviton5 on Amazon EKS Auto Mode — with no compromise on latency or reliability. This hands-on workshop covers the full playbook: building multi-architecture container images, designing ARM64 NodePools, configuring IAM Roles for Service Accounts for secure agent-to-AWS communication, and tuning Graviton-optimized inference runtimes for predictable tail latency. Run live cost benchmarks against x86 equivalents to see exactly where Graviton5 pays back, and instrument with CloudWatch Container Insights to confirm performance parity. Walk away with a reusable pattern, a reproducible benchmark methodology, and a clear migration path you can apply to your own workloads the same week.

sessions.title: Cut through Kubernetes signal overload with unified observability
sessions.abstract: Kubernetes at scale buries teams in high-cardinality signals that traditional pipelines truncate or split across separate backends, so the answer you need is never in one place. In this hands-on builders session, you send OpenTelemetry metrics and logs from an EKS cluster into Amazon CloudWatch, deploy Container Insights, and decide which signals actually matter. You use automatic resource enrichment to build your own dashboards and alerts, deciding what to alert on and why rather than running pre-made scripts. You leave knowing how to cut through high-cardinality noise and set up alerts that drive action.

sessions.abstract: Security Hub prioritizes critical security risks and helps you respond at scale. By correlating threats, vulnerabilities, and misconfigurations across AWS and multicloud environments, it surfaces attack paths and prioritizes what needs attention first. In this chalk talk, we deep dive into how exposures work, how risk prioritization scores are calculated, and how to operationalize the findings in your environment.

sessions.title: Cut through the options: Choosing the right AWS connectivity solution
sessions.abstract: AWS offers a growing range of connectivity services, including AWS Direct Connect, AWS Interconnect (multicloud and last mile), AWS Transit Gateway, and AWS Cloud WAN. But when should you use one over another? In this chalk talk, evaluate your connectivity options and avoid over-engineering your network design. Walk through real-world scenarios and a structured decision framework to understand which service aligns with your requirements. Attendees gain clear guidance and discover practical decision tools for selecting the right service for your scenario. Come prepared with your questions.

sessions.title: Cutting manual accounts payable work
sessions.abstract: Enterprise customers pay for cloud services across dozens of payer accounts and countries through procurement/accounts payable platforms like SAP Ariba and Coupa and track it all in spreadsheets and email threads. Purchase orders run out unnoticed. Payments land on the wrong invoices. Disputes take months. In this session, see how a new first-party application gives Accounts Payable teams one live view of purchase orders, invoices and payments matched against billing records no console login required.

sessions.title: Cut token costs by 50%: Building context efficient agents with Strands
sessions.abstract: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. This code talk covers the three-tier context cache hierarchy of AWS's open source Strands Agents SDK. We'll discuss context management as composable primitives with extension points for custom backends, compression, and retrieval. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. For developers building or extending agent frameworks.

sessions.title: Cut your data lake and lakehouse bills: Cost and performance tuning best practices
sessions.abstract: Open data lakehouses and data lakes can quietly accumulate cost through uncompacted small files, over-partitioned tables, and inefficient scan patterns. In this session, learn advanced cost savings and tuning techniques on AWS that cut storage and compute costs while improving performance. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, graviton efficiencies, intelligent-tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples of real-world workloads on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower you analytics costs.

sessions.title: Danske Bank's AI City: Scaling AI agents across an enterprise
sessions.abstract: Getting AI agents into production across a regulated enterprise means solving governance and security first. Danske Bank started with a handful of generative AI experiments and now runs more than 40 use cases in production. In this session, learn how Danske Bank built "AI City"—a governed, reusable platform that cut time-to-production from months to days. See how they structured the platform so new teams can ship agents without rebuilding authorization, logging, or model access controls from scratch, with production examples from personal banking, compliance, and capital markets, and explore the Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore architecture underneath it all.

sessions.title: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO)
sessions.abstract: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS  (sponsored by Veeam)
sessions.abstract: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Datacenter to Cloud: Safety, Security, & Trust for AI Agents & Models (sponsored by Red Hat)
sessions.abstract: Deploying enterprise AI requires a unified framework across four governance pillars: Safety, Security, Risk, and Trust. Demystify multi-layer vulnerabilities spanning base models, agentic harnesses, and tool usage, addressing threats like Mythos model risks. Learn defense-in-depth strategies for agents—including sandboxing, privilege control, reasoning tracing, and dynamic red-teaming—to mitigate prompt injection, data leakage, and excessive agency. We’ll map these practices to global frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act to ensure continuous production readiness. This presentation is brought to you by Red Hat, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: In this hands-on workshop, transform fictional retailer RetailMax's raw, ungoverned data into trusted, governed data products using Amazon SageMaker platform . Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Data mesh at scale: The automation layer, proven at Experian
sessions.abstract: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.
