sessions.title: Data Mesh to Agentic AI: Building an AI-Ready Enterprise on AWS
sessions.abstract: How do you build an AI-ready data foundation in a global investment organization without compromising trust, governance, or speed? CPP Investments—manager of one of the world’s largest pension funds—is evolving from fragmented data toward a governed enterprise data platform on AWS, using data mesh principles, federated ownership, and platform engineering to scale with guardrails. Join their CTO for a look inside the architecture, operating model, and critical trade-offs shaping this evolution, and how it brings trusted data closer to investment decisions while laying the foundation for conversational data experiences and agentic AI.

sessions.title: Data Prep to Deployment: How Tencent Games Scaled to 1,000 GPUs on SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Join us to see how Amazon SageMaker HyperPod lets teams build complete training pipelines, from data prep and transformations through distributed training to seamless model deployment, all on one resilient, self-healing platform with no re-platforming required. Then, hear how Tencent Games, a game AI team (not an infra team), went from first cluster to thousand-GPU training in weeks for their VISVISE engine powering 90+ titles including PUBG Mobile. Walk away with lessons learned from real production workloads and best practices for EFA networking, FSx storage, and GPU fault tolerance.

sessions.title: Data protection and resilience with AWS storage
sessions.abstract: Risks to data availability are intensifying, and the cost of getting recovery wrong is rising. Recovering well means recovering deliberately, not reactively, with a strategy built for the unpredictability of what can go wrong. In this session, you'll learn how the 3-2-1-1-0 defense-in-depth framework provides that structure, guiding you from failure scenario analysis through recovery objective planning to layered protection across local, cross-region, and immutable isolated copies. The result is a playbook for how AWS storage services bring each layer to life, from native replication and disaster recovery to centralized backup with immutable isolated vaults for cyber recovery.

sessions.abstract: Contact center AI agents require critical architecture decisions around tool integration, voice prompt engineering, and quality evaluation. In this chalk talk, we'll explore when to use first-party tools, when AWS Lambda gives you more flexibility, and when MCP integrations make sense—with latency, operational complexity, and compliance requirements as the deciding factors. We’ll discuss patterns for voice prompt engineering with Amazon Connect Customer AI agents and automated evaluation pipelines using Contact Lens and generative AI to score 100% of interactions. You'll leave with a decision model you can apply to your own contact center, including guidance for financial services and regulated industries.

sessions.title: Decompose a monolith database into microservices with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Enterprise architects face a critical challenge: breaking monolithic database-centric applications into microservices while managing risk and cost. Where do you draw domain boundaries? How do you extract 20 years of business logic from stored procedures into the application layer? This chalk talk reveals the two-layer decomposition strategy—combining database structure and runtime execution patterns—to identify service boundaries. Leveraging AWS Transform and Kiro, collapse months of manual analysis, design and development into hours of executable code. Through live whiteboarding, learn the data-driven framework enabling business logic extraction, independent deployment, licensing cost reduction, and faster modernization.

sessions.title: Decouple and scale Amazon ECS workloads with event-driven patterns
sessions.abstract: Not every container workload needs to run all the time. Some should wake up when an event arrives, process it, and stop. Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.

Amazon ECS makes this straightforward, but choosing the right trigger pattern matters. In this chalk talk, discuss how to connect events to containers using Amazon EventBridge, Amazon SQS, and AWS Step Functions. Walk through four common patterns: single-event task launch, queue-based consumer scaling, fan-out processing, and multi-step workflow orchestration. Explore how to handle failures gracefully with dead-letter queues and retry policies, and how Amazon ECS provides serverless compute for event-triggered deployments.

sessions.title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora and its innovations
sessions.abstract: With an innovative architecture that decouples compute from storage and advanced features like Aurora Global Database and low-latency read replicas, Aurora reimagines what it means to be a relational database. Aurora is a built-for-the-cloud, serverless relational database that delivers unparalleled performance and availability at global scale for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DSQL. In this session, dive deep into the newest Aurora features. Explore how Aurora supports agentic AI through vector search and MCP servers for agent access. Also, learn about Aurora DSQL, the fastest serverless distributed SQL database.

sessions.title: Deep dive into Amazon Aurora DSQL and its architecture
sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database that uses decades of Amazon innovation and operational excellence. In this session, dive into the design and key innovative technologies that make Aurora DSQL the ideal choice for new applications and applications that require the highest level of resilience. Learn how active-active architecture in Aurora DSQL delivers single- and multi-Region resiliency and virtually unlimited scale

Whether you're running financial trading platforms, gaming backends, or large-scale SaaS, learn practical blueprints for designing architectures that deliver high availability and predictable performance while maintaining inline security inspection and compliance.

sessions.title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
sessions.abstract: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

sessions.title: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4)
sessions.abstract: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Defeat Player Evasion: AI Moderation at Scale on Amazon Bedrock.
sessions.abstract: Players evade moderation with leetspeak, homoglyphs, emoji sequences, and fast-evolving slang. Brute-force AI classification catches evasion but is cost-prohibitive at scale. In this workshop, build a tiered moderation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock that routes 80–90% of traffic through deterministic normalization and pre-filters before invoking a model. Ambiguous content gets classified by Amazon Nova at sub-500ms latency. Only the hardest cases escalate to multi-agent analysis on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for context-dependent decisions. Configure per-category thresholds, instrument cost-per-decision tracking, and stress-test against real gaming evasion patterns. Walk away with a deployable, cost-optimized pipeline. Laptop required

sessions.title: Defending the Three Lanes: Preventing Toxic Agentic Combinations with Cyera and AWS (sponsored by Cyera)
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI is entering production faster than enterprise authorization models can keep up, and most access decisions are made without regard to the sensitivity of the data agents can reach, turning over-permissioned agents into high-value targets. This session introduces the three lanes: the data agents touch, the identity they act as, and the actions they take, as the framework for defending agentic AI on AWS. See how Cyera's Agent Guardian extends Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with data-aware authorization to enforce least privilege, monitor agent-to-data activity, and prove it to auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Defense-in-Depth for Containers on Amazon EKS: A Layering Story
sessions.abstract: On a default Amazon EKS cluster, a single pod is a compromise away from the whole cluster - shared node credentials, flat networking, implicit trust, open egress. In this code-first session we start there, then trace how EKS security grew layer by layer as the threat model matured. We rebuild an over-privileged workload live, adding one control at a time: scoped pod identity, admin and DNS network policies, and private certificate trust with zero-downtime CA rotation. We finish by running a lateral-movement attempt against the hardened workload and watching it fail at multiple layers — the whole point of defense-in-depth.

sessions.title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
sessions.abstract: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.

We'll cover building a compelling case for change, defining KPIs that resonate with executives, and driving adoption through change management. Learn the pitfalls that stall outcome conversations, how to accelerate buy-in, and how to frame impact in terms executives act on. Leave with a repeatable approach for your next engagement and a foundation for a customer success practice that scales.

Guardrails automatically redact low-risk identifiers and block critical PHI, routing flagged content through Amazon EventBridge to an SQS review queue. AWS CloudTrail captures the full audit trail, and IAM restricts the agent to BAA-covered services only. You leave with a deployable CDK stack ready for production.

sessions.title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Build a multi-agent architecture on Amazon EKS using S3 Files as the shared workspace and S3 Vectors as persistent semantic memory. Mount an S3 file system across agent containers using standard POSIX file I/O. Agents read, write, and hand off artifacts without custom SDKs or message brokers. A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

sessions.abstract: Millions of patients wait too long for imaging each year as demand outpaces capacity, and the shortage is projected to worsen significantly by 2030. sessions.abstract: Multimodal AI agents need to understand more than text and interact through more than a screen. We’ll examine cross-modal retrieval, audio and video segmentation, multimodal context, conversational orchestration, latency, and grounding tradeoffs for building responsive agents that can listen, understand, retrieve, and converse across modalities.

sessions.title: Designing for Operability: Catching Performance Gaps Before Scale
sessions.abstract:
A training workload had plenty of GPU capacity, yet utilization remained low and training time kept increasing. The GPUs were healthy. The real bottleneck was upstream: the data pipeline could not feed them fast enough, leaving expensive accelerators waiting for work.

This talk walks through how we traced that utilization gap, found where throughput was being lost, and identified the signals that could have exposed the problem earlier. Through this production experience, we’ll look at what it means to design for operability before scale, when performance, utilization, and cost problems are still easier to fix.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

sessions.title: Designing performant and cost-effective data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
sessions.abstract: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. In this session, we dive into the design and maintenance choices that determine whether your Iceberg lake stays fast and cost-efficient or slowly deteriorates, including compaction strategies, snapshot expiration, and partition design. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.

sessions.title: Designing Portable Multicloud Architectures with Open Specifications
sessions.abstract: Enterprises pursuing multicloud strategies often equate portability with containerization — but true architectural portability requires deliberate decisions across the full stack. In this chalk talk, we start from the foundational layers of compute, storage, and networking and build outward through data, security, observability, and AI. At each layer, we explore how open specifications enable portability — and in what parts of your architecture does portability matter most. Along the way, we challenge common myths: that managed services equal lock-in, that Kubernetes equals portable, and that open source alone guarantees freedom. Through interactive whiteboarding, we'll design portable architecture patterns together — examining real trade-offs, open specifications like Apache Iceberg, OpenTelemetry, OPA, and MCP, and how to make deliberate portability decisions across your stack.

sessions.title: Designing security governance for your AWS multi-account foundation
sessions.abstract: AWS gives you flexibility to design your multi-account environment, but customer needs guidance choosing the right security services to deploy, where, and how to validate the deployment against AWS best practices. This session shows how the AWS Security Reference Architecture provides a prescriptive security blueprint you layer on top of your account governance foundation. Using whiteboarding, you cover OU design, service prioritization, centralized vs. distributed placement, design considerations, validation with SRA Verify, and deployment acceleration. You leave with a tailored governance model ready for implementation.

sessions.title: Designing your AWS network for scale: From one VPC to many
sessions.abstract: You started with a single Amazon VPC, and it worked. But as your organization grows, so does your network complexity. In this chalk talk, we'll work through the decision points of scaling from one VPC to many. When should you split workloads? How do you connect VPCs - peering, hub-and-spoke, or mesh? How do you segment traffic, centralize inspection and egress, plan IP addressing at scale, and integrate hybrid connectivity? Bring your architecture challenges, and we'll draw through solutions together on the whiteboard.

sessions.abstract: Most AI agent projects stall between pilot and production. In this workshop, you go from an idea to a production-ready agentic customer experience in a single session using Amazon Connect Customer. No months-long timeline.

sessions.title: Design your AWS Transform pipeline for parallel modernization at scale
sessions.abstract: How do you modernize thousands of applications concurrently to meet aggressive migration timelines? In this chalk talk, we'll work through architectural patterns for scaling AWS Transform with CI/CD integration: parallel processing with serverless compute, programmatic orchestration via APIs, container strategies, observability at scale, and campaign coordination across teams. Bring your use case and whiteboard it with us. Whether you need pipeline integration, secure private repo processing, or a self-service modernization platform, we'll design your architecture together.

sessions.title: Design your cedar authorization model with AI coding agents
sessions.abstract: Your identity provider handles authentication, but how do you design the authorization model that follows? In this chalk talk, learn how to use OIDC token claims from providers, including Amazon Cognito, with a Cedar-based authorization model. We'll walk through implementing RBAC, ReBAC, and ABAC patterns locally or in Amazon Verified Permissions, and show how to use AI coding agents (Kiro, Claude) to generate your schema and policies. Bring your use case for this interactive session. You'll leave with a repeatable approach to designing fine-grained authorization from scratch.

sessions.title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
sessions.abstract: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

sessions.title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
sessions.abstract: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

sessions.title: Developing Apps from Specs with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Kiro, the Agentic IDE, transforms a single natural language prompt into structured requirements, a technical design, and an executable implementation plan. You also configure a Kiro Hook that automatically validates data files on save.

The role of a developer has shifted, with organisations moving from AI adoption to looking for impact. This is presenting developers with new opportunities and challenges. What are the organisations and developers who are moving faster, and delivering at a higher quality point doing differently to those still looking for impact? In this session, we’ll explore the results from the latest State of DevEx report, diving into how developer roles have changed, and how you can unlock the transformational power of AI. This presentation is brought to you by Atlassian, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
sessions.abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall every active generation — and letting each phase scale on its own terms. It isn't free: KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still win. The difference is your traffic. In this hands-on builders session, you run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn the decision framework — input length, prefix reuse, latency SLO — and leave with runnable configurations.

We'll walk through the request lifecycle, debate trade-offs around latency, budgets, and MCP tool calls, and show how the same broker pattern governs any agent touching sensitive data.

sessions.title: Drug discovery and materials use cases with Amazon Braket and Q-CTRL
sessions.abstract: Classically hard problems such as simulating strongly correlated electrons and 1D NMR spectra, critical to material and drug discovery, can be sped up on quantum computers but until now had not been demonstrated. Q-CTRL shows how Fire Opal on Amazon Braket enables simulating 1D NMR spectra for spin systems up to 34 qubits and achieved a 3,000x speedup on the Fermi-Hubbard model at 120 qubits, demonstrating practical quantum advantage. This chalk talk unpacks how AWS hybrid workflows enabled these outcomes and what enterprises should do now to capture ROI with quantum.

sessions.title: DTCC: Rethinking mainframe modernization with spec-driven development

DTCC has adopted a spec-driven approach to COBOL refactoring, front-loading the process with a focus on principles, target architecture, and anti-pattern avoidance. In this session, you’ll see how a small team of engineers produced a fully functional microservice-based trade data ingestion platform in a few weeks, cutting the development timeline by 60% while laying the foundation to scale to peaks of 300+ million trades per day and beyond.

sessions.title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
sessions.abstract: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

sessions.title: EC2 at 20: Rebuilding the control plane while it is running
sessions.abstract: Amazon EC2 launched in 2006 as four services backed by a single MySQL database. Twenty years later, it is one of the largest distributed systems ever built — and most of that original architecture had to be replaced while serving production traffic, with no maintenance window and no change to the API contract customers depend on. In this session, EC2 engineers dive deep on two of the hardest migrations: making the control plane Availability Zone independent so a single-AZ event cannot escalate into a regional one, and moving EC2 metadata off MySQL. We walk through the failure modes that forced each decision, how correctness was verified before every cutover, how we proved a single-AZ failure stays in a single AZ, and the things we got wrong along the way. You will leave with migration and isolation patterns you can apply to your own systems at any scale.

sessions.title: EC2 Flex and T instances: Get modern performance at lower cost

Whether you're new to EC2 or a seasoned practitioner, leave with a clear map of modern compute on AWS.

sessions.title: EFA deep dive: Architecture, evolution, and scaling with OpenAI
sessions.abstract: We built EFA to deliver multi-tenant, elastic, high-performance networking with portability across every instance type and accelerator through Libfabric. The architecture that followed, such as multipath packet spraying, out-of-order delivery, and encryption of every byte in transit, has scaled from HPC workloads to the backbone of today's largest AI training clusters. Now it's evolving again to support disaggregated inference and expert parallelism. OpenAI joins to share how they adapted their production inference stack to EFA on EC2 UltraServers, covering Reliable Datagram semantics for GPU-to-GPU collectives, NCCL tuning, and topology-aware communication patterns that unlock new performance.

sessions.title: Elastic Fabric Adapter powering the largest AI workloads on AWS
sessions.abstract: AWS built Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to bring high-performance networking to the cloud - powered by the Scalable Reliable Datagram (SRD) protocol designed for elastic, reliable, cloud-scale performance. This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.

sessions.title: Elasticsearch - the Search database for Context Engineering and AI (sponsored by Elastic)
sessions.abstract: Your agentic applications have an accuracy and cost problem, and it's not your model choice. Sound familiar? If you're a developer trying to get LLMs to work effectively with your business context, this session is for you. Come learn how we rearchitected Elasticsearch as the database of choice for the different data types your enterprise knowledge is buried in — docs, logs, metrics, tickets, sales call transcripts, and more. From foundational innovations like Columnar and VectorDB mode with no ETL, to best-in-class retrieval that combines vector search, Jina embedding models, and native inference, Elastic is the context database for your production needs. Join this session to learn the best practices, from optimizing data preparation to retrieval patterns, to make your agents a production reality. This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Elevate your observability with OpenTelemetry on AWS
sessions.abstract: Getting full visibility across your stack shouldn't mean stitching together disconnected tools and proprietary formats. When you standardize on OpenTelemetry with AWS, you get rich, unified telemetry from metrics, logs, and traces across your containers, Kubernetes clusters, AI workloads, and everything in between. Collect deep telemetry using OTLP ingestion, PromQL querying, and automatic enrichment with Amazon CloudWatch's native OpenTelemetry. No fragmented data. No vendor lock-in. Just one telemetry foundation that gives you the context you need to understand what's happening across your entire environment. Learn how to achieve richer data, unified observability, and a production-ready architecture that scales with you.

sessions.title: Eliminate wasted compute capacity with Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Running containers on Amazon EC2 often means paying for capacity you never use, from idle instances to fleets that drift out of shape as workloads change. This chalk talk shows how Amazon ECS Managed Instances tackles that waste through consolidation and infrastructure optimization, automatically right sizing instances to real demand and repacking workloads off underutilized capacity. Work through practical scenarios on the whiteboard to see how these decisions play out and how instance selection and capacity provider design shape your monthly bill. Bring the cost and utilization challenges from your own clusters, because this session is driven by group discussion.

sessions.title: Embed Amazon Quick Chat Agents in Enterprise Applications
sessions.abstract: Deploy a fully serverless, production-ready solution that embeds Amazon Quick agents and dashboards into your enterprise web applications. Using AWS CDK, configure Amazon Cognito OAuth 2.0 authentication, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, and WAF to create a secure embedding architecture. Implement the Quick Embedding SDK, configure domain security and token validation, and deploy a working chat agent accessible from any enterprise application — turning Quick into the conversational AI layer that meets users where they already work.

In this chalk talk, we explore the newest collaboration paradigms gaining momentum, including ephemeral agent patterns and self-improving agents, alongside established approaches like hierarchical, sequential, and peer-to-peer coordination. Walk through how to apply these patterns to claims adjudication, underwriting, and financial portfolio advisory using Strands Agents and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness engineering best practices. We'll discuss when to select each pattern, how to combine them for complex workflows, and how AgentCore harness capabilities enable scalable, governed multi-agent architectures. sessions.title: Empowering 155,000 people without compromising trust: Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Allianz needed to empower 155,000 employees with AI without sacrificing trust. With operations across dozens of regulated markets, the security, privacy, and works council requirements were non-negotiable. Every stakeholder asked the same question: how do you move fast and still earn the trust of those guarding your company's security? Hear how Allianz partnered with AWS to deploy the capabilities that make Amazon Quick enterprise-ready: protection of confidential information, structured approval workflows for agentic actions, custom branding per business unit, and multi-language support. Learn how Allianz navigated the full approval process and moved from "not yet" to "go" in six weeks.

sessions.abstract: Agentic coding loops let AI develop, test, and iterate on code autonomously. This session will show how simulating your AWS application environments locally can enable AI agents to identify and fix bugs faster, more securely, and more effectively than human engineers can when building in live cloud development environments. sessions.title: Encoding Authorization in Logic from Puzzles to Production
sessions.abstract: Automated theorem provers can reason symbolically about a system's behavior and prove properties like "no user can ever escalate their own privileges" across all possible inputs. Of course, this requires modeling your problem in first-order logic, which demands careful thinking to precisely capture all behaviors of your system. In this session, learn how to encode your problem in first-order logic: starting with a logic puzzle to build intuition, then a toy authorization language, and finally what it takes for a full production system like Cedar, a fine-grained authorization language built with high assurance. We discuss challenges including ensuring correctness and completeness of the encoding.

sessions.abstract: Legacy applications across mainframe, midrange, and distributed platforms have long resisted modernization efforts. A new approach that combines deterministic methods with agentic AI is changing that by delivering speed and accuracy. Learn how United Airlines modernized crew operations while maintaining FAR compliance, and how Bank Hapoalim analyzed a 3.2-million-line mortgage application and delivered an insurance module to production under a board-mandated deadline while reducing operational risk. Follow the end-to-end journey, from automated discovery and business rule extraction with AWS Transform through microservices engineering with Kiro to production deployment. Leave with a playbook for modernizing the applications everyone said were untouchable.

sessions.title: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j)
sessions.abstract: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. See how NetEase enforces governance with company-wide AI policies, Bedrock Guardrails for content safety, and Bedrock AgentCore for orchestrating agentic AI workflows with centralized governance and observability. sessions.title: Escaping IIoT Pilot Purgatory: Why Your Database Breaks at Scale (sponsored by Tiger Data)
sessions.abstract:
Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen.

See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. This presentation is brought to you by Tiger Data, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Evaluate and ship AI agents confidently
sessions.abstract: Amazon CloudWatch Omni converges application and AI agent observability into one AI-powered experience built on open standards. In this session, instrument an agent with a popular framework and trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step in the Trace Explorer. Run built-in evaluators to score responses for correctness, coherence, and faithfulness, then test prompt variations in the Playground and compare configurations against golden datasets with Experiments. Explore auto-discovered topology, correlate agent behavior with downstream services, and investigate issues with AWS DevOps Agent using natural language. sessions.title: Evaluate, Disclose, Safeguard: A Production-Readiness Framework for AI Agents
sessions.abstract: Every organization is building AI agents, but few have made it to production. You can't prove it works, you can't prove it's responsible, and compliance won't sign off. In this chalk talk, we walk through a production-readiness framework for AI agents on Amazon Connect. First, evaluation: measuring resolution with the Connect Simulation API to score AI agents on the same bar as human agents. Second, responsible AI: disclosure patterns that build trust, escalation triggers for sensitive journeys, and harm avoidance for regulated industries. Third, safeguards: defense-in-depth governance for agents that process refunds and access sensitive data, including asymmetric PII, MCP tool authorization for human confirmation, and automated escalation when confidence drops. Leave with a checklist: what to measure, what to disclose, what to block, and when to ship.

sessions.abstract: Production agents need to dispatch long-running actions, wait on external systems, fan results out to analytics, and re-enter the conversation when work finishes — not sit in a synchronous loop. sessions.title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does

Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: ​​Every Candidate, Every Time: AI-Led Structured Interviews at Scale
sessions.abstract: ​​Who you hire is the most important decision you make, and the hardest to get right at scale. What if AI agents could run structured interviews grounded in Amazon’s hiring science and evaluate every candidate the same way? In this chalk talk, we show how role requirements become evaluation criteria and questions, how AI agents hold a natural conversation while covering each competency and gathering evidence, and how responses are scored against a rubric tied to specific evidence. See a single job posting become a scored, evidence-backed evaluation. Leave knowing how to tell hiring science from gut feel, and why that shows up in better hires and a fairer experience for every candidate.

sessions.title: Every Flight Has a Story. Here’s What It Takes to Power It. (sponsored by ZS)
sessions.abstract: United and ZS go behind the scenes of the data, AI and technology powering personalized flight stories for travelers at scale. This presentation is brought to you by ZS, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

sessions.title: Everyone is a Coder. Govern what they build. (sponsored by Coder)
sessions.abstract: Suddenly, everyone is a coder. People who never wrote code now build apps, dashboards, and prototypes with AI, faster than most teams can govern them. The result is shadow AI, ungoverned data, and IP risk. See how a leading global private investment firm gave citizen developers a governed place to build on its existing AWS infrastructure, replacing scattered, unmanaged tools. Learn how approved models, scoped templates, centralized container management, and a complete audit trail let hundreds of builders move fast inside guardrails. Attendees leave with a practical model for governing AI adoption on their own AWS environment. This presentation is brought to you by Coder, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Everyone Says They Have an Ontology. Almost Nobody Does (sponsored by TextQL)
sessions.abstract: Ontology has become one of the defining ideas in enterprise AI. Every cloud and data platform now claims to have one. They rarely converge on the same structure, conventions, or architecture. Those differences determine whether an ontology can support agentic AI. That test comes down to three things: how it's structured, how it's generated from the systems and context already in place, and how it stays current as the business changes. This talk lays out the practical requirements for an ontology built for agentic AI, drawing on the architecture TextQL runs across the messiest data estates at Fortune 50 companies. This presentation is brought to you by TextQL, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

sessions.title: Everything your web app needs in one place
sessions.abstract: Your coding agent builds fast but builds across providers. The result: a multi-vendor stack you didn't design, limits you can't grow past, and costs you can't predict. In this lightning talk, see a live demo: one prompt to go from code to a full-stack web application, integrated and ready in seconds. One account, one bill, spending caps you set. Built on open source, runs on AWS. Easy to start, built to last.

sessions.abstract: Getting the best compute performance is an art, and knowing low-level details helps a lot. This talk covers everything you've wanted to know: memory topology, accessing hardware counters, hyperthreading side-effects, and how to properly run performance tests and optimize your latency for production.

sessions.title: Evolve Amazon DynamoDB data models with no application impact
sessions.abstract: Master advanced techniques for evolving Amazon DynamoDB data models without application interruption. Learn versioning strategies, backward compatibility patterns, and migration approaches for production applications. In this session, architect a solution that covers attribute addition and removal, data type changes, and index modifications while maintaining 24/7 availability. Explore real-world migration scenarios, rollback strategies, and handling distributed application dependencies. The best practices covered in this session are essential for teams managing large-scale DynamoDB applications requiring continuous evolution while serving millions of requests.

sessions.title: Expand your GPU playbook: Amazon EC2 G7e/G7 for inference and training
sessions.abstract: Not every ML workload needs the same GPU. Amazon EC2 G7e and G7 instances, powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with GDDR7 and native FP4 support, deliver compelling price-performance for inference and select training use cases. This session breaks down where G7e/G7 fits: inference prefill (competitive FLOPS/$) and decode (FP4 and higher concurrency close the HBM gap), and training via pipeline parallelism. We'll cover the toolchain (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TransformerEngine, CUTLASS FP4 kernels), walk through a TCO comparison, and close with a decision framework for when G7e/G7 is the right call vs. P-family instances.

sessions.title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
sessions.abstract: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. In this chalk talk we benchmark four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI for lazy-loading container image layers, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU pipelining. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.

sessions.title: Experience catalog federation on AWS: build a multi-cloud open data lakehouse
sessions.abstract: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.

sessions.title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
sessions.abstract: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with Amazon Inspector Code Security to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

sessions.title: Explore agentic data engineering in Amazon SageMaker
sessions.abstract: Data engineering teams lose time to siloed data, manual ETL, and tribal knowledge. This session shows how agents change that in Amazon SageMaker. Use SageMaker Data Agent to trace errors, refactor code, and deploy pipelines in natural language, then bring your own agents through MCP servers to work with third-party clients and models directly on your data. See how the same agentic approach extends across SageMaker, so teams can consolidate fragmented pipelines, standardize environments, and put agents to work on more of the data engineering lifecycle.

sessions.title: Extend Amazon EKS clusters for on-premises and edge use cases
sessions.abstract: This chalk talk covers strategies for modernizing distributed applications with Amazon EKS across AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, and AWS Outposts. It demonstrates how EKS delivers a consistent experience across these deployment options, minimizing latency and enabling data residency. The session explores deploying a real-world application to an EKS cluster across distributed environments while maintaining a unified control plane. It covers use cases and design patterns for architecting resilient and scalable applications, following AWS Well-Architected Framework principles for consistency and security.

sessions.title: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm)
sessions.abstract: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
sessions.abstract: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, you'll design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. We'll start with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability. Then, we'll work through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links. You'll leave with reference architectures you can adapt to your environment and a clear understanding of how the constellation fits in your network design.

sessions.title: Fanatics path to AWS: 5 data centers, 1,800 servers, 48% savings
sessions.abstract: If your migration is stuck because no one can agree on what moves first while licensing costs compound and dependencies stay undocumented, the problem isn’t willingness. It’s sequencing. Fanatics Commerce had 1800 servers across five data centers and projected 48% infrastructure savings on AWS. Their team shares the structured path: OLA for licensing clarity, DAP for dependency mapping, EBA for organizational alignment, MAP for execution. Walk away with: (1) a concrete OLA-to-MAP sequence, (2) an AI-assisted dependency mapping approach that surfaced connections no one had documented (3) a phased AWS Transform modernization strategy that earns engineering trust before scaling.

sessions.title: Fast and easy bulk operations with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: In this session, learn patterns for executing fast, safe, cost-aware bulk operations in Amazon DynamoDB using AWS Glue, Spark SQL, and open source tooling that hides the complexity. Discover how to find, filter, diff, load, and update billions of items in parallel. Explore how lightweight AI can make bulk work more powerful and user-friendly. Learn proven patterns, real-world workload insights, and tools that simplify DynamoDB bulk processing.

sessions.title: Faster root cause analysis for IAM access denied errors
sessions.abstract: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. Now, access denied error messages go beyond surfacing the policy type or ARN that blocked a request—they tell you the exact reason access was denied. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.

sessions.title: Faster tech debt remediation without the setup overhead
sessions.abstract: In this Code Talk, learn how continuous modernization enables faster tech debt analysis and remediation by starting directly from your cloud accounts. Instead of manually connecting code repositories upfront, you can begin identifying tech debt immediately using lifecycle-event signals from your cloud environment. The platform then provides an easy path to resolution with automatic generation of pull requests. We will walk through the account-first workflow and how it gets you from discovery to remediation faster with less setup.

sessions.title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
sessions.abstract: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

sessions.title: Fewer Incidents, Faster Fixes: Expert-led Cloud Operations on AWS
sessions.abstract: Automation can close tickets, but it takes human expertise to understand your business, anticipate what's coming, and make the judgment calls that keep your cloud resilient at scale. See how AWS combines deep human expertise with AI-powered capabilities to go beyond automated remediation. AWS cloud experts, armed with intelligent tooling and deep environmental context, proactively identify risks, guide architectural decisions, and help your team navigate complex challenges automation alone can't solve. Through real-world examples, see how this expert-led approach reduces incidents, accelerates resolution, and frees engineers to focus on innovation.

sessions.title: Financial data modeling with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: Designing business applications for low latency, high throughput, high consistency, and high availability presents unique challenges at scale. In this session, learn how to model business entities including accounts, journals, and ledgers using Amazon DynamoDB to support workflows that process millions of requests per second. Explore distributed computing patterns that leverage multi-Region replication features in DynamoDB. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
sessions.abstract: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.

sessions.title: Find failure modes faster: AI-powered resilience assessments
sessions.abstract:
Manual resilience reviews are slow, inconsistent, and routinely miss failure modes that don't surface until an incident occurs. In this workshop, you'll use the generative AI-driven assessment engine in AWS Resilience Hub to automatically discover dependencies across AWS services, internal endpoints, and third-party systems. You'll evaluate workloads against the Well-Architected Framework and your own defined resilience policies including availability SLOs, RTO, and RPO targets, then receive prioritized, actionable recommendations tied to business impact. Working with a reference architecture, you'll build a complete end-to-end assessment and leave with a repeatable framework you can run against any workload as your architecture evolves.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Find, prove, and fix code vulnerabilities at machine speed
sessions.abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. In this builders' session, close that gap end to end on a live application. You build a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is actually reachable, confirm exploitability through a sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generate a validated fix. You will see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. Leave able to move your team from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.

sessions.title: Find the waste hiding in your accelerator fleetÂ

Most platform owners can't tell which workload is using which device, whether it's working or idle, or what a stalled run is costing per hour. When something degrades, teams find out after a crash or a surprise bill.Â This lightning talk explores how to spot what's sitting idle, pinpoint a failing device without sacrificing the healthy ones around it, and prioritize fixes by how much spend you can recover.

sessions.title: Fine-Tune Agents That Reason: Multi-Turn RL on SageMaker AI
sessions.abstract: AI agents doing real work, like financial advising, coding, customer operations, reason across turns, call tools, and recover when steps fail mid-conversation. Prompting won't get you there; building multi-turn RL from scratch takes weeks. We'll whiteboard how SageMaker AI's managed MTRL connects your Strands, LangChain, or CrewAI agent under 10 lines of code - handling rollouts, trajectories, and checkpointing, auto-cataloged in SageMaker catalog. We'll cover reward design, rollouts in managed gym environments, decoupled training compute keeping GPUs from idling, and smaller specialized models outperforming larger ones at lower inference cost. Bring your agent use case for mapping the path.

sessions.title: Fine-tune and evaluate NVIDIA Open models on Amazon SageMaker
sessions.abstract: Learn how to customize NVIDIA Open models using Amazon SageMaker without managing training infrastructure. This session walks through preparing a dataset, fine-tuning the model, and evaluating the customized model against the base model to measure improvements in quality. Attendees will leave with a practical workflow for adapting NVIDIA's open models to domain-specific use cases on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: FinOps for AI: Cost allocation strategies for Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how spend maps to business outcomes. In this builders' session, you'll get hands on with the latest cost management capabilities for Amazon Bedrock. You'll tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control Gen AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. You'll then query new product metadata in CUR2 and visualize cost-per-million-token trends in CUDOS. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

sessions.title: FinOps for AI: Open the black box on AI spend (sponsored by Apptio)
sessions.abstract: AI spend often arrives as a black box: a rising bill with little clarity into which teams, models or features drove it. In this breakout, learn how Cloudability helps teams apply FinOps discipline to AI on AWS by categorizing costs, connecting spend to business goals and identifying waste. Discover how we turn that visibility into action for AI workloads running on Amazon EKS, improving GPU efficiency, Kubernetes workload right-sizing and application performance. Then apply the same cost discipline to Amazon Bedrock, including smarter provisioned throughput decisions, so teams can explain, defend and optimize AI spend. This presentation is brought to you by Apptio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: FinOps for AI: Scale Investments That Work. Stop Ones That Don't. (sponsored by Kion)
sessions.abstract:
Most organizations can tell you what they spend on AI. Fewer can tell you what they're getting for it.
FinOps for AI closes that gap, but it takes three things: visibility into spend by use case; controls that act on what the data tells you instead of just surfacing it; and value tracking that connects spend to outcomes your stakeholders can evaluate.
This session includes real examples of token attribution, guardrail patterns that respond to data, and a model for turning ROI signals into corrective action. This presentation is brought to you by Kion, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Firewall policy management for mixed regulated and legacy workloads
sessions.abstract: Your firewall policy now has to cover new workloads on modern tech stacks alongside legacy systems still running Windows. Some of them fall under financial regulations, and others under privacy controls. In this code talk, we show how new firewall management features help you write policy elements your team can understand and maintain, avoid policy sprawl, and spend less time preparing for audits.

sessions.title: First principles at LLM scale: Architecting Forge
sessions.abstract: When we set out to build Forge, Amazon's foundation model customization platform, we assumed the hardest problems would be ML problems. They weren't. They were classical problems Amazon's been solving for years, at a new scale. Same Well-Architected principles, evolved techniques. We will deep-dive into three workloads from the team behind Forge. First, serverless training of large language models on AWS. Second, enterprise-grade inference serving. Third, observability and evaluation tools optimizing toward smaller, performant models. Leave with lessons for your own AI platform.

sessions.title: Fix a Security Hub finding once with four layers of controls
sessions.abstract: You remediate a finding today and see the same class of finding next week. This chalk talk shows how to break that cycle. You take a real AWS Security Hub finding category and work through four control layers. An SCP stops the misconfiguration, an AWS CloudFormation Guard rule catches it before deployment, an AWS Config rule detects existing violations, and AI-generated auto-remediation corrects drift. Each finding you remediate this way becomes a rule that keeps it from coming back.

sessions.title: Fix Data Gaps Fast: Agentic Onboarding with Amazon Connect Decisions
sessions.abstract: 81% of enterprises report AI initiatives delayed or abandoned due to data and governance gaps — and 80–90% of new enterprise data is unstructured. The bottleneck isn't the model; it's the data. In this session, see how Amazon Connect Decisions uses agentic AI teammates to eliminate that gap. Watch a supply chain planner go from zero to a running demand forecast — connecting raw CSVs with no pre-cleaning, letting AI intelligently map and type-convert data, catching and fixing quality issues conversationally, and encoding tribal knowledge from a Word doc into live decision rules. No ETL code, no JIRA tickets, no months-long implementation. Onboarding in weeks, not months.

sessions.title: Fleet-wide AIOps for Amazon EKS with the AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Operating one EKS cluster is manageable. Operating a fleet of them is where the hard problems live: failures that surface far from their cause, VPC CNI IP exhaustion, Karpenter churn, and upgrades that stall across clusters. This chalk talk shows how AIOps and the AWS DevOps Agent bring order to operations at fleet scale. See how the DevOps Agent correlates signals across clusters to find root cause instead of chasing symptoms. Learn how it turns noisy telemetry into a diagnosis and a recommended fix. Discover the guardrails that let agents act on your fleet safely, with the blast radius bounded.

sessions.title: Follow that log from pipeline to intelligence
sessions.abstract: You've got logs flowing from everywhere, but when an issue spans multiple accounts or regions, you're stuck jumping between consoles trying to piece together what happened. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard the end-to-end path a log takes from ingestion pipeline to a unified data layer to log analytics. We'll break down where visibility gaps form and why. Learn how you can connect these layers to trace a problem across your entire environment without losing context.

sessions.title: Foundational architecture excellence: the operability trade-off
sessions.abstract: Elegant architectures that ignore operational reality become expensive liabilities. From hundreds of enterprise engagements, we expose the architectural decisions that silently create operational debt — decomposition without observability boundaries, blast-radius assumptions that fail under correlated load, and abstraction layers hiding the signals operators need. We unpack where good architecture and operable architecture diverge, which trade-offs are worth making early, and what questions your team should be asking before committing to a design. The best architecture is one you can actually run in production.

sessions.title: Foundational Model Ops with Amazon SageMaker AI and Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Build a fine-tuning pipeline that proves its own results. In this workshop, run the full loop, baseline eval, fine-tune, RL, re-eval, against the same bar every time. Start with a benchmark baseline on a Hugging Face model. Then fine-tune with QLoRA on Amazon SageMaker AI Training Jobs, with full control over your training script and compute. Add an RL pass with RLAIF or RLVR to optimize against a reward signal the benchmark alone can't score, and re-evaluate against that same baseline to see whether the gain is real or just a lower loss number. Put the whole sequence into a SageMaker Pipeline so it reruns on new data without manual rework. Bedrock Guardrails sit at the deployment gate.

sessions.title: Four agents, one answer: multi-agent synthesis on AWS
sessions.abstract: We live-build a multi-agent system where specialized agents — a document searcher, a data analyst, a claims verifier, and a synthesizer — collaborate to produce evidence-backed summaries from unstructured sources. Along the way we solve hard coordination problems: message routing, shared state, deadlock avoidance, and cost control. One presenter codes; the other narrates architecture decisions. Whether you synthesize research literature, member feedback, grant requirements, or compliance updates — leave with replicable patterns for your domain.

sessions.title: Four labs to shrink your Windows and SQL Server licensing bill
sessions.abstract: Lift-and-shift gets you to the cloud, but it doesn't solve the licensing costs that follow. In this builders' session, you'll work through four labs to reduce your Windows and SQL Server spend on Amazon EC2: (1) enable Compute Optimizer for continuous fleet right-sizing; (2) use Optimize CPU to align cores with compute requirements; (3) classify SQL Server HA clusters to remove passive-node licensing fees; and (4) downgrade SQL Server Enterprise to Standard edition. sessions.abstract: Cyber conflict has entered a new phase, accelerated by AI that increases the volume, velocity, and sophistication of attacks. The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we’ll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We’ll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. We’ll walk through how these patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and large-scale inference workloads from a single accelerator to 20,000. You’ll leave with reusable operational patterns for running AI workloads reliably at any scale.

sessions.abstract: The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team's time disappears. Amazon Quick changes that equation. Instead of one AI assistant doing one task, specialized agents each handle their piece and hand off to the next automatically. The human stays in the loop for judgment calls, not for data gathering and routing. Hear from a customer who moved from standalone AI use cases to compound, multi-agent workflows with Amazon Quick. Learn how they identified which workflows to orchestrate first, how they designed agent handoffs that satisfy compliance, and what it means now that the coordination layer runs autonomously.

sessions.title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
sessions.abstract: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

sessions.abstract: A confirmed exploit still needs a code fix, and that fix often takes days or weeks. The exploit path stays open the whole time. This session shows how Terra Security turns a validated pentest finding into a scoped virtual patch inside the application's existing AWS WAF: matched to the specific attack, not a site-wide block, activated by a human on your team, and checked against both the exploit and normal traffic before you trust it. You will leave with a clear picture of how the integration works and a model for closing the gap between proof and fix without breaking the app you are protecting. sessions.abstract: AWS has spent a decade proving the correctness of critical infrastructure, from IAM policy evaluation to cryptographic implementations and network isolation. This session traces the evolution from early automated reasoning tools to today's neurosymbolic AI, where formal verification and large language models converge. We examine how mathematical proof engines like Lean, combined with reinforcement learning and agentic workflows, enable provable security guarantees at scale. Attendees will learn how specification-driven development, whole-service data flow analysis, and Bedrock Guardrails' automated reasoning checks are moving the industry beyond "test and hope" toward mathematically verified trust.

sessions.title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
sessions.abstract: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.

sessions.title: Future-proof your keys: HSMs to AWS KMS in the post-quantum era
sessions.abstract: Cryptography is changing fast. The dedicated HSM you rely on today, whether AWS CloudHSM or an on-premises appliance, carries operational overhead that will only grow as the industry moves toward post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and stricter digital sovereignty requirements. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now covers most workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, with the same FIPS 140-3 Level 3 security, lower cost, and zero infrastructure management, while giving you a clear on-ramp to PQC and the sovereignty controls to keep your keys and data under your control. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through it together: we'll assess your workload, map signature and encryption migration paths, and show how moving to KMS puts you on the fastest path to post-quantum readiness. Meet the AWS Cryptography team and leave with a plan and concrete next steps.

Whether you're a 5-person nonprofit team or a 5,000-person enterprise, leave with deployable IaC for your own environment.

sessions.title: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
sessions.abstract: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves traders with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs adjacent to the matching engine with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency to the matching engine through Amazon VPC peering: bringing compute into New York Local Zone cuts round-trip latency by roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the AWS Region offers a fully managed API that also serves agentic trading systems via Model Context Protocol (MCP). Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever for your location-sensitive workloads.

sessions.title: GenAI chip selection: From training to inference
sessions.abstract: Every GenAI workload hits the same question: GPU, Trainium, Graviton, or Inferentia—and when do you use each? In this chalk talk, we walk through a practical decision tree covering model training, real-time inference, and agentic AI workloads. We then go deep on inference cost optimization: right-sizing GPU instances, offloading pre/post-processing to Graviton, using Spot for batch inference, prompt caching, and moving production inference to Inferentia2. Expect opinionated guidance, real customer math from teams that cut inference costs without sacrificing latency, and a whiteboard framework you can take back to your team on Monday.

Bring your toughest questions — we'll cover setup, agent workflows, and best practices for your environments.

sessions.title: Give your AI agents business context with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.abstract: An AI agent pointed at a data catalog that has schema but no meaning will guess — and in a regulated environment, guessing is a compliance liability. In this builders' session, learn how to turn the AWS Glue Data Catalog into a trust layer for AI agents. Enrich the catalog with business context — Skill Assets, golden queries, business glossary terms, ownership, and access restrictions — then connect an MCP-compatible AI agent and watch its answers shift from hallucination to governed, data-literate reasoning. Use semantic search to discover data by business meaning, add queryable metadata forms at scale, and leave with architecture patterns to roll this out across your existing catalog. You must bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Give Your Best Engineers Back to the Roadmap, Not the Pager (sponsored by NeuBird AI)
sessions.abstract: Forty percent of engineering time goes to firefighting instead of the roadmap you funded. The problem isn’t a lack of dashboards or headcount, it’s that these engineers are forced to act as the glue across these fragmented tools. Between incidents, an autonomous Production Ops Agent keeps working. It deepens its model of your environment, right sizes observability spend, and turns every incident into a captured fix nobody has to relearn. This session shows how NeuBird AI has helped teams recover 200 plus engineering hours a month and cut incident costs 60 percent or more, not by hiring more people or buying more dashboards, but by giving one agent the job of running production so your senior engineers can go back to building it. This presentation is brought to you by NeuBird AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Giving Your AI Agent a Wallet: The Architecture of Spend Control
sessions.abstract: AI agents can now hold a wallet and pay for APIs, data, and even other agents. The demo takes a few hours; making it safe to ship takes much longer. At the whiteboard, using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments, x402 micropayments, and Cedar policy, we design an agent that spends under a hard budget, then break it together. We work through where guardrails belong, why session limits aren't enough, custodial versus non-custodial tradeoffs, and human-in-the-loop without human-in-the-way. Bring your edge cases. You leave with a reference architecture and a checklist for bounded agent autonomy.

sessions.title: Global Technical Capability Lead Key & Certificate Services
sessions.abstract: Post-quantum migrations succeed when organizations can discover cryptographic assets, assign ownership, and continuously manage risk. Organisations are facing a rapid increase in machine identities, service identities, APIs, containers, AI workloads, and other cryptographic assets. At the same time, certificate lifetimes continue to shrink, making manual lifecycle management increasingly unsustainable. AWS and DXC Technology show how enterprise governance connects with crypto agility. See how DXC built a cryptographic asset intelligence and orchestration platform on AWS to discover and correlate assets across AWS and enterprise PKI, automate certificate lifecycles, and assess post-quantum readiness. A live proof of concept demonstrates inventory, prioritization, and continuous reassessment. Leave with an operating model aligned with NIST and CNSA 2.0 timelines.

sessions.abstract: Amazon Aurora DSQL is a serverless, distributed SQL database built for global scale. In this session, Marc Brooker, AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer, dives into the exact algorithms Aurora DSQL uses to achieve faster-than-light consistent reads, strong isolation, durability, and atomicity across regions. The session covers the specific tradeoffs each algorithm makes and what those tradeoffs mean in practice.

Use the AgentCore CLI to scaffold a Strands agent with a custom tool, test it locally against the Runtime contract, then deploy to AgentCore Runtime via CDK. Invoke the agent to demonstrate session isolation, inspect automatic CloudWatch logs and X-Ray traces, and confirm the framework-agnostic contract by replacing the agent with a plain Python function.

sessions.title: Go Hack Yourself. With AI. (sponsored by Horizon3.ai)
sessions.abstract: Defenders often drown in noise while attackers move at machine speed. To truly secure your environment, you must adopt an attacker’s perspective. Horizon3 CEO Snehal Antani shares insights from 250,000+ autonomous pentests across 6,000+ environments, demonstrating how AI hackers find exploitable paths that scanners miss, such as credential theft and domain compromise without CVEs. You’ll learn why vulnerable doesn’t mean exploitable, how to validate controls through a Hack-Fix-Verify loop, and where AI belongs in offense and defense: tool for scale and proof, not a black box. This presentation is brought to you by Horizon3.ai, an AWS Partner.
