sessions.title: Go headless: managed harness to custom DevOps orchestration
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents need production-grade orchestration, but should you own the loop or let AWS handle it? We build one on-call responder three ways: an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for a managed loop with built-in memory and tool routing, AgentCore Runtime for full control, and AWS DevOps Agent as a batteries-included DevOps harness. Then we build the shape most teams land in: your own orchestrator, DevOps Agent composed in headless over remote MCP and A2A. Bring your challenges and leave with patterns for building composable, robust pipelines that automate complex DevOps workflows end-to-end.

sessions.title: Golden Opportunities: Unlocking Business Value with Agentic AI (sponsored by Atos)
sessions.abstract:
Companies have shifted from talking about agents to putting them to work, but moving from an AWS Bedrock AgentCore demo to a governed, production multi-agent system inside a regulated enterprise isn't a straight line. Atos will show what that path looks like, where it breaks, and how to fix it.
What you'll learn
⮚Enterprise patterns that separate successful AWS agentic AI deployments from stalled pilots
⮚Building a governance layer on Amazon Bedrock that regulated industries will approve
⮚How GSI partners turn ideas into completed, production-ready deployments
⮚Where AWS tooling is mature, where it's still evolving, and how to architect around the gaps This presentation is brought to you by Atos, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Go-Live to ROI: How Partners Turn Customer Outcomes into Revenue
sessions.abstract: The partners thriving in the AI era aren't the ones who just deploy, they're the ones who prove impact. The Business Value Realization (BVR) motion is how consulting and managed services partners are building their next growth engine: documenting outcomes, unlocking milestone-based funding, and turning deployments into expansion revenue. Explore how BVR helps partners quantify ROI, earn a new Competency, build customer success practices that drive revenue beyond go-live, and where the motion is heading next. As AI moves from pilot to production, the partners who own the value conversation won't just retain customers, they'll shape what is built next.

sessions.abstract: How do you secure that which has no network? AWS services such as S3, SQS, and DynamoDB help teams build and scale faster but come with a different set of security implications than services that live in your VPC. In this session, you'll learn about best practices and architectural patterns for building secure networks on AWS using network features like DNS firewall, and Network firewall and layering them with AWS IAM policies like VPC endpoint policy, and Resource Control Policy to help ensure that your resources that live outside of your network behave like they are in your network.

sessions.abstract: Participants build and command autonomous drone fleets to identify rogue devices using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS IoT Greengrass, and Strands Agents. This gamified scenario showcases a Human-Machine Teaming architecture in which AI operates autonomously within defined trust boundaries, with human-in-the-loop escalation at configurable confidence thresholds.

sessions.title: Governance across engines with AWS Glue Data Catalog
sessions.abstract: Your data lives in a catalog but is queried from many engines. How do you enforce consistent access policies without duplicating rules everywhere? In this chalk talk, we explore how AWS Glue Data Catalog centralizes governance so that permissions defined once are enforced uniformly. We'll work through patterns for column and row-level security, tag-based policies, cross-account sharing with least-privilege grants, and how to audit who accessed what. Bring your multi-engine governance challenges.

sessions.title: Governance foundations for AI workloads that grow into autonomous agents
sessions.abstract: Agentic workloads are reaching production, and governance has to keep up without slowing teams down. This session shows how to build a governance foundation for AI with AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, AWS Organizations, and automatic evidence collection, then extend it to autonomous agents. You apply preventive and detective controls to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, automate compliance evidence, and map controls to frameworks such as ISO 42001. The same controls hold whether the workload is a single model call or a fleet of agents acting on their own.

sessions.title: Govern and optimize AI agents for desktop work on WorkSpaces
sessions.abstract: Your most valuable business processes often run inside desktop applications and mainframes that expose no APIs for AI agents to call. In this session, learn how to use Amazon WorkSpaces to give agents a governed desktop where they operate these applications directly, just as an employee would. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into scoping what agents are permitted to do, auditing agent actions, and configuring agent identity. We'll walk through strategies for agent optimization:  how to choose the right agent tools, select the right model for your workflow, and build reusable agent skills. Applied together, these techniques cut task time, lower cost, and increase the accuracy of your agent workflows.

sessions.title: Govern, Bill, and Attribute: The Unit Economics of Production Agents
sessions.abstract: Your agent demo costs $0.02 a call; in production it's $4. Can you still price it profitably, and can you capture the full AWS consumption it drives downstream? This chalk talk walks the complete unit economics of a production agent: right-sizing cost with prompt caching, model routing, and tool-call minimization; pricing through consumption versus outcome-based billing; and attributing the full impact through AWS Marketplace metering and PRM, so it converts into AWS investment back to you. Real examples like bid optimization, content moderation, and shopping advisors ground each step.

In this session, learn how to ground your AI agents in trusted metadata using AWS Glue Data Catalog. See how to flow business context like glossary terms, descriptions, and quality scores into agent workflows so they generate accurate, schema-aware queries instead of guessing. sessions.abstract: Join us in working through the ModelOps lifecycle, starting with experiment, train, register, approve, to deploy, anchored by the Amazon SageMaker catalog system of record. Using SageMaker managed MLflow and the catalog within SageMaker AI Studio, you'll build governance in as you go with no end-of-cycle compliance scramble. Training runs auto-catalog with model cards, lineage, and audit trails; you'll discover assets with semantic search, trace lineage with OpenLineage, configure access control, gate promotion on quality and compliance, and publish models across accounts. You'll leave able to trace any endpoint to its dataset, experiment, and approval in seconds.

sessions.title: Governing AI assets at scale with MCP Gateway and Registry
sessions.abstract: As enterprises onboard AI assets (MCP servers, Agents, Skills) they face a governance problem: no unified way to discover, authenticate, or observe them. MCP Gateway and Registry is an open source control plane with centralized registration, OAuth2 auth, semantic tool discovery, and end-to-end telemetry. Walk through the project's architecture, pluggable auth and storage backends, and deployment patterns on Amazon EKS. An AI/ML platform VP shares their production rollout, governance patterns that scaled across business units, and lessons learned contributing back upstream.

sessions.title: Governing autonomous AI agents across cloud boundaries
sessions.abstract: When autonomous agents coordinate across cloud boundaries, who enforces the rules — and how do you revoke access instantly when one goes rogue? In this chalk talk, we whiteboard governed multi-agent coordination: Cedar as a portable policy engine across AWS, Azure, and GCP, A2A protocol for cross-cloud agent communication, and a kill switch for instant revocation. The audience picks the scenario — flight delays, trade failures, or healthcare cancellations — and we draw how policy, identity, and coordination work at each boundary crossing.

sessions.title: Governing hundreds of accounts in seconds: agentic AI meets Landing Zone operations
sessions.abstract: When you manage hundreds of AWS accounts, governance can fall behind. Drift accumulates, controls take days to propagate, and problems go undetected until something breaks. We demonstrate Landing Zone Accelerator 2.0 with built-in AI that lets operators use natural language to apply organizational changes in minutes, if not seconds. We deploy org-wide security controls, provision accounts, and enforce encryption through a Bedrock-powered interface supporting CloudFormation and Terraform. An AI agent generates each change plan, and before anything is applied, an org-wide preview catches conflicts and policy violations. Issues are surfaced up front instead of discovered after a break. Attendees learn how we built LZA 2.0 with Kiro spec-driven development and Rust, and how to design pre-deployment previews that keep multi-account operations safe.

sessions.title: Govern your context layer for AI agents with AWS Context
sessions.abstract: Learn how to carry your existing data permissions into a governed context layer your AI agents need to work accurately across structured and unstructured data. AWS Context assembles semantic data from your catalogs, glossaries, query logs, and access patterns into one governed context layer, honoring the governance contract placed on your data assets. Each user's identity flows through the agent so every answer is scoped to what they are authorized to see. We will whiteboard and interact on how identity propagates, how retrieval is filtered, and where permissions break.

sessions.title: GPU cluster failure patterns on AWS: observe, diagnose, recover
sessions.abstract: At scale, GPU clusters fail in ways single-node debugging never taught you: NCCL timeouts that are actually storage problems, DataLoader forks that silently hang collectives, and GPUs that pass every health check yet corrupt your results. In this hands-on builders session, you diagnose these failures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter. Read NCCL debug logs, interpret all-reduce bus bandwidth against per-instance baselines, and run open-source health checks that catch faults before your jobs do. You leave with a failure-signature runbook and a triage method distilled from operating large GPU fleets on AWS.

sessions.title: GPU orchestration using NVIDIA Run:ai across the edge
sessions.abstract: AWS and NVIDIA have collaborated for over a decade to deliver GPU-accelerated solutions across the cloud and edge, yet Kubernetes still treats GPUs as opaque, unshareable integers. In this Level 400 code talk, learn how to deploy NVIDIA Run:ai on Amazon EKS and execute a complete model lifecycle on shared GPU infrastructure. Using Terraform, provision EKS clusters on Amazon EC2 instances with NVIDIA L4 GPUs, install the Run:ai control plane and cluster agents, and configure project-scoped GPU quotas with priority-based sharing. Then see how Run:ai orchestrates a QLoRA fine-tuning job on Qwen3-14B and serves the resulting adapter with vLLM so you can compare base model responses against your fine-tuned model in real time.

sessions.title: Graviton5 for data workloads
sessions.abstract: Data workloads are bottlenecked by how fast they can access and process information — whether that data lives on local storage, in memory, or behind a lightweight service. New Graviton5 instance families are purpose-built for each tier.

sessions.title: Graviton5: Migrate your workloads, cut costs, get better performance
sessions.abstract: AWS Graviton5 delivers up to 25% better compute performance than the previous generation, features caches up to five times larger, and offers some of the fastest memory performance available in the cloud. But what do those improvements actually mean for your workloads? In this session, we go beyond the spec sheet into real-world benchmarks across databases, web applications, and ML inference. Hear from a customer who migrated production workloads across multiple Graviton generations and the compounding performance and cost gains they achieved. Walk away with concrete performance data and a practical framework to evaluate Graviton5 for your own migration.

sessions.title: Graviton. Serverless. Apache Iceberg. Your guide to a modern data warehouse strategy
sessions.abstract: You need your data warehouse to be fast, open, and accessible to everyone on your team. This session shows you how to get there with Amazon Redshift. Take advantage of Graviton-powered RG instances for faster analytics at lower cost. Eliminate the complexity of managing infrastructure with Redshift Serverless. Query open data formats directly in your data lake with native Apache Iceberg support. And put insights in the hands of every team with natural language access. You'll also learn how multi-warehouse architectures let teams scale independently without duplicating data. Leave with a clear architecture strategy you can apply to your environment.

sessions.title: Grounding LLMs in Truth: Build a Live Fact-Checking Pipeline
sessions.abstract: Walk through the reference architecture of a real-time fact-checking pipeline built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See how a live audio stream is turned into fact-by-fact verdicts (true, misleading, or false), with source citing at broadcast-compatible latency. Learn how to build it yourself using a chain of specialized agents on AgentCore, hybrid search on Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and custom tool-use hooks. Leave with a mapped path to create a reference architecture, plus answers to the concrete design questions blocking you such as: agent sharding, tabular corpus indexing, guardrails, and streaming reasoning to the UI.

sessions.title: Ground your agents with AWS Context and Amazon SageMaker
sessions.abstract: Agents are only as good as the context they're given. In this session, see how AWS Context makes the agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker more accurate and useful by grounding agents in business metadata. We'll show how context-aware agents like SageMaker Data Agent break complex requests into structured, multi-step plans, generate validated SQL, Python, and PySpark against your real data, and keep humans in the loop with built-in checkpoints. You'll learn practical techniques to feed the right context to your agents, connect additional sources, and turn a capable assistant into one that truly understands your environment.

sessions.title: Grow Adoption Where Customers Work with AWS Bedrock and Quick
sessions.abstract: Your customers increasingly live inside an AI work surface, and your product needs to be there too. In this hands-on session, you'll take a SaaS product—its API and a simple agentic capability—and bring it into Amazon Quick using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll adapt it for AgentCore, wire up secure identity, then build Chat Agents, Research, Flows, and Apps that put your product's intelligence in front of users. Customers get your whole product in Quick, as-is. Walk out with a working reference pattern and the ability to spin up POCs for product leadership.

sessions.title: Growing role of CPUs in AI: Inference and agents AI on EC2
sessions.abstract: CPUs play a critical and growing role in production AI systems. This session explores two CPU-intensive AI patterns on EC2. First, AI inference: serving language model predictions at scale using Graviton and x86 instances, with real-world cost and latency tradeoffs. Second, agentic AI: running sandboxed environments where autonomous agents compile code, execute tools, and interact with external systems, requiring fast, isolated, ephemeral compute. We share production architectures, performance benchmarks across instance families, and practical guidance on matching your AI workload to the right EC2 CPU. Walk away with a decision framework for running AI beyond GPUs.

sessions.title: Guardrails for AI-generated Serverless infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Coding agents generate full serverless architectures in seconds, but without guardrails they produce over-permissioned IAM policies, skip encryption at rest, and deploy resources that violate your organization's tagging and cost policies. In this chalk talk, discuss operational controls for AI-generated infrastructure: automated security reviews that catch policy violations before deployment, cost estimation gates that flag unexpected spend, compliance checks against organizational standards, and MCP server configurations that enforce service boundaries and naming conventions. We whiteboard which guardrails to automate versus which require human review, and where teams are getting the balance wrong.

sessions.title: Guide to deploying landing zones & modernized networks in hours
sessions.abstract: Reimagine what migration looks like when landing zone setup and network translation go from weeks to hours. In this chalk talk, we show how AWS Transform's agentic AI compresses that timeline, from migration inventory to fully deployed, validated landing zones and modernized networks. See how production-ready account structures deploy through Control Tower with guardrails in place, and how firewall configurations become optimized VPCs, subnets, and security groups. Bring your questions and hear from the experts building these capabilities.

Discover the customizations that Amazon RDS enables for HA and DR while also allowing you to bring your own license (BYOL) for SQL Server. Also learn how globally resilient solutions architected with Amazon RDS minimize downtime and meet stringent business continuity requirements for mission-critical workloads.

sessions.title: Hands-on distributed training with AWS Trainium and PyTorch
sessions.abstract: Get hands-on with AWS Trainium and PyTorch's TorchTitan to train models using a fully native PyTorch workflow. This workshop walks you through distributed training on Trainium—covering cluster setup, parallelism strategies, and performance optimization—all through familiar PyTorch APIs. Whether you're training LLMs or fine-tuning domain models, you'll learn how Trainium and TorchTitan simplify scaling without sacrificing native PyTorch flexibility. Leave with the skills to scale model training on Trainium without changing your PyTorch workflow.

sessions.title: Hands-on: Harden your AI agents with Nitro Confidential Computing
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI systems autonomously orchestrate tools, integrate third-party components, and make decisions, introducing risks from compromised dependencies and agents deviating from intended behavior. Protecting prompts, agent memory, retrieval context, and model weights requires strong isolation and verifiable trust. In this workshop, you will build agentic AI apps, identify threats from untrusted supply chains and uncontrolled autonomy, and mitigate them using AWS Confidential Computing on EC2 with cryptographic attestation, isolated execution, open weight models, and Amazon Bedrock.

sessions.title: Hands-on training world models and deploying agents for Physical AI
sessions.abstract: Physical AI is transforming robotics and autonomous systems with world models that enable agents to understand and interact with their environments. AWS Trainium and the AWS Neuron simplify this with PyTorch integration — apply standard distributed training techniques using familiar APIs while the software stack handles multi-device coordination, compilation, and optimization. sessions.title: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
sessions.abstract:
Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose.

Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.

In this session, learn how to build production agents by writing SOPs in natural language. We'll cover how to write SOPs that let agents exercise judgment while embedding guardrails. A single SOP becomes a deployable agent, and this pattern scales across different business processes. Using Kiro's spec-driven development and Strands agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, partners own the full agent lifecycle and differentiate by layering domain expertise and industry-specific IP into SOPs. Walk away with hands-on experience building the agentic architecture that enables autonomous enterprise operations for your customers.

sessions.abstract: Orchestrating AI conversations across channels requires more than just connecting APIs. Learn how to build agents that understand context, respond instantly, and adapt to channel constraints. Explore Twilio Agent Connect and Amazon Bedrock integration patterns, plus the operational playbook for deploying engagement AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Twilio, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: How to decompose Oracle and SQL Server into purpose-built databases
sessions.abstract: A monolithic traditional RDBMS databases serves transactions, reporting, and search, but serves none of them well. In this chalk talk, we'll whiteboard how to decompose a proprietary database into purpose-built layers on AWS, including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for transactional workloads, Aurora pgvector for semantic search and GenAI (RAG), and Amazon Redshift via zero-ETL for real-time analytics, for a smarter modernization approach. We'll walk through how this pattern eliminates licensing costs, removes ETL pipelines, and turns your operational data into an AI-ready platform. Come ready to whiteboard your decomposition use case.

sessions.abstract: Providers lose hours daily to documentation, manual coding, and admin work. Leading health IT builders are solving this with purpose-built AI on AWS. In this chalk talk, Innovaccer joins AWS to share how they trained task-specific clinical small language models that deliver consistent outputs where general-purpose LLMs produce unacceptable variance. We use their architecture as a jumping-off point to discuss the full spectrum of paths to production: custom model training on accelerated compute, multi-step agentic workflow orchestration, and embedding fully managed clinical AI capabilities into existing applications.

sessions.title: How to Govern an agent fleet: auto-approve the routine, escalate the ambiguous
sessions.abstract: Your teams are building agents faster than anyone can review them by hand, and that creates operational and security risk along with the visibility problem. In this workshop, you build a layered controls stack for an agent fleet. You enforce content and business-logic boundaries with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, apply an evaluator pattern for policy validation, and track compliance posture with AWS Config conformance packs. Then you connect these into an operating model that approves routine actions automatically and sends only the ambiguous ones to a person, so you can deploy more agents than your team could review individually.

sessions.title: How to improve your security and governance maturity and prove it to your auditor
sessions.abstract: With so many security best practices available, knowing what to do first is a challenge. In this session, you learn how to use the AWS Security Maturity Model to systematically identify and prioritize security improvements for your AWS workloads through a phased approach. You discover how to extend your governance capabilities to manage security consistently across multi-cloud environments. Finally, you see how automatic evidence collection helps you continuously demonstrate compliance to auditors, turning security posture into provable assurance.

Join this session to learn how Grok Bot is an orchestration layer for technical knowledge work, coordinating workflows while saving time and mitigating costs. Through live demos, see Grok Bot operate from its own VM and browser, maintain authenticated tool access, monitor usage, and provision cloud agents on demand. We’ll be joined by a customer in production as well as SpaceXAI engineers as they share the workflows they run today. This presentation is brought to you by Cursor, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: How to solve for multicloud identity lifecycle management
sessions.abstract: Organizations operating in multiple clouds face a compounding multi-cloud identity lifecycle governance challenge. How do you provision, manage, audit, and decommission identities when each cloud provider enforces different authorization models, attribute schemas, and lifecycle hooks? In this session, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), a federal research organization, describes how it uses a centralized identity governance platform to provision identities and entitlements across AWS and Microsoft Azure. You will learn how to avoid governance divergence and design identity lifecycles where access reviews, birthright provisioning, and decommissioning work consistently, regardless of which cloud the identity lands in.

sessions.title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
sessions.abstract: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.

sessions.title: How to use AI to develop and deploy controls from your internal policies
sessions.abstract: You maintain internal security policies but turning them into implemented, risk-prioritized controls could be manual and slow. This lightning talk demonstrates how to use Kiro to develop and deploy controls at scale across three layers. Preventive controls that block non-compliant actions, detective controls that identify violations and trigger remediation, and proactive controls that validate configurations before deployment. You leave with a practical approach to using AI to accelerate the entire control lifecycle from policy to enforcement.

sessions.title: How Trainium powers the next AI frontier, from silicon to application
sessions.abstract: Every AI breakthrough demands innovation across the full stack: chips, servers, software, and the models built on top, each layer making the next one faster and cheaper to run. In this session, discover how AWS and frontier AI builders drive full-stack innovation on AWS Trainium to scale post-training and reinforcement learning, serve at high throughput, and bend the cost-per-token curve. Examine real architectural decisions from silicon to application, then look ahead to what's next in Trainium and AWS infrastructure. You will see how each layer of innovation compounds and learn where to place your bets on AI infrastructure.

sessions.title: How Vanguard Scales AI Oversight Without Scaling Human Review (sponsored by Capgemini)
sessions.abstract: Human review can't scale linearly with generative-AI volume. Vanguard's AI Center of Excellence built a closed-loop oversight system where every AI response is scored by an LLM-as-judge, confirmed or overturned by a subject-matter expert, and routed through a confusion matrix: confirmed catches sharpen the agent, disagreements calibrate the judge. Each SME label grows a benchmark that resets how much oversight the next cycle needs, proving mathematically that coverage can fall while risk holds flat. Built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda-hosted detector SLMs, SQS, DynamoDB, and SageMaker, the loop moves toward real-time interruption of harmful responses before customers see them. This presentation is brought to you by Capgemini, an AWS Partner.

Learn how WBD and AWS are replacing decades of manual process with self-improving agents that drive precision, yield, and entirely new monetization models at scale.

You will see how this open standard based approach lets AI agents reason over trusted enterprise data in place, with governance and business context preserved.

sessions.title: Human search to agent retrieval: Rearchitecting with OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: Agents don't search like humans. They fire hundreds of sub-queries per task, maintain stateful memory across sessions, and demand, verified answers before taking action. Traditional search architectures weren't built for this, and at agent scale, latency budgets compress, relevance requirements compound, and retrieval failures cascade into hallucinated outputs. In this session, we walk you through how the shift from human search to agent retrieval is reshaping infrastructure requirements and how the latest capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service help you address these unique challenges. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, why it matters, and how to get started.

sessions.title: Implement AI agent safety controls with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Scaling AI agents into production without safety controls creates compliance, cost, and operational risk for financial services organizations. In this workshop, build an agent safety control system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Starting with a deployed agent, configure three signal pipelines: observability via Amazon AgentCore Observability and Amazon CloudWatch; cost monitoring with AWS Budgets; and Amazon AgentCore Runtime Evaluation for behavioral deviation detection. Then build an admin control panel that aggregates alerts and enables human-in-the-loop interventions including session termination and fine-grained authorization via Cedar policies. Leave with a proven approach you can replicate to deliver responsible, governed AI agents at scale.

sessions.title: Implement semantic caching for AI agents using ElastiCache for Valkey
sessions.abstract: Semantic caching uses vector similarity search to retrieve cached LLM responses for semantically equivalent queries, reducing inference latency and cost in agentic AI architectures. In this session, dive deep into implementing semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, covering embedding generation, similarity scoring, and relevance threshold tuning. Explore advanced production patterns including per-user cache namespacing for personalized responses, tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant data leakage, and techniques for validating that cached responses remain contextually appropriate for incoming queries at scale. sessions.title: In-Country HPC: How TGS Processes Seismic Data on AWS Brazil
sessions.abstract: TGS -- one of the world's largest multi-client geoscience data providers -- faced a significant cost challenge running its business-critical Rackmon EFWI GPU workload at scale. By strategically deploying this workload on AWS infrastructure in Brazil, TGS leveraged Brazil's ReData Special Tax Regime to dramatically reduce the tax burden on GPU-intensive seismic processing. The result: material cost savings on one of the most computationally demanding workloads in the energy industry -- and a reusable in-country processing architecture that can serve future customers with data residency requirements in other geographies.

Every pattern discussed is one you can adopt today.

sessions.title: Inside Amazon S3: How a one-page design reached planetary scale
sessions.abstract: When Amazon S3 launched in 2006, its design requirements fit one page: scalable, reliable, fast, inexpensive, simple, with no single points of failure. The system was built to treat component failure as normal and use scale as an advantage. Today those founding principles describe an architecture serving hundreds of millions of requests per second across tens of millions of drives, maintaining eleven nines of durability while shipping features without downtime. Hear S3 principal engineers trace the decisions from single host to strong consistency at global scale, how formal methods verify correctness, and how the team balances innovation with operational safety.

sessions.title: Inside Amazon S3 Vectors: architecture and cost optimization for vector search
sessions.abstract: Vector embeddings power everything from semantic search to RAG, but running them at scale often means high infrastructure costs and operational overhead. In this session, go inside the architecture of Amazon S3 Vectors to see how it delivers vector search at up to 90% lower cost than specialized alternatives, with support for up to 2 billion vectors per index. We'll whiteboard the indexing approach that makes this possible, then explore recent enhancements, including a 100x increase in the per-query search result limit and reduced query pricing, and what they mean for your application's performance and cost.

sessions.title: Inside AWS Trainium3: Hardware innovations for better AI economics
sessions.abstract: What does it take to build a chip purpose-made for AI? In this deep dive, we explore Trainium3 architecture innovations: NeuronCore innovations that delivers higher TFLOPs, hardware-accelerated quantization, softmax acceleration, near-memory compute and Mixture-of-Experts optimizations. We'll share micro-benchmark data showing how these choices translate to real performance for Mixture-of-Experts and other demanding workloads. At the system level, we examine the Trn3 UltraServer family, scaling from 32 to 144 chips via NeuronLink fabric to enables up to 4.4x more performance. Leave with a deep understanding of how to evaluate and leverage purpose-built AI Chips for your AI workloads.

sessions.title: Inside Bayer’s AI agent: Interpretability as governance (sponsored by Thoughtworks)
sessions.abstract: Enterprise AI governance has focused on controls around agents—identity, permissions, sandboxing, and audit trails. But what happens inside the model? This session explores a live production system: Bayer’s PRINCE research assistant, built with Thoughtworks on AWS to give researchers access to 18,000+ preclinical study reports. We’ll share how Thoughtworks’ AI Research Labs applies mechanistic interpretability research, published at ICML, NeurIPS, and AAAI, to understand why the assistant answers, cites, or refuses queries. See how sparse autoencoders identify internal circuits behind refusal, how targeted steering changes behavior without retraining, and why this matters in regulated environments. Leave with a practical framework for making interpretability a core component of AI governance. This presentation is brought to you by Thoughtworks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
sessions.abstract: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose built AI chips to deliver better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference, and leave equipped to write custom, hardware-optimized kernels.

sessions.title: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly)
sessions.abstract: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders, partners, and teams putting agents into production go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join us for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Inside the Agentic Engineering Org of the Future (sponsored by Harness)
sessions.abstract: What does it actually take to become an AI-native engineering organization? A senior technology executive from a Fortune 500 enterprise sits down with Harness Field CTO Nick Durkin to talk through what it's really taken to go all in on agentic software delivery, orchestrating agents across the entire SDLC instead of one-off automations. They'll get into what that transformation actually looks like end to end, how they decide when an agent runs on its own versus when a human stays in the loop, how agentic engineering has affected cloud migration and consumption, and what it takes to do this at the scale of a Fortune 500 engineering org. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Inside the Architecture: Building Secure AI Applications on AWS (sponsored by TrendAI™)
sessions.abstract: AI is rapidly moving from experimentation to production, creating new challenges for developers, architects, and security teams. In this technical session, explore the real-world architectures enterprises use to build and secure AI applications on AWS. Learn how organizations leverage Amazon Bedrock, EKS, ECS, Security Lake, CloudTrail, and cloud-native automation to protect AI workloads, monitor risk across multi-account environments, and streamline security operations. Through practical deployment patterns and lessons learned from large-scale AWS environments, discover how to build AI applications that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. The session draws on deployment patterns described for TrendAI Vision One on AWS, including AI workload protection, cloud telemetry integration, and AWS-native architecture approaches. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees)
sessions.abstract: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true. This presentation is brought to you by CloudBees, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Inside T-Mobile's Kinetic Edge: Real-Time Physical AI at Scale
sessions.abstract: In a Physical AI world, tokens traveling across a telecom network must trigger real-world actions with sub-millisecond latency. Learn how T-Mobile built its Kinetic Edge Platform using AWS Outposts, Amazon SageMaker, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, delivering deterministic performance, ultra-low latency, and precise synchronization on a network serving 130M+ customers. We'll cover how to assess Physical AI network requirements and map them to AWS infrastructure options. You'll leave knowing how to build AI into the network edge and where it creates the most value.

Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.

Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

sessions.title: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS)
sessions.abstract: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Introducing AWS Context: Build governed intelligence for agents at scale
sessions.abstract: AI agents need to understand what your data means, how it connects, and which definitions and rules apply to each use case. AWS Context automatically builds a governed knowledge graph by unifying structured and unstructured data, managed knowledge bases, and technical and business metadata from AWS and third-party sources. This shared foundation grounds agents in your organization’s data, business rules, relationships, and domain knowledge. In this session, dive into the reference architecture and learn best practices for integrating agents with AWS Context, including considerations for identity management, workload sizing, and production deployments.

sessions.title: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
sessions.abstract: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.

sessions.title: Investigate Incidents Across Teams with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Production incidents typically involve multiple teams, but tooling and investigations are often siloed. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS DevOps Agent meets teams where incident response already happens. See how engineers can interact with the agent directly from tools like Slack, consolidating investigation activity, findings, and recommended actions alongside team communication. Bring your multi-team incident patterns and discuss approaches to faster, more connected incident response across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments.

sessions.title: Investigating Threats to AI: Incident Response to Compromised AI Workloads
sessions.abstract: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

sessions.title: It's live. Now what? Operating AI on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Your AI workload is live, and now you own it: latency creeping up, costs outgrowing usage, and no line from spend to teams. Start with the metrics that matter on Amazon Bedrock: time to first token, latency, throttles, and cache tokens. Then learn why latency alone cannot tell you what broke, and how output tokens per second separates a slower model from a longer answer. Also learn why throttling starts before you reach your quota. Finally, attribute token spend to teams using request metadata and caller identity. Leave with an instrumentation checklist and the alarms worth paging on.

sessions.title: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
sessions.abstract: There are now three ways to migrate Java from x86 to Graviton. AWS Transform Custom runs at scale across hundreds of repos with managed CI/CD and validation. The open-source Java skill runs locally in any agentic IDE, no AWS credentials needed. The Arm MCP server (in Kiro) goes broader, covering non-Java languages and general x86-to-Arm patterns. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and migration timeline. We demo all three on the same codebase, show where each succeeds and where it hands off, and give you a decision framework so you pick the right tool before you start.

sessions.title: Journey to post-quantum (PQ) authentication in AWS
sessions.abstract: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

sessions.title: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost (sponsored by Cloudera)
sessions.abstract: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow.  Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.

Nightshift draws on native Prometheus and PromQL metrics in Elastic. Kubernetes logs, out-of-the-box EKS dashboards and workflows, and ES|QL subqueries that correlate metrics with logs and traces in a single investigation. We'll also show how the 30x faster columnar metrics engine and full telemetry retention give Nightshift the complete context it needs to work like your best engineer This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu)
sessions.abstract: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud

sessions.title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
sessions.abstract: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously — reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that don’t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.

sessions.title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3

See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.

sessions.title: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
sessions.abstract: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.

sessions.title: Lambda Managed Instances: Always-on Serverless Compute
sessions.abstract: Some Lambda workloads run constantly. For steady-state, high-throughput functions, per-invocation pricing becomes more expensive than running the same code on EC2, but you don't want to manage instances. Lambda Managed Instances give you EC2 economics with multi-concurrency while Lambda handles instance lifecycle, patching, and scaling. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the decision: when Managed Instances beat standard Lambda pricing, what workloads migrate cleanly versus what needs adaptation, and how to model your break-even point. Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

With Lambda Managed Instances, you can optimize the performance and cost efficiency of your functions by utilizing specialized EC2 instance types and EC2 pricing benefits, while maintaining the familiar Serverless programming model and benefits like automatic patching, scaling, and 200+ AWS services integration for event-driven workloads. This session will provide an in-depth overview of how to get started with Lambda Managed Instances, recent launches like 90-minute function timeout, enhanced observability, and a behind-the-scenes look at how Lambda manages and scales your instances to ensure a seamless serverless experience.

sessions.title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
sessions.abstract: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

sessions.abstract: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

sessions.title: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
sessions.abstract: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.

sessions.title: Lambda performance tuning and cost optimization
sessions.abstract: Most Lambda functions run at default memory settings, which means you're paying more for slower execution. Right-sizing memory often reduces cost and latency at the same time. In this chalk talk, we go beyond memory tuning: cold start elimination with SnapStart and provisioned concurrency, architecture-level savings like batching and right-sizing event source mappings, and when Lambda Managed Instances deliver better economics than per-invocation pricing. We whiteboard the decision points using real cost data and discuss which CloudWatch and Cost Explorer metrics actually drive optimization decisions.

sessions.title: Land migrated workloads with controls already in place
sessions.abstract: Most migrations add governance controls after workloads land on AWS, and that creates rework. This chalk talk shows how to build guardrails into your AWS Transform migration workflow with AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, AWS Config, and AWS Security Hub so workloads arrive with controls in place. Bring your migration challenges, and we design a secure-by-default landing together that carries governance through each phase of the migration.

sessions.title: Large-scale VMware exit: engineering a 10,000+ server migration wave engine
sessions.abstract: Organizations facing VMware licensing pressure need more than a migration plan. They need a structured exit strategy spanning assessment, mobilization, migration, and modernization. In this session, we discuss how AWS Transform drives business outcomes at each phase: portfolio assessment that quantifies TCO reduction, wave planning that protects application uptime, automated cutover orchestration that eliminates risk, and post-migration modernization that captures cloud-native savings. Drawing from real-world examples, we explore how teams compressed 18-month timelines into ten or lower using AWS Transform and agentic capabilities for migrating compute, database and storage resources, then open the discussion to address your specific use cases.

sessions.title: Latest trends: Network/EBS intensive workloads on Amazon EC2 instances
sessions.abstract: EC2 network 'n' and EBS-optimized 'b' instances deliver the highest, most consistent network and EBS performance in the cloud. Join us for a tour of the latest Graviton and Intel instance types in these families, plus the networking and EBS technologies that unlock peak performance for your workloads. Learn how customers leverage these instances for new workloads associated with AI/ML training and inference, and traditional network-intensive workloads such as security & network virtual appliances, and EBS-intensive workloads such as SQL, NoSQL, and in-memory databases.

We'll discuss real-world patterns customers use to move from reactive security posture to proactive guardrails — covering both EKS Auto Mode and self-managed configurations. You'll leave with actionable strategies you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Learn faster: Experimentation in an AI world
sessions.abstract: AI makes it possible to generate and test far more product variations than a team could create by hand. But running more experiments only helps if you can release each variation safely, measure the right signals, and separate meaningful results from noise. In this code-focused session, you’ll learn how to use AI and feature flags to control experiment variants, target audiences, adjust exposure, and shut down underperforming tests without redeploying. We’ll also examine how Amazon has recently used AI in experiments on Amazon.com to create variations and extract better signals from the results.

sessions.title: Lessons from Netflix's distributed PostgreSQL migration to Aurora
sessions.abstract: In this session, explore the migration playbook and lessons learned from moving some of Netflix's largest workloads from a self-managed, distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database on Amazon EC2 to Aurora. Discover how PostgreSQL compatibility minimized code changes while the shared storage architecture of Aurora eliminated cross-node coordination overhead, delivering up to 75% lower, more predictable latency and up to 28% cost savings. Learn about workload selection and sequencing, near-zero downtime cutovers with data consistency validation and rollback planning, and post-migration operational lessons including vacuum debt, connection management, and query plan stability.

sessions.title: Lessons in Scale and Innovation Through the Deployment of AI Agents
sessions.abstract: AI agents on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at velocity and scale. Discover how Amazon Finance Operations, supporting 6,000+ analysts across nine global service centers, deploys AI agents to resolve millions of contacts and hundreds of thousands of cases annually, automating low-value tasks and running autonomous workflows in a high-stakes finance environment. Then explore how Amazon Operation’s Workforce Intelligence & Scheduling Engine (WISE) enables them to orchestrate the operating, management, and adjustment of labor and flow across more than 1,200 facilities. When a gap in a tool, process, or service appears, it spins up autonomous coding agents on Bedrock AgentCore to build, test, and deploy solutions or mechanisms to close the gaps. Leaders will share the innovations that enabled them to stop managing systems and start orchestrating them.

sessions.abstract: Most forecasting stalls when history is thin or inputs disagree. See how Amazon Connect Decisions produces accurate forecasts from your first day, even with limited data. AI teammates orchestrate more than 18 forecasting tools and models trained on Amazon data, then harmonize statistical forecasts, customer commitments, and cross functional inputs into one consensus plan. sessions.title: Level up your bot defense for mobile apps and web with AWS WAF SDK
sessions.abstract: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. Learn how to go beyond basic rule-based blocking to implement dynamic, data-driven defenses that adapt to evolving threats. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

sessions.title: Leverage the power of MCP servers for resource inventory and compliance across clouds
sessions.abstract: AI agents can now interact with AWS services through the Model Context Protocol. In this code talk, we live-build a governance agent that uses MCP to query AWS Config for resource configurations. You'll see how to construct compliance checks, detect configuration drift, and trigger automated remediation using natural language all powered by Config's recording and advanced query capabilities. We explain the architecture decisions and trade-offs so you can adapt this pattern to your own governance workflows.

sessions.title: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
sessions.abstract: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation

sessions.title: Lights, Camera, Fargate—A Reality-TV Startup Hardened for Scale on AWS
sessions.abstract: In six weeks on reality TV coding show The Full Stack, we built DataSwarm — a data-observability solution shipped as an open-source CLI with cloud-hosted data analysis and remediation. Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

In this session, Decart will explore the infrastructure powering this shift, what it takes to deliver AI-generated video in real time, and how to bring these experiences to scale. Join us for a look at the technology behind Live AI, and where it’s going next. This presentation is brought to you by Decart, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: Agentic workloads are multi-step, tool-calling, and retrieval-augmented, which means they stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. You leave with working code for all three patterns that you can adapt to your own agents.

sessions.title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
sessions.abstract: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

sessions.title: LOTA: Detecting and preventing advanced lateral movement
sessions.abstract: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

sessions.title: LSEG: Scaling multi-agent AI with assurance on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) manages one of the world's largest risk intelligence datasets, processing millions of records that demand continuous curation and validation. In this session, learn how LSEG built a durable agentic AI framework on Amazon Bedrock—orchestrating multi-agent workflows that combines deterministic rules, AI enrichment, and human review to reduce false positives in financial crime screening. LSEG will share their approach to continuous AI assurance with golden dataset evaluations and staged rollout gates with real-time observability and automated rollback to safely scale automation while maintaining the accuracy global financial institutions require.

sessions.abstract: We're entering a new era of software operations where the question is no longer whether intelligent agents have a role in production, but whether humans should still be the first responder. As production environments continue to grow more complex, agents are becoming part of the operations team, handling the repetitive work of operating production while engineers focus on the decisions that require judgment, creativity, and experience. This session explores how leading enterprises are rethinking on-call, improving reliability, and reshaping the way production is operated by putting machines on call for humans. This presentation is brought to you by Resolve AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Maintain accountability when using IAM federation
sessions.abstract: Many enterprises access AWS through IAM federation with providers like Okta and Microsoft Entra ID. But if your analysts share an IAM role, downstream services do not distinguish who has assumed that role making per-user access controls and audit more challenging. In this chalk talk, we'll explore considerations when using federated environments, discuss why it matters for compliance and security, and examine what it takes to maintain individual accountability without overhauling your existing federation setup.

sessions.title: Make AMD Your Default on AWS: Efficient EC2 for the Agentic AI Era with EPYC (sponsored by AMD)
sessions.abstract: What if you could run agentic AI for over 30% less on Amazon EC2—within the contracts you already have? As autonomous agents call inference models and tools, compute demand explodes and the CPU-to-GPU ratio inverts from 1:8 to 8:1, making processor choice the defining ROI decision. This session proves how 5th-Gen AMD EPYC "Turin" on EC2 runs general-purpose workloads faster and smaller, delivering >30% OpEx savings you can redirect from IT overhead into AI budgets. Partners see how MAP-aligned migration funding, POC support, and co-sell turn efficient, variety-ready AMD infrastructure on AWS into bigger, faster customer wins. sessions.title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
sessions.abstract: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.

See how Confluent Tableflow turns Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg tables and registers them in the AWS Glue Data Catalog—eliminating the need for custom streaming pipelines. In this session, you'll learn best practices, tools, and patterns that power users have perfected to set up and scale your multi-agent workloads and take on hours-long tasks with confidence.

sessions.title: Make your vector search faster, more relevant, and cost-efficient
sessions.abstract: You have a vector workload running and questions piling up: How do I raise relevance? How do I control cost as I scale? Which ranking technique fits my data? We give you a quick tour of vector capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service, then spend the rest of the session working through your problems. Topics on the table include hybrid search combining lexical and vector results, ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, maximal marginal relevance, and filtering strategies, when to reach for Automatic Semantic Enrichment or neural sparse vectors instead of building your own embedding pipeline, and cost optimization techniques including quantization, tiered storage, GPU-accelerated indexing, and auto-optimization. Come with a workload in mind and leave with tuning direction for your specific situation.

sessions.title: Making Enterprise Data AI-Ready Without the Data Engineering Overhead (sponsored by Eon)
sessions.abstract: Enterprise data is spread across databases, object stores, and compute, but making it usable by AI often requires months of data engineering and a growing web of pipelines to build and maintain. In this session, we’ll show how Eon continuously discovers, connects to, classifies, and transforms data across Amazon RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EC2, S3, and more into a unified, AI-ready data layer. We’ll walk through the architecture and semantic layer on AWS, then share how agents can use Amazon Bedrock to query that governed context in natural language through MCP, with Claude, Amazon Quick, and other AI clients. sessions.title: Making Kiro Crew work for your team
sessions.abstract: Kiro Crew is the persistent, open source development workspace that remembers your context, learns how you work, and coordinates across your unique tools and workflows, so you come back to progress instead of another workflow to restart. In this session, you'll learn how to make Kiro Crew work for your team: wire in the tools your team already use over MCP, set up scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs so work keeps moving while you're away, and shape shared memory and reusable skills so agents don't start cold and maintain team standards and best practices.

On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.

sessions.title: Managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at scale: customer lessons

Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints, spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Attendees will learn strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.

sessions.title: Managing Bots, Mentoring Brains: The Future of Hybrid Leadership
sessions.abstract: The traditional playbook for executive leadership is undergoing fundamental change as hybrid ecosystems of human employees and autonomous AI agents become commonplace, with agents acting as co-workers, specialists, and decision-makers. This shift requires executives to expand their skill set, dividing organizational goals between human creative strategy and agentic operational execution. Moving past the AI hype, this session examines how human roles must evolve from executors to context engineers and decision architects, and how career progression must be rewritten when entry-level and repetitive work is owned by digital labor. Explore how women in leadership will adapt and build tomorrow's leaders.

sessions.title: Managing Lambda Runtimes at Scale for Platform Teams
sessions.abstract: Lambda's managed runtimes work until your platform team needs a pinned language version, a pre-loaded monitoring agent, or an SDK that every function must use. Today that means managing custom layers, coordinating updates across teams, and hoping nobody is running a version you deprecated last quarter. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard strategies for taking control of your Lambda runtime layer. Bring your runtime requirements and the constraints you're working around today.

sessions.title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
sessions.abstract: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.

sessions.title: Map once and prove everywhere across multiple compliance frameworks
sessions.abstract: Regulatory frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and the EU AI Act each demand separate assessments, yet a significant portion of their requirements overlap. You spend time collecting duplicate evidence for controls you already have. This chalk talk introduces the control inheritance approach and shows how a single AWS Config rule or organizational policy can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks. You walk through real examples of framework overlap, automation patterns that eliminate duplicate evidence collection, and a governance approach you can implement immediately.

sessions.title: Mapping and Securing the Enterprise AI Attack Surface (sponsored by Zscaler)
sessions.abstract: AI is racing across the enterprise—showing up in endpoints, apps, workflows, agents, and data paths faster than most security teams can track. But securing AI takes more than knowing where it exists; it requires understanding how data flows, where it comes from, where it goes, and which users, devices, apps, and AI endpoints interact with it along the way. In this session, we’ll explore how to map the AI attack surface and its data lineage while securing the AI endpoints where innovation actually happens. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Master Agent Skills: From Desktop Builds to Production Deployment
sessions.abstract: Build, govern, and scale production-ready agent skills across your enterprise on Amazon Quick. Author custom skills on Quick, then shift to the admin perspective: register skills in Quick Catalog for org-wide discovery, configure access policies, and schedule autonomous execution at scale. Through two business-driven use cases — churn prevention from contact center data and intelligent claims processing that eliminates manual back-office work — you'll deploy measurable automation. Leave with working skills, a governance framework for hundreds of agents across teams, and a playbook for communicating ROI to leadership.

sessions.title: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
sessions.abstract: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.

sessions.title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
sessions.abstract: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.
