sessions.title: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
sessions.abstract: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

sessions.title: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
sessions.abstract: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

sessions.title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. Through live whiteboarding, demos, and production architectures; we'll cover how customers are maximizing GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and multiple teams with shared architectures and GPUs. Then learn how SageMaker Studio gives give data scientists, AI researchers, and machine learning engineers an easy way to to iterate on jobs all on the shared pool of resources. We'll also see how Humain has optimized utilization of compute resources across two large HyperPod clusters, onboarding multiple teams of researchers with team isolation and advanced task submission strategies. Participants will walk away with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure

sessions.title: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
sessions.abstract: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.

sessions.title: Maximizing EC2 NVMe local storage
sessions.abstract: Discover how to leverage the latest high-performance Nitro SSDs in EC2 storage-optimized instances for data-intensive workloads. This technical session explores new capabilities for monitoring and managing NVMe instance storage, including enhanced performance metrics—latency, IOPS, and throughput—to optimize and troubleshoot your workloads. We also demonstrate the new AWS Local Instance Storage (LIS) CSI driver for simplified NVMe volume management in Amazon EKS. Learn best practices for storage performance monitoring and integrating the LIS CSI driver in containerized applications.

sessions.title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
sessions.abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.

sessions.title: MCP is Just An MVP. Knowledge Lakes Are The Sequel. (sponsored by Atolio)
sessions.abstract: MCP lets agents connect to systems. It's a minimum viable product, not a complete way to run that connection at scale. Raw database access hit the same wall decades ago, before warehouses and data lakes brought structure and governance at scale. Point-to-point agent connections hit it again: costs climb with every added tool call, latency stacks with every cross-system hop, and permissions rarely travel with retrieved data, making synthesized knowledge a sharper security risk than raw SQL ever posed. This session traces that history, breaks down each failure mode, and maps what a knowledge lake built for agents solves. This presentation is brought to you by Atolio, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

sessions.title: MCP Meets GraphQL: A Typed Foundation for Enterprise AI Agents (sponsored by Apollo GraphQL)
sessions.abstract: Enterprises connecting AI agents to systems of record face three unsolved problems: can an agent discover what data exists and what it means, get that context without runaway token cost, and touch only what it's authorized to touch. GraphQL, the proven Linux Foundation-backed standard beneath many of the world's largest customer experiences at brands like Netflix, AirBnB, Shopify, Walmart, and countless others, already solves all three through self-describing schemas and field-level queries. This talk lays out the architecture for combining GraphQL with MCP, including Apollo's approach to graph-based orchestration for cost and reliability. This presentation is brought to you by Apollo GraphQL, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
sessions.abstract: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

sessions.title: Meet Your AI Teammate for WorkSpaces Administration
sessions.abstract: Whether you run WorkSpaces today or are evaluating cloud desktops for the first time, operational overhead follows every virtual desktop deployment: ongoing monitoring, systemic issues that surface as tickets, and end-user requests that consume administrator time. Most teams operate reactively, triaging problems after they surface and manually guiding users through resolution. This session explores how Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor is using AI to reduce resolution time for both IT administrators and end users. We'll walk through the operational challenges we're hearing from customers, share our approach to solving them, and demonstrate early results from production environments. Bring your deployment architecture questions.

sessions.title: Migrate and modernize infrastructure from your IDE with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Migration and modernization involve dozens of manual steps across landing zones, networking, and containerization. What if you could drive the entire workflow from your IDE? In this code talk, you'll see how Kiro and AWS Transform work together as an agentic toolkit. First, generate a multi-account landing zone as infrastructure as code. Next, feed a VMware configuration export to the network agent and get Terraform modules or CDK constructs for VPCs, security groups, and production-ready network topology. Then point the containerization agent at a repo to produce ECR images and deploy to Amazon EKS.

sessions.abstract: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. sessions.title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage

Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.

This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.

In this chalk talk, we'll work through proven migration patterns for moving legacy ETL workloads to AWS Glue. We will tackle topics such as converting complex transformation logic, handling incremental and change-data-capture loads, preserving data quality and lineage, and phasing cutover to minimize risk. Bring your toughest migration questions and leave with a practical framework f of how serverless ETL changes the economics and operations of data integration.

sessions.abstract: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. sessions.title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.

Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. sessions.title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
sessions.abstract: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

sessions.title: Modernize a Legacy Telecom Billing App with AWS Transform Custom
sessions.abstract: Got an old telecom application buried under decades of technical debt? In this hands-on session, you'll take a legacy BSS billing system and modernize it using AWS Transform Custom. Start by analyzing the codebase to understand business logic, dependencies, and technical debt. Then apply a built-in catalog transformation to upgrade the language and framework instantly. Next, define your own custom transformation in natural language to convert legacy interfaces to modern APIs. Validate, test for functional equivalence, and deploy to AWS. Walk away with a running modernized app and reusable transformation recipes, plus hands-on experience modernizing real-world telecom applications.

In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

Working from a legacy app, you'll port .NET Framework code to modern, cross-platform .NET, migrate SQL Server to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, then containerize and deploy to Amazon ECS or EKS. You'll leave with a proven approach to transform your full stack into a scalable, cloud-native architecture. Come ready with your personal GitHub account. Laptop required.

sessions.title: Modernizing Care for the Underserved: Montefiore's Cloud Journey
sessions.abstract: Montefiore Einstein is one of New York's leading academic health systems, serving 1.3 million Bronx residents across 11 hospitals and 300+ ambulatory locations. To best care for patients, most of whom rely on Medicare or Medicaid, Montefiore needed to modernize its enterprise technology. Montefiore selected AWS as its strategic cloud provider to build a secure, scalable, and resilient foundation that strengthens security and optimizes costs. This session explores how the transformation—including an Epic migration—enables AI-powered clinical decision support, improves the reliability of critical medical records, and expands patient access through Amazon One Medical. Learn the strategies, lessons, and cloud-first approach driving better outcomes for the patients and communities Montefiore serves.

sessions.title: Modernizing .NET to Serverless: Native AOT and SnapStart, live
sessions.abstract: .NET workloads on Lambda have historically meant slower cold starts and JIT warmup time that doesn't match Serverless execution patterns. Native AOT and SnapStart on .NET 10 close that gap, bringing cold starts under 200ms, but modernization isn't flip-a-switch. In this code talk, modernize a .NET function to AOT live, watch it fail, then fix it on stage: serialization with source generators, reflection-based DI replaced, trimming warnings resolved. See real measurements across AOT, SnapStart, and the managed runtime. Walk away with a library compatibility matrix and modernization patterns for your own .NET Serverless journey.

sessions.title: Modernizing VMware workloads with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
sessions.abstract: Migrating VMware workloads to AWS often means rethinking storage, but it doesn't have to. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a storage foundation built for VMware migrations. Learn how FSx for ONTAP delivers multi-protocol support, enterprise data management, and ONTAP compatibility that VMware administrators already know. We'll discuss real world migration patterns, cost optimization through deduplication and compression, and high availability with Multi-AZ and zero RPO. Bring your questions and join us to design a migration strategy that minimizes disruption and maximizes your existing ONTAP investments.

sessions.title: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
sessions.abstract: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

sessions.title: Molecule to Market: Bayer & Capgemini Accelerate Drug Discovery with NVIDIA BioNeMo (sponsored by NVIDIA)
sessions.abstract: Join us to learn how Bayer Crop Science needed to accelerate target identification and lead optimization within its drug/crop-science discovery pipeline, and was able to accelerate their process with NVIDIA GPUs and BioNeMo. Building on AWS, they created a drug discovery workflow accelerating target identification and lead optimization through GPU-accelerated inference, molecular generation, and protein modeling, running on NVIDIA hardware. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Monetize AI Bot Traffic: Agent-Ready Media with AWS WAF & AI Analysis
sessions.abstract: More than half of web traffic now comes from AI bots that consume content built for humans while returning little value to publishers. This hands-on workshop tackles both the content and the monetization side. First, you'll build a pipeline that converts images, video, and audio into concise, agent-friendly markdown summaries including interpreting what's shown, said, and meant, while preserving the originals for human readers. Then you'll monetize bot traffic with AWS WAF AI traffic monetization, setting per-request pricing by bot verification tier and collecting payment via the x402 protocol. You'll build a working dual-audience pipeline and WAF pricing configuration you can deploy against your own media.

sessions.title: Monetizing your applications with AWS
sessions.abstract: In this session, learn how to transform your finished application into a revenue-generating SaaS product. Learn about analyzing your cloud infrastructure, choose pricing models, and instrumenting code for usage metering. You'll see how to manage the complete billing lifecycle, from subscription management and invoicing to tax calculation and payment processing. Walk away with a clear path to accelerate your time-to-market and start charging customers.

sessions.title: Monitor Agent Performance and Telemetry using AgentCore Observability
sessions.abstract: A personal finance assistant agent deployed on AgentCore Runtime starts showing intermittent failures and slow responses. In this lab, you will use AgentCore Observability with CloudWatch GenAI dashboards and Transaction Search to diagnose production issues. Trace errors through spans, correlate telemetry with application logs, and identify root causes including a tool timeout and conversation history bloat. Apply fixes, redeploy to AgentCore Runtime, and set up CloudWatch Alarms to catch issues before users do.

sessions.title: Monitor AI workloads and agents end to end
sessions.abstract: Get hands-on with Amazon CloudWatch Omni, the next evolution of CloudWatch that converges application and agent observability into one AI-powered solution. Instrument an agent, trace its execution, run evaluations, and experiment with prompts and models in your IDE. Explore auto-discovered topology, golden metrics, and AI-powered investigation with AWS DevOps Agent.

sessions.title: Monitor and optimize costs for Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: As AI adoption accelerates, organizations need visibility into who is consuming Amazon Bedrock resources and how that spend maps to business outcomes. In this lightning talk, see how to tag API calls for granular cost attribution, set real-time budgets to control AI spend, and track costs as they happen in the Billing and Cost Management console. Walk away with a practical framework for aligning AI spend to business outcomes.

sessions.title: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
sessions.abstract: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. We will walk through use cases for each tool, including when to reach for one over another, and deep dive into Storage Lens for optimizing at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

sessions.title: More than a heartbeat: Designing health checks that matter
sessions.abstract: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing, not just that a port is open. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard meaningful health check patterns across ELB, Amazon Global Accelerator, and Amazon Route 53 that covers how to validate database readiness, confirm replica currency, and verify end-to-end request success. We'll explore thresholds, timing configurations, and graceful failover strategies. Bring your architectures, including diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard, and we'll design your health strategy together. Leave with actionable patterns that reflect true application liveness.

For developers, platform engineers, and security teams building with AWS AgentCore, this session shows how 1Password uses the same governed credential workflow from a local sandbox to the cloud without code changes. Attendees will see how this approach helps engineering teams move faster, limits the blast radius of a compromised agent, and gives security teams a clear audit trail. The session covers short-lived credential delivery through the AgentCore gateway and policies that apply consistently from development through production. This presentation is brought to you by 1Password, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Move code modernization at scale from one-time to continuous
sessions.abstract: Technical debt doesn't stop accumulating when a modernization project ends. Across thousands of repos, outdated dependencies, framework drift, and security gaps compound daily. So why treat code modernization at scale as a one-time campaign? In this chalk talk, we'll explore how AWS Transform is evolving into always-on, autonomous remediation at portfolio scale. We'll dig into what continuous mode looks like in practice, what early enterprise customers are seeing, and how this changes the way your teams think about maintaining code health over time. Bring your questions.

See a live demo where any agent, model, or tool acts only with the right context, identity, policy, approvals, and cost controls. Learn why the unit of value is the governed workflow. In a few minutes, you will see how to identify which workloads are ready to move and what the path looks like, so your teams ship applications while AWS runs the operations underneath. You own the application. AWS owns the operational responsibility.

sessions.title: Move your multi-tenant agents to serverless AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Running multi-tenant agents on Kubernetes gives you flexibility, but it introduces certain operational overhead like cluster management, scaling decisions, and identity plumbing. Starting from a working agentic SaaS application on Amazon EKS, you'll progressively refactor each component onto AgentCore: implement tenant isolation, configure shared MCP tools with per-tenant scoping, and instrument tenant-aware memory and observability. sessions.title: Multi-agent AI: Orchestration and choreography, compared
sessions.abstract: Every multi-agent AI system needs a coordination layer. The hard question is who decides what happens next: a central orchestrator or the agents themselves. In this session, you deploy the same five-agent travel booking pipeline through both orchestration (Step Functions) and choreography (EventBridge). Run identical load tests, inject the same failures, and add a sixth agent to each. Measure blast radius, extensibility cost, and debugging speed to see where the two approaches diverge. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

Three Oracle industry leaders will explore what that value looks like in practice. Hear how financial institutions can strengthen fraud detection, risk management, and customer experiences; how healthcare organizations can generate trusted clinical and operational insights; and how manufacturers can improve forecasting, supply chain decisions, asset performance, and operational efficiency. Leave with a practical understanding of Oracle AI Database@AWS and concrete examples of how multicloud can support industry-specific AI and business outcomes. sessions.abstract: Many organizations do not operate in a single cloud provider, creating the need for security solutions that cover multiple providers. In this lightning talk, see how AWS security services deliver unified multicloud security across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. From posture management and vulnerability detection to risk correlation and asset visibility, learn how security teams can gain a consolidated view and respond to risks across their entire cloud estate.

sessions.title: Multicloud-to-AWS transformation: HealthEdge migrating 8,700 servers
sessions.abstract: Running workloads across multiple clouds and on-premises data centers creates compounding complexity: inconsistent tooling, duplicated licensing costs, and operational overhead that slows everything down. HealthEdge faced exactly this across Azure, GCP, and four data centers while serving 130 health plans daily, where security is paramount. Hear how they're consolidating 8,700 servers via AWS Transform, 1,600 databases, and thousands of cloud services onto AWS on a 2-year roadmap, raising their security bar, and building internal AWS expertise to drive a lasting culture change - all without disrupting the plans that depend on them.

sessions.title: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
sessions.abstract: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.

sessions.title: Multi-tenant agentic AI with Aurora and DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: AI agents are autonomous, stateful, and capable of invoking external tools. In a multi-tenant SaaS system, every one of those capabilities is a potential data isolation failure. In this workshop, build a complete multi-tenant agentic AI solution enforcing tenant isolation across Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level security, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon S3 Vectors. Implement tenant-scoped vector stores for RAG, agent memory backed by multiple database engines, MCP-based tool authorization gated by subscription tier, and usage metering. Leave with a working reference architecture that prevents cross-tenant data leakage. Bring a laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Multi-Tenant Agentic Platforms: A Scalable Reference Architecture
sessions.abstract: SaaS is going AI-native. ISVs must orchestrate third-party agents at scale. This session presents a multi-tenant architecture covering MCP, A2A, and AgentCore for orchestration, entitlement-based monetization, secure token exchange, agent lifecycle via Agent Registry, and cross-tenant observability.

sessions.title: Multi-tenant compute modernization with Amazon EMR on EKS
sessions.abstract: What does it take to run millions of diverse jobs a day across many tenants without costs spiraling or one bad workload taking down the fleet? In this chalk talk, we explore how organizations modernize a multi-tenant compute layer on EMR on EKS to serve batch analytics, streaming, ML, and agentic AI from one platform. We whiteboard the choices that make it possible: custom bin packing to mix heterogeneous tenant workloads efficiently, EKS provisioned control planes to sustain high job throughput per cluster, and Graviton to drive down cost per job. Bring your scaling challenges and we'll design solutions together.

sessions.title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
sessions.abstract: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.

sessions.abstract: Amazon EKS has become the runtime of choice for ISVs building agentic SaaS, offering the control, workload isolation, and networking flexibility that managed runtimes cannot. The challenge is multi-tenancy: how do you run agent workloads for hundreds of tenants on shared infrastructure without blast radius, cost leakage, or isolation drift? In this workshop, build a multi-tenant agent deployment on EKS with tenant isolation across namespaces and network policies, IRSA-backed credentials per agent workload, and per-tenant observability via OpenTelemetry. Each lab ends with an isolation proof. Leave with a reference architecture you can apply directly to your cluster.

sessions.title: NatWest: Embedding AI agents into the software delivery lifecycle
sessions.abstract: AI is moving beyond code completion to reshape how software is built. In this session, learn how NatWest, one of the UK's largest banks, uses Kiro and agentic AI to accelerate design, development, and delivery across its engineering organization. NatWest will share how it embeds AI into everyday engineering while meeting the demands of a highly regulated environment, from security and compliance guardrails to identity and access integration and governance. Explore how the team measures developer productivity and reinvents its delivery workflows. You’ll learn how to bring agentic development to your own engineering teams.

sessions.title: Navigating mergers and divestitures across multiple AWS organizations
sessions.abstract: Enterprises go through mergers, face divestitures, and inherit multiple AWS Organizations, each with its own structure and identity provider. Consolidating or separating these environments is complex. This interactive session covers patterns for merging AWS organizations, managing multiple organizations in parallel, and splitting organizations cleanly. You dive into the identity challenge of migrating between Microsoft Entra ID, Google, and Okta when each entity brings its own IdP to AWS. You leave with practical patterns and lessons learned engagements with customers like you.

sessions.title: Navigating the inter-workings of an agentic SOC & threat hunting analyst
sessions.abstract: Security analysts face an expanding attack surface with finite time and attention. In this session, we show how analysts can leverage AI-powered agents to accelerate their core workflows — from automated triage and log correlation to proactive threat hunting across CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and threat intelligence feeds. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. You will see how to configure trust boundaries so agents act within your approved scope, how source attribution ensures every AI-surfaced claim traces back to a specific log, and how to evaluate whether the AI is actually making your team faster.

sessions.title: Need for Speed: The journey to high EBS performance on EC2 instances
sessions.abstract: Achieving consistent, low-latency block storage at cloud scale requires rethinking every layer of the IO stack. In this session, we walk you through the architectural evolution of Amazon EBS, and show how a series of innovations reduced hypervisor overhead, slashed network latency, and enabled higher block storage IOPS and throughput on your EC2 instances. We will also discuss how Nitro enabled specific EBS features such as Instance bandwidth Configuration, Torn Write Protection, and detailed performance statistics via NVMe logs. Bring your questions and leave with an understanding of how EBS delivers high performing block storage for your mission-critical applications.

sessions.title: Network Firewall deployment models: pros, cons, best practices
sessions.abstract: One firewall, many ways to deploy it, and each mode unlocks a different architectural superpower. This session maps your options: distributed, centralized, multi-endpoint, explicit proxy, and the newest firewall modes. Through real architectures, you'll see where each one shines, how they scale, and the patterns that make your network security clean, flexible, and future-ready. Whether you're protecting a single VPC or a global multi-account estate, you'll leave knowing exactly which mode fits your environment and why. If you route traffic through AWS, this is the map that gets you there faster.

sessions.title: Network firewall deployment without the guesswork: codify, deploy, done
sessions.abstract: Level up your firewall policy operations at scale in this hands-on workshop. Learn to integrate AWS Network Firewall into an existing AWS environment using Terraform. You will then implement the latest Network Firewall features such as web category filtering, JA4 fingerprinting, and EventBridge automation. By the end of this session you will have both practical experience adding Network Firewall to existing environments and reusable patterns ready for your own infrastructure.

sessions.title: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights
sessions.abstract: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. This chalk talk explores how to close that gap with Container Network Observability, Network Flow Monitor, and OpenTelemetry-based Container Insights on Amazon EKS. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.

sessions.title: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights
sessions.abstract: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. This chalk talk explores how to close that gap with Container Network Observability, Network Flow Monitor, and OpenTelemetry-based Container Insights on Amazon EKS. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.

sessions.title: Network policy across hundreds of accounts with AWS Network Security Manager
sessions.abstract: Once an organization grows to hundreds of accounts, managing network security policies by hand becomes a liability. AWS Network Security Manager deploys AWS WAF, AWS Shield, and soon to come AWS Network Firewall across a multi-account environment from a single policy definition. This session covers how to build defense in depth with Network Security Manager, and how to keep centralized network security manageable as you add accounts.

sessions.abstract: As organizations scale across multiple accounts with hybrid connectivity, designing effective network inspection becomes critical. sessions.abstract: As organizations scale across multiple accounts with hybrid connectivity, designing effective network inspection becomes critical. sessions.title: Network security innovations for agentic workloads
sessions.abstract: AI agents plan and execute actions autonomously, at machine speed, with real-world consequences. Unlike traditional automation that follows pre-defined network paths, agent traffic is non-deterministic, calling different APIs and chaining different services each time it runs. In this session, we cover the network security capabilities AWS has built for this shift. You'll see how to inspect and control autonomous traffic at every layer, from DNS resolution to application-layer filtering, enforce least-privilege connectivity for agents, and detect anomalous behavior in machine-to-machine communication.

sessions.title: Next-gen threat detection: GuardDuty advanced security capabilities
sessions.abstract: Amazon GuardDuty protects millions of accounts using AI and ML models purpose-built for cloud security, and the detection engine keeps getting smarter without requiring action from you. In this session, the lead scientist behind GuardDuty's detection engine takes you inside the research. Learn how the team designs models for security inference at scale, uses distillation and reinforcement learning to keep detection cost-efficient without sacrificing accuracy, and distinguishes normal from anomalous behavior without using customer data for training. See how these advances translate into expanded coverage, faster detection of sophisticated threats, and deeper investigation workflows. You leave with an understanding of the engineering tradeoffs behind AI-native threat detection at AWS scale and how to operationalize the latest capabilities.

sessions.title: Nine Seconds to Zero: Protecting AWS from AI Agent Disasters
sessions.abstract: In April 2026, an AI coding agent deleted a company's entire production database in nine seconds, without being asked. The agent was confidently wrong and had the permissions to act on it. In this session, we recreate that incident live using Amazon Bedrock, walk through every failure in the chain, then rebuild the architecture with six hardening layers: Bedrock Guardrails, human approval gates, least-privilege IAM, deletion protection, isolated backups, and real-time monitoring. Walk away with a concrete checklist for designing AI-assisted systems that plan for when the AI is wrong, not just when it performs perfectly.

sessions.title: Nitro Isolation Engine: Formally verifying confidentiality
sessions.abstract: What does it mean, *precisely*, for the data of a virtual machine to be confidential? Answering this question will take us on a journey into low-level systems and high-level mathematics as we unpack this question in the context of the AWS Nitro System, the underlying virtualization platform that powers Amazon EC2. You will discover the low-level hardware and software that isolate virtual machines, our precise mathematical definition of confidentiality, and the methods we use to establish this crucial property for the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine. No background in virtualization systems or formal verification is expected.

sessions.title: No Data Left Behind: The AI-Ready Path Through AWS (sponsored by Qlik)
sessions.abstract: Your enterprise data is scattered across SAP, mainframes, databases, and cloud platforms that were never designed to talk to each other — and every AI initiative depends on enabling that communication. This session shows how Qlik and AWS modernize that data without downtime, rewrites, or re-platforming risk: zero-footprint CDC, Qlik Open Lakehouse with Apache Iceberg and Amazon Athena, Spark Structured Streaming on Amazon EMR, and governed data products built for AI. You'll also get a bonus preview of Qlik's Studio AI Assistant on Amazon Bedrock and what's next for agentic workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Qlik, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: No room for error: deploying trusted AI when the stakes are high (sponsored by Monte Carlo)
sessions.abstract: Deploying agents at scale is a major endeavor for any organization; in healthcare, the stakes are especially high. Unpredictable behaviors & unreliable outputs pose a risk to patients, invite scrutiny from regulators, & erode hard-won institutional trust. Regulated industries must balance accuracy alongside their drive to innovate. Barr Moses, co-founder & CEO of Monte Carlo, will delve into this challenging topic with leaders from GE Healthcare. They’ll dissect some of the most difficult failure modes for agents & discuss how reliability practices have to evolve as teams scale agentic workflows in high-stakes environments. Discussed: how AI itself can be turned back on the problem of observing, resolving, and optimizing agents as well as building the guardrails, ownership models, & trust infrastructure that let a highly regulated organization move quickly without compromising on trust. This presentation is brought to you by Monte Carlo, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Northwestern Mutual: Reinventing policy servicing with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Financial representatives at Northwestern Mutual traditionally logged service requests and waited for back-office resolution. In this session, we'll walk through the production architecture behind this transformation: Amazon Bedrock Agents connected to core insurance systems through the Model Context Protocol, with orchestration and governance controls designed for a regulated environment. We'll cover authorization patterns, auditability, human oversight, and lessons learned moving from proof of concept to production. Representatives now resolve significantly more requests directly—reducing resolution times, improving good-order processing, and driving higher satisfaction, with participants reporting better outcomes for their clients.

sessions.title: Not all bots are bad: building a secure perimeter with AWS WAF
sessions.abstract: Your edge traffic is a mix of customers, AI agents, scrapers, and attackers. Treat them the same and you lose either security or revenue. In this workshop, you turn AWS WAF into a decision layer that classifies traffic in real time and routes it. Legitimate users get a fast lane, suspicious traffic goes to deception environments that waste attackers' time and reveal their intent, and AI agents get their own treatment that opens the door to new ways of charging for access. None of it requires changes to your origin logic.

sessions.title: Now serverless has servers. What now?
sessions.abstract: I spent years advocating for serverless, but as a CTO, I could not always see a viable path to bring it into certain business scenarios. In this talk, I share what has changed with the new AWS capabilities, why this can change the game for larger companies, and, along the way, I explore the concepts and how these services work in more depth to help us think about architecture with more clarity.

sessions.title: OAuth delegation patterns for AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
sessions.abstract: AI agents act on behalf of users and systems, and delegating the right access without over-permissioning is hard. In this chalk talk, we use code examples to work through authorization delegation with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity. We cover the OAuth grant flows that matter for agents, including authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine calls, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. For each flow, you see which agent scenario it fits and when to choose it over the others.

sessions.title: Observability and operations in the AI era
sessions.abstract: Generative AI broke the assumptions traditional monitoring was built on, and teams struggle to keep non-deterministic systems predictable, explainable, and affordable. This session opens on that challenge, then shows how the newest observability capabilities give you visibility into model quality, cost, and agent behavior across your AI stack, using traces, spans, and confidence scoring, illustrated with real customer patterns.

sessions.title: Observability-driven scaling: Teaching EKS clusters to right-size themselves
sessions.abstract: Scaling container workloads reactively by waiting for CPU to spike or pods to crash leaves money on the table and risks user-facing latency. This chalk talk explores observability-driven scaling: using CloudWatch Container Insights, KEDA, and custom metrics pipelines to make Amazon EKS clusters anticipate demand before it arrives. We walk through real architectures where teams replaced reactive HPA with predictive scaling informed by business metrics, reduced over-provisioning by 40%, and cut P99 latency during traffic ramps. Bring your scaling headaches and we'll whiteboard solutions together.

sessions.title: Observability for AI agents: Strands, OpenTelemetry, and Langfuse
sessions.abstract: You're running AI agents in cloud ops, but can you see inside them? In this hands-on workshop, deploy a Strands Agents SDK agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, then wire up full observability using Strands' built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation and Langfuse (open-source) as the backend. Trace every LLM call, tool invocation, and reasoning step. Debug failures, analyze token costs, version prompts, and score output quality — all with open source and open standards.

sessions.abstract: When AI agents run as long-lived, multi-invocation workflows on Lambda Durable Functions, standard observability breaks down. A single durable execution spanning five specialists producing independent telemetry, replays pollute logs with duplicates, and no tool can tell you which agents are failing across thousands of concurrent runs. We'll build a multi-agent purchasing coordinator with Lambda durable functions, instrument it with the OpenTelemetry plugin for one coherent trace across all invocations, and CloudWatch insights to answer fleet-wide queries with business context. Attendees leave with fully observable architecture and the investigation pattern from CloudWatch alarm to end-to-end traces and correlated log entries.

sessions.title: Observe AI agents beyond your perimeter
sessions.abstract: Your developers are burning tokens on AI coding agents with zero visibility. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex run on laptops, outside your perimeter, with no telemetry reaching your observability backend. In this session, we fix that. Using native OpenTelemetry export and Amazon CloudWatch's OTLP endpoint with a single bearer token, with no collectors, no sidecars, no credential wiring, we ship metrics (token usage, cost, productivity), logs (tool decisions, errors), and traces (agent reasoning chains) directly from developer machines. Then we build a live dashboard with per-team cost attribution and anomaly alerting, all queryable with PromQL. Walk out ready to deploy in minutes.

This session covers how to bring OpenTelemetry with zero-code/no-touch instrumentation in applications running on AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, ECS and EKS, as well as how to bring into your OpenTelemetry pipelines telemetry from various AWS managed services and how to use agentic skills to level up the quality of your instrumentations and get better value out of your telemetry backends, coding agents, and AI tools. You will leave this session with a concrete map to get your OpenTelemetry journey started with tangible results in minutes. This presentation is brought to you by Dash0, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Observe your applications and agents in one place
sessions.abstract: Traditional monitoring tools weren't built for the complexity of modern agentic and distributed applications. Teams juggle siloed dashboards, fragmented logs, and disconnected signals with no unified way to troubleshoot across agents, applications, and infrastructure. Amazon CloudWatch Omni is an AI-powered observability experience organized around your teams and the applications they run, combining OpenTelemetry interoperability with CloudWatch scale. See how you can troubleshoot applications faster and manage agents with confidence using automatic service discovery, dependency mapping, built-in evaluations, and natural-language investigation — all from the Omni UI, your IDE, or your favorite tools.

sessions.title: One agent, any robot: building physical AI with Strands Robots
sessions.abstract: Physical AI puts agents in the real world. This chalk talk builds a robotics agent with the Strands Robots SDK: one Robot() call gives an agent hands — a MuJoCo simulation by default, real hardware with one code parameter change. We'll whiteboard the loop around the embodied agent: perception, a vision-language-action policy (GR00T, Cosmos 3, LeRobot), and low-level control. We'll cover the the edge-to-cloud intelligence split, the peer-to-peer mesh and AWS IoT bridge coordinating a fleet, and sim-to-real transfer.

sessions.title: One agent to thousands: Building for scale with Newforma
sessions.abstract: When every team builds agents independently, you get the same ungovernable sprawl that drove the shift from artisanal EC2 to container platforms. Agents are non-deterministic workloads that require deterministic governance, and this tension drives every platform decision, from dual orchestration for known vs. emergent topologies, to policy-based boundaries around soft reasoning, to defense layers that compose without coupling. We walk through how Newforma operationalized this architecture on AWS, and attendees leave understanding how to layer orchestration, policy, and defense into an enterprise agent platform that scales safely.

sessions.title: One AI Assistant, Every Data Source: Unifying Access with Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask Amazon Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.

sessions.title: One Context Layer, Every Surface: Enterprise Knowledge for Agents That Work Anywhere
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can reach. In most enterprises, that data is scattered across dozens of systems, siloed, ungoverned, and invisible to the agents that need it most. In this chalk talk, we architect a context layer from the ground up: connecting enterprise knowledge into a unified index, then enriching that foundation with a knowledge graph that maps organizational relationships, business rules, and domain context, giving agents permission-scoped, relationship-aware intelligence at runtime. Then we take that intelligence to where users work: browser, desktop, mobile, collaboration tools, and productivity suites. Each surface independently governed yet sharing one agent identity, one memory, and one set of guardrails. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard the end-to-end path together.

sessions.title: One Control Plane for Every Agent: Architecture Patterns for Cost, Risk, and ROI (sponsored by Boomi)
sessions.abstract: Every agent call carries cost, permission, and blast radius, and as agents multiply across tools, frameworks, and SaaS, the gaps compound: uncapped spend, unapproved permissions, no shared record. This session breaks down an AI infrastructure layer, running on AWS, that governs every model, agent, and system. A design-time layer publishes an approved catalog of agents, tools, and MCP servers; a runtime layer routes, meters, and enforces policy on every call before it executes. See how spend caps, in-tenant SLMs, and governed APIs turn cost into a controlled input, while one trace gives finance, security, and engineering a shared, audit-ready record. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: One Control to Rule Them All: Guardrail Automation for Every Identity (sponsored by Sonrai Security)
sessions.abstract: Separate guardrails for humans, machine identities, and AI agents get messy, and rewriting every IAM policy takes forever. SCPs deployed at scope are easy to write. What follows is not. Nobody can say what a policy will break, so it never deploys. Someone gets blocked and the fix becomes a two hour hunt. The tenth control behaves nothing like the first. New accounts inherit none of it. This lightning talk answers all four using only AWS Organizations, SCPs, and RCPs. See how usage data makes a default deny safe, how access returns in seconds, and how least privilege holds. This presentation is brought to you by Sonrai Security, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: Your team is under pressure to deliver real-time applications, AI agents, operational experiences, and analytics faster—but separate databases, serving layers, and pipelines create stale data, duplicated copies, governance gaps, and scaling challenges. In this session, we’ll explore how Databricks on AWS brings these workloads together with Lakehouse//RT, Lakebase, and the Lakehouse Transactional Application Platform (LTAP). See how teams serve low-latency, high-concurrency analytics, power operational applications and AI agents with live transactional data, and analyze data where it is created—all from one platform and one governed copy of data. You’ll leave with practical architecture guidance for building reliable real-time and AI applications on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: One query across every signal: centralized security investigations at scale
sessions.abstract: When an alert fires, your first question is "what else happened?" Answering it means correlating API calls, network flows, DNS queries, and application logs, often across dozens of accounts and regions. In this session, we show how security practitioners centralize every signal into a single queryable layer using Amazon CloudWatch unified data store, then investigate incidents with faceted queries that span all telemetry types at once. We walk through building always-on visibility dashboards, running cross-account investigations without switching tools, and using AI-assisted analytics to surface context before you need to go looking for it. You leave with a reference architecture for turning centralized logs into faster investigations and clearer security posture.

sessions.abstract: AI/ML teams want to move fast - experiment with models, fine-tune them on their data, and serve them in production, without stitching together separate tools at every step. In this session, see how Amazon SageMaker AI lets you build, customize, deploy, and run inference, all within one service. Learn how to match the right approach to each stage: serverless experimentation for fast iteration, fully managed environments for custom frameworks and training, persistent clusters for large-scale research, and optimized inference for real-time and batch serving in production. Walk away with a practical decision framework and a reference architecture to start simple and scale without switching platforms.

sessions.abstract: "AWS turns 20 this year. Starting fresh in 2026 means navigating hundreds of services with no clear map for which decisions are one-way doors. I'll share how we built a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse from the AWS Organizations up. The full security stack (Access Analyzer, Config, GuardDuty, Macie, Security Hub, and WAF) built in the right order from day one. We almost walked through the wrong door. A pre-launch architecture review with our engineers and AWS solution architects caught it in time. Here's how to have that conversation before it's too late."

sessions.title: On-Policy Distillation on HyperPod EKS: Train Smarter Small Models
sessions.abstract: Frontier models are powerful but costly to deploy. On-policy distillation, adopted by Qwen3, MiMo, and GLM-5, lets you compress a large teacher into a lean, domain-specialized student by training on the student's own rollouts with dense token-level feedback. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, it's cheaper, more stable, and doesn't require a verifier. In this code talk, walk through a working implementation on HyperPod EKS: orchestrate teacher inference and student training across GPU pools, manage the rollout buffer, and evaluate convergence.

Ontologies solve this by structuring manufacturing knowledge so agents can trace decisions back to their source data. In this chalk talk, we show how ontology-grounded agents, powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents SDK, make verifiable decisions across the lifecycle with a live demo. Then explore Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI, for deploying OpenAI-powered agents in your AWS environment. Leave with a map of OpenAI on AWS and when to choose each path.

sessions.title: Persistent memory, shared context, instant discovery. Solving storage for AI agents
sessions.abstract: Production AI agents need to remember what happened yesterday, share work with other agents today, and find the right data in milliseconds. Most storage wasn't built for this. sessions.title: Prefill, decode, schedule: LLM inference without bubbles
sessions.abstract: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, but creates new problems. Head-of-line blocking on prefill, stragglers on decode, and pipeline bubbles when phases switch. This session goes deep on how to solve them. We cover temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism to eliminate phase-switching bubbles, adaptive scheduling across heterogeneous instances, tensor vs. pipeline parallelism tradeoffs for latency and throughput, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars for structured output without sacrificing token throughput, and KV-cache parallelism for multi-million context serving.

sessions.title: Production Agentic Trading: Build the pipeline Moeve runs on AgentCore
sessions.abstract: This session details the implementation of an agentic workforce managing the trade lifecycle in production energy trading operations. In this workshop, you'll build the pipeline Moeve runs in production: a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that extracts deal data from unstructured emails, resolves ambiguity deterministically against master data, and carries evidence per field. You'll harden it with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on input and output, then score it for accuracy and run-to-run consistency, including the fields that measured badly, and why. You'll leave with a reusable pattern for production deployment of mission-critical trading workflows with strict latency and reliability requirements.

sessions.title: Productionize, secure, and scale agentic applications on Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: AI agents are easy to prototype but hard to run in production. They have unique compute requirements, isolation between tenants, networking that connects to tools and APIs, and infrastructure that scales with unpredictable workloads. In this builders session, deploy an agentic AI application on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate and take advantage of what containers give you, including task isolation, unlimited runtime for long-running agent conversations, VPC networking for secure tool access, and Service Connect for multi-agent communication. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.title: Production-ready Lambda: Security and performance patterns
sessions.abstract: A Lambda function that handles traffic well in prototype isn't necessarily production-ready—there's a gap between "works" and "hardened." In this builders' session, take a working Lambda function and add the security and performance layers that production demands. You'll implement least-privilege IAM policies, add request validation and secrets management, reduce cold start duration with SnapStart and right-sized memory, and configure reserved concurrency for predictable performance under load. Each change includes the trade-off: what you gain, what it costs, and when to skip it. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Proof of What You Know: Building Trust in an AI Skills Economy (sponsored by Pearson)
sessions.abstract: As AI reshapes hiring and learning, proving what you know is becoming just as important as proving who you are. Pearson's digital wallet vision connects verified credentials, skills, and identity into a trusted, portable record that learners can use across certification, education, and employment journeys, helping employers and institutions move beyond self-reported claims to verified evidence of capability. This presentation is brought to you by Pearson, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Protect EKS and ECS workloads without chasing pod IPs
sessions.abstract: Pod IPs in Kubernetes change constantly as containers scale and restart, making IP-based firewall rules brittle and hard to maintain. In this lightning talk, learn how container attribute-based rules in AWS Network Firewall let you write policy using native attributes like namespaces, cluster names, and labels instead of ephemeral IPs. We'll show how a container association auto-discovers matching pods, refreshes IP mappings in near real-time, and enriches alert logs with container context for faster troubleshooting and audit. Bring the same Layer 7 inspection, FQDN filtering, and managed IDS/IPS protections you already trust to your Amazon EKS and ECS workloads.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

sessions.title: Protecting hundreds of accounts from one place with AWS Backup
sessions.abstract: Protecting a single workload is straightforward. But when every team owns their own accounts, organizations need a centralized approach to enforce consistent data protection across all of them. We'll dig into how to build backup architectures that scale across your entire AWS estate, covering Organizations backup policies to enforce protection standards across accounts, cross-account and cross-region copy strategies, and Backup Audit Manager for compliance monitoring and audit evidence. Whether you're onboarding new accounts or tightening controls on existing ones, we'll walk through patterns for centralized data protection you can prove.

sessions.title: Protect, recover, validate: Data resiliency for AWS storage
sessions.abstract: Data protection strategies today must span workloads and prove recovery works before an incident demands it. In this workshop, you'll implement recovery and data protection strategies for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, and Amazon EBS with AWS Backup. Using a financial services application architecture, you'll configure protection mechanisms for ransomware and insider threats and execute step-by-step recovery procedures against simulated cyber threats. Recover across multiple services, validate restored data integrity, and walk away with patterns to strengthen your own recovery capabilities. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

sessions.title: Protect your analytics workloads with cross-region resilience
sessions.abstract: Explore best  practices for designing active-active and active-passive architectures for AWS analytics services including AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon Redshift and AWS Lake Formation based on your  RTO and RPO requirements. Learn how to build cross-region resilience when  Apache Iceberg tables become an integral part of your architecture, including catalog  replication and metadata synchronization. Explore real-world architectural patterns and  trade-offs for choosing the right resilience strategy.

sessions.title: Proving your defenses work: validating GuardDuty runtime detection
sessions.abstract: Your board wants to know your detections work and auditors want evidence. The only way you find out today is when something real hits. In this code talk, you;ll see us build a detection validation program that answers the question before it gets asked. We'll live-code realistic attack scenarios mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, generate the correlated signals that trigger GuardDuty runtime findings, scope detection rules to specific accounts, and interpret findings as they fire. You'll walk out with a repeatable framework your team can run after every GuardDuty update to prove coverage, not assume it.

sessions.title: Provision Desktops for Builders Faster with WorkSpaces
sessions.abstract: Builders lose days configuring environments. IT teams struggle to govern the growing sprawl of AI tools and extensions across their organization. In this session, we explore these challenges and share how Amazon WorkSpaces is approaching the builder desktop experience. We'll discuss what enterprises need to provision environments faster, maintain governance across multiple surfaces, and keep pace as AI-assisted development becomes the norm. Bring your questions.

sessions.title: Pushing AI Boundaries: Transform Marketing with Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker and AWS (sponsored by Adobe)
sessions.abstract: As generative AI matures into autonomous ecosystems, enterprise marketing demands a new era of collaboration. In this session, discover how Adobe and Amazon co-innovate to deliver next-generation AI capabilities for marketers, business practitioners, and developers. At the center of this revolution is Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, an advanced AI teammate powered by Adobe Harness. We will showcase how Coworker and its flexible, headless capabilities seamlessly unite Adobe’s deep customer experience expertise with the power of AWS. Attendees will discover how this combined innovation enables teams to transition from manual execution to goal-based, automated workflows with built-in governance. Join us to learn how this partnership helps enterprise organizations take a massive leap forward in operational effectiveness and unlock entirely new business outcomes. This presentation is brought to you by Adobe, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Put your data to work: build a knowledge assistant on Amazon Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Your data lives in documents, images, databases, warehouses, and relationships between entities. In this builders session, build a knowledge assistant that works across all of it on Amazon Bedrock. Use Managed Knowledge Bases with multimodal ingestion to handle PDFs and images, add natural-language querying over structured data, and wire in GraphRAG for questions that span connected entities. Then make it enterprise-ready: secure tenant isolation, concurrency-aware ingestion, and the Agentic Retrieval API for multi-hop, cited answers. Leave with a deployed stack and retrieval patterns you can reuse across your organization.

sessions.title: PyTorch optimizations: Faster AI and lower costs with AWS Graviton
sessions.abstract: Explore the latest PyTorch optimizations for Arm-based hardware, from improved kernel performance on AWS Graviton to faster training and inference at lower compute cost. We cover real benchmark results, the open-source contributions driving these improvements, and what it looks like to run modern AI workloads on Arm today. Whether you are tuning a model, contributing upstream, or just curious about what the community has been shipping, come get a grounded view of where things stand and where they are heading.

sessions.title: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
sessions.abstract: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.

sessions.title: Quantum-proof your IoT fleet: migrate devices to Post-quantum cryptography OTA
sessions.abstract: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.

sessions.title: Queue-based decoupling trade-offs for event-driven workloads
sessions.abstract:
Every decoupling pattern makes trade-offs, and the right one depends on your workload's constraints. In this session, you work through scenarios with competing demands: exactly-once processing, tenant isolation, back pressure, and ordering. Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why.

Bring your laptop to participate.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

sessions.title: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
sessions.abstract: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.

sessions.title: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
sessions.abstract: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic, and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session, we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.

sessions.title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
sessions.abstract: Batch  jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a  stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment  an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive  rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail  independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and  analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive  agentic AI on AWS.

Services: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)

sessions.title: Real-time AI video enrichment with AWS Elemental Inference
sessions.abstract: Retrofitting videos to add subtitles, vertical formats, social cuts, and searchable metadata often means new encoders, manual editors, and multiple integrations. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS Elemental Inference can help extend reach, enhance engagement, and improve monetization by layering subtitling, vertical framing, key-moment clipping, and contextual metadata onto live and on-demand video without rebuilding your stack. Learn about the benefits of a single managed service that will improve latency, quality, and lower costs for video workflows.

sessions.title: Real-world migrations: Lessons learned migrating to AWS Outposts
sessions.abstract: Organizations with data residency and digital sovereignty requirements face a critical question: how do you move workloads from on-premises infrastructure to AWS Outposts without disrupting compliance posture or operations? This Level 300 session distills lessons from migrating customers to Outposts across industries, organization sizes, and migration strategies. We walk through the processes that delivered results, the quantifiable outcomes we measured, and the critical mistakes we learned to avoid. Learn how to select the right migration approach and navigate common blockers. We also cover transitioning from first-generation to second-generation Outposts hardware.

sessions.title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Architecting AI Governance & Security at Scale
sessions.abstract: Everyone wants AI. Nobody wants to be the team that shipped it without security and governance. In this Rodeo, you'll join a team and face three demanding stakeholders: a security hawk, a data visibility champion, and a platform lead, racing to get Agentic AI live. Your team's mission: build a governance architecture that keeps all three happy. Together, you'll whiteboard, debate, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Best architecture rides away with the win.

sessions.abstract: Your data estate wasn't designed for AI agents. Nobody's was. But somewhere between your RDBMS, NoSQL clusters, and that untouchable data lake, an agentic-ready architecture waits to be built. In this Rodeo session, your team draws a challenge: a legacy warehouse needing a semantic layer, a sprawling lake needing an ontology, or a metadata mess that lets agents in without letting governance out. Your job: build a data layer that makes agents productive, keeps compliance calm, and gives analysts self-service. You'll whiteboard ontologies, debate metadata, and wire up multi-agent access against the clock. Best architecture rides away with the win.

sessions.title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Designing Agentic AI Applications
sessions.abstract: Ever stared at multiple disconnected systems held together by manual handoffs and thought, "there has to be a better way"? Agentic AI is that better way. In this hands-on Rodeo session, you team up to design an end-to-end agentic solution for a real-world scenario: multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop decision points, and MCP integration. Swap ideas with other teams, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns for turning manual chaos into autonomous workflows. Bring your A-game, the best design rides off with the win.

sessions.title: re:Architecture Rodeo: Transforming Customer Experience with AI
sessions.abstract: "Your call is important to us." Nobody believes that anymore, and neither do your customers. Contact centers are being rebuilt around AI, and getting the architecture right is what separates the experiences people love from the ones they dread. In this Rodeo session, you'll join a team and design the transformation yourself: voice AI that understands people, routing that knows why they're calling, and handoffs to humans that don't start with "can you repeat your issue?" You'll whiteboard, swap ideas with teammates, and build against the clock, pressure-test your architecture with expert coaches, and walk away with reusable patterns. Saddle up! The design that finally makes "your call is important to us" true rides off with the win.

sessions.title: Rebuild a legacy ETL pipeline as serverless with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Enterprise data teams maintain ETL pipelines built on legacy tools like stored procedures, custom bash scripts, IBM DataStage and others, that resist migration due to undocumented dependencies. In this builders' session, use AWS Transform Custom to discover and map an existing ETL pipeline, generate a modernization blueprint, and rebuild it as a serverless workflow using AWS Glue and Step Functions. Each attendee picks one legacy source module (stored procedures, bash/SQL scripts, or DataStage jobs etc) and works hands-on through discovery, transformation logic analysis, and deploying a modernized pipeline.
