sessions.title: Rebuild CI for AI coding agents with content based caching (sponsored by RWX)
sessions.abstract: Continuous integration was designed around human pace. A developer pushes a branch, a webhook fires, and a ten minute wait feels acceptable. AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. Learn which parts of a pipeline are structurally slow and which are simply misconfigured. This presentation is brought to you by RWX, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Rebuilding a Platform's Foundation on DynamoDB Streams and Lambda
sessions.abstract: Our platform had single points of failure baked into its original design. In this session, I walk through how we closed those gaps across all five AWS Well-Architected pillars: moving event-driven workloads onto DynamoDB Streams and Lambda, cutting costs through smarter data tiering, and building the observability needed to trust the new design under real operational pressure.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

sessions.title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
sessions.abstract: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.

times.room: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

sessions.title: Recovering AWS Graviton workloads with orchestrated DR
sessions.abstract: You moved to AWS Graviton for better price-performance, but is your disaster recovery keeping pace? A recovery that lands on the wrong architecture, or brings tiers up out of order, turns a routine failover into an outage. In this chalk talk, whiteboard with disaster recovery experts how AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) now protects Graviton-based (arm64) Linux servers and recovers them onto Graviton instances, keeping the architecture intact end to end with nothing extra to configure. Then design a recovery plan that brings your application back tier by tier, in the right order, with wait times and critical-server gates. Bring your toughest arm64 and recovery-order questions, and leave with a DR design you can drill on Monday.

sessions.title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
sessions.abstract:
AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards.

Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Red team CTF: when auth and guardrails aren't enough
sessions.abstract: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. After each breach, you enable the real fix and verify the attack fails. You will compete on a live leaderboard and leave with a fully hardened agent and a defense-in-depth playbook.

sessions.title: Red teaming Aurora and gen AI: offense, defense, response
sessions.abstract: Databases and generative AI workloads are high-value targets that demand continuous adversarial testing. In this session, learn how AWS red team engineers use AI to discover innovative ways to strengthen Amazon Aurora and other cloud-native database services against modern threats. Explore how red team findings shape architectural decisions that contain blast radius by design, and how AI-augmented detection and response mechanisms close the loop at machine speed. Learn a practical framework for red teaming cloud environments and AI systems, designing for assumed breach, and building response capabilities that match the velocity of modern threats.

times.room: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

sessions.title: Reduce EKS cluster compute costs with EC2 Flex instances
sessions.abstract: Container orchestration promises to improve resource utilization, but often we find ourselves with nodes that over-provision CPU, and therefore overspend. This might happen when our workloads have a high memory footprint, or when the number of replicas is driven by resilience targets and not actual load. In this session, we'll learn how easy it is to save cost in these situations without losing performance by taking advantage of EC2 Flex instances (e.g., C8i-flex, M8i-flex, R8i-flex). You'll migrate existing EKS cluster nodes, monitor relevant metrics, and measure the actual cost improvement.

sessions.title: Reduce incident response time on Amazon ECS with AI observability
sessions.abstract: You get paged. Your ECS service is returning errors. You open six tabs, task logs, ALB metrics, deployment history, CloudWatch alarms, container health and start piecing together a timeline by hand. In this chalk talk, explore how AI-powered observability changes that workflow. See how CloudWatch Investigations ingests your existing telemetry, correlates signals across services and infrastructure, and produces root cause analysis in minutes instead of hours. Discuss how to structure logs and metrics so automated investigation actually works, and how Managed Daemons keep your collectors consistent without redeploying applications. Bring your incident response questions for an open discussion.

sessions.title: Reduce LLM inference costs up to 80% through caching with Valkey
sessions.abstract: LLM inference depends on limited GPU memory, and a KV cache lets agentic AI applications reuse computed intermediate states across prompts to reduce latency and costs. In this talk, we explain how KV caching works and walk through a production architecture using Valkey as a high-performance datastore, LMCache for KV reuse at inference, and llm-d for cache-aware routing. You will leave with practical implementation guidance and a framework for evaluating when a KV caching tier is the right choice to reduce costs for your AI applications.

sessions.title: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
sessions.abstract: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Redshift Graviton instances deliver up to 35% better price-performance, accelerating workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.

sessions.title: Reduce spend and data movement with Amazon Redshift Data Sharing and Graviton
sessions.abstract: Organizations sharing data across business units often rely on slow, error-prone ETL jobs that create costly duplication. Amazon Redshift Data Sharing enables secure, live access across provisioned and serverless warehouses — within or across accounts and regions — eliminating data movement entirely. Additionally, Redshift Graviton instances deliver up to 35% better price-performance, accelerating workloads on Apache Iceberg tables through optimized columnar processing and parallel I/O. In this session, learn how to break down data silos with cross-warehouse data sharing and boost open data lakehouse performance with Redshift on Graviton.

sessions.title: Reduce token costs by caching inference results on ElastiCache
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent AI systems now orchestrate complex workflows requiring frequent foundation model calls. In this session, learn how you can reduce latencies to single-digit milliseconds from single-digit seconds with for Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in agentic AI applications using semantic and KV caching, while also reducing the cost incurred from your foundation models for production workloads. By implementing these caching strategies in agentic architectures like RAG-powered assistants and autonomous agents, customers can create performant and cost-effective production-scale agentic AI systems.

sessions.title: Reducing Lambda cost with Graviton and managed instances
sessions.abstract: Lambda's default x86 pricing works fine until your steady-state workloads make the per-invocation model expensive at scale. In this builders' session, start with a baseline workload and apply two cost levers: migrate to ARM64 (Graviton) for better price-performance, then deploy on Lambda Managed Instances for EC2 economics with multi-concurrency on steady-state traffic. You'll measure before-and-after cost and performance data at each step, evaluate when each approach makes sense versus default Lambda pricing, and leave with a repeatable migration playbook. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Re-Engineer Enterprise Processes for Agentic AI on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (sponsored by Camunda)
sessions.abstract: Enterprise AI is moving from experimentation to production, but legacy workflows designed without AI in mind keep agents disconnected from the processes, systems, and controls that determine successful business outcomes. Understand why reengineering now matters: organizations that preserve legacy workflows risk slowing AI adoption while others redesign operations for an AI first world. Discover how Camunda ProcessOS works with Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to discover, re-engineer, and improve end-to-end processes. See how Camunda’s agentic orchestration combines deterministic controls with dynamic AI agents, human approval, observability, and auditability. Learn why you need to re-engineer now, and stop adding agents to yesterday’s workflows. This presentation is brought to you by Camunda, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Refactor your monolith for multi-tenancy and agentic AI in one pass
sessions.abstract: Most ISV monoliths get modernized in three sequential passes: refactor, then multi-tenant, then agentic. Three trips through the same code, each longer than the last. In this chalk talk, we'll dig into the unified refactor pattern that makes tenancy and agentic bets in the same window. We'll explore how data partitioning decisions shift when agents are also a target, when Amazon EKS becomes the substrate for both migrations, and which patterns create more debt than they solve when combined wrong. Leave with a framework for the one refactor window you can afford. Bring your questions.

sessions.title: Regulation to Innovation: A Global Enterprise Guide to Digital Sovereignty (sponsored by Accenture)
sessions.abstract: Digital sovereignty is a growing priority for global enterprises operating across Europe as they navigate regulatory requirements, geopolitical uncertainty, and increasing demand for cloud and AI innovation. Organizations must balance data residency, compliance, resilience, and business agility without slowing transformation. Learn how leading enterprises are using AWS European Sovereign Cloud as part of a broader cloud strategy to meet sovereignty requirements while continuing to adopt modern cloud services and AI. Accenture will share practical approaches to assessing sovereignty needs, designing compliant architectures, and integrating sovereign cloud capabilities into enterprise environments. Attendees will leave with actionable guidance for balancing trust, resilience, compliance, and innovation at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Reimagine legacy apps to be agentic AI ready with AWS Transform & Kiro
sessions.abstract: Enterprise core applications were built for stability, not agentic AI. Tightly coupled dependencies across mainframe and interconnected systems make it nearly impossible to add intelligent capabilities without rearchitecting. In this workshop, take a legacy application through the full modernization journey: scope it, reverse-engineer existing behavior with AWS Transform, classify logic into deterministic microservices and AI agents, design target layers with Kiro, build the agentic layer on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, then deploy and validate. Leave with hands-on experience rebuilding a legacy application into an architecture ready for agentic AI. Laptop required.

sessions.abstract: Explore how Generative AI, powered by Proximie and AWS, is fundamentally reshaping the operating room. This session will detail how computer vision and LLMs are creating the OR of the future, supported by Deloitte, to improve productivity and treat more patients in UK NHS Trusts. Attendees will gain insights into the practical application of this powerful alliance and why this innovative approach is vital for the future of healthcare. sessions.title: Reinvent cloud security with runtime and AI (sponsored by Upwind)
sessions.abstract: This session explores the evolution of cloud security and why traditional approaches fall short in the era of ephemeral compute and agentic AI. While legacy CloudSec relied on static scanning for visibility, today’s environments are dynamic, real-time, and increasingly autonomous, resulting in blind spots, excessive noise, and incomplete protection. We’ll examine how AI-driven and hybrid cloud architectures introduce new challenges across visibility, protection, and validation, from cross-provider gaps to real-time attack vectors and model vulnerabilities. To address this, Cloud and AI security must move beyond static analysis to a unified, runtime-driven approach. By continuously monitoring activity across the environment and embedding security throughout the SDLC, including production, organizations gain real-time context, better prioritization, and proactive threat mitigation. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Reliable data processing with AWS serverless services
sessions.abstract: In this chalk talk, learn how to optimize your serverless data processing workflows at scale. We cover AWS Step Functions Distributed Map for massive parallel batch processing and AWS Lambda durable functions for durable execution workflows. See how to combine these with Lambda event source mappings for stream and queue processing. We discuss cost optimization strategies and when to choose each approach for your data workload.

sessions.title: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
sessions.abstract: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.

sessions.title: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
sessions.abstract: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. We built a different path: Ingesting policy, using Large Language Models, and building a formal logic representation, followed by using neurosymbolic techniques to produce a verified rule set, enabling deterministic eligibility decisions with full audit trails. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

sessions.abstract: Intel and Databricks are collaborating to optimize price-performance for workloads running on AWS. This session covers optimizations for ISVs running Photon/Spark on Databricks leveraging custom Amazon EC2 instances powered by Intel Xeon processors, delivering advanced AI capabilities and high core density. sessions.title: Resilience for Data Foundations: The Lessons Iceberg Forced Us to Learn (sponsored by Commvault)
sessions.abstract: When customers needed to recover Iceberg environments in production, we discovered that restoring data was often the easy part. Preserving metadata, table state, consistency, and downstream dependencies proved far more challenging than we expected. In this session, Clumio's product and engineering leaders share the assumptions that didn't survive production, the recovery scenarios that surprised us most, and the architectural lessons that emerged along the way. Leave with practical guidance for designing more resilient data foundations on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Commvault, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
sessions.abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn’t there? In this session we discuss Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. We’ll walk through the trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. We’ll ground the discussion in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, but the takeaway is portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don’t fully control.

sessions.title: Resilience starts where your assumptions end, feat. Autodesk
sessions.abstract: The challenge most companies face is knowing where they stand with resilience, being willing to validate their assumptions safely, and disciplined enough to continuously improve without slowing delivery. In this session, we walk through Autodesk's journey with resilience testing and automated recovery failover as proof that investing in validation pays off, and you leave with a repeatable lifecycle for turning your own assumptions into proven capabilities. Discover how the next-generation AWS Resilience Hub handles the tedious work like mapping dependencies, assessing posture, and preconfiguring resilience tests, leaving your teams to focus on closing the gap between the system you think you operate and the one you actually do.

sessions.title: Resilient by design: Simplifying last-mile connectivity with AWS
sessions.abstract: Establishing resilient private connectivity from data centers and branch offices to AWS has traditionally required weeks of partner coordination, physical cross-connects, and manual resilience configurations. Yet true resilience demands more than provisioning a second connection. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how AWS Direct Connect and AWS Interconnect each address location diversity, device diversity, BGP routing policy, and failover validation. Compare dedicated links with full routing control to fully managed connections with built-in redundancy, explore integration with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN, and evaluate maximum versus high resiliency models. Bring your hybrid connectivity challenges.

sessions.abstract: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.

sessions.title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
sessions.abstract: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

sessions.title: Resolve Amazon ECS incidents faster with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

sessions.abstract: Follow an issue from detection to resolution. In this builder's session, see how AWS DevOps Agent investigates incidents across AWS, multicloud, and on-premises environments, analyzing telemetry and correlating signals to pinpoint root causes and deliver targeted remediation. Then use the AWS DevOps Agent release management agent to review the code changes for production readiness before they reach your customers. Every review is informed by production intelligence that AWS DevOps Agent continuously builds from your environment.

sessions.title: Resolve it all: Build hybrid DNS architectures on AWS
sessions.abstract: Your enterprise runs workloads across multiple Amazon VPCs while maintaining connectivity to on-premises data centers, and DNS is the glue holding it all together. In this workshop, build a realistic hybrid DNS architecture using the latest Amazon Route 53 capabilities. Participants will learn how to centralize DNS configurations with Route 53 Profiles, replace conditional forwarding rules with native delegation using Resolver Delegation Endpoints, detect and block DNS-based threats with DNS Firewall, and enable secure authenticated resolution for distributed clients with Route 53 Global Resolver. Bring your laptop and resolve hybrid DNS once and for all.

sessions.title: Responsible AI Enablement: Balancing Innovation, Governance and Control (sponsored by Island)
sessions.abstract: Most organizations are currently stuck between two worlds: the urgent need to adopt AI to remain competitive, & the critical mandate to protect corporate data & reputation. AI is evolving faster than any tool in IT history, and faster than any organization can keep up with. The temptation to simply block access to AI is strong, but just saying "No" means ceding the advantage to those able to say "Yes!". The 3 Pillars of a "Secure Yes": Visibility: Knowing what AI is being used across the org. Accountability: Defining who owns the data & the output. Resilience: Building frameworks that adapt as regulations change. In this session, we will outline the framework for secure AI adoption. We will move past the hype to discuss how leaders can build visibility, maintain accountability, and foster a culture of responsible innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Island, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera)
sessions.abstract: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
sessions.abstract: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. With the new AWS SDK for Python, async is native, concurrent calls no longer require thread-pool workarounds, and bidirectional streaming enables use cases like live transcription and speech-to-speech that go beyond what's available in boto3 today. Follow along as we put those capabilities to work with clean concurrent calls, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Transcribe streaming, and a practical path to migrating your own code to the new SDK.

sessions.title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
sessions.abstract: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Replay, request-response, ordering, and high throughput increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Through a real CQRS architecture, we build a practical decision framework for when to choose messaging, streaming, or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.

sessions.title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
sessions.abstract: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

sessions.title: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
sessions.abstract: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.

sessions.title: Right-size and scale Amazon ECS with effective autoscaling patterns
sessions.abstract: Autoscaling containerized workloads means scaling both tasks and the infrastructure underneath them. This chalk talk explores Amazon ECS autoscaling patterns including target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling across AWS Fargate and Amazon ECS Managed Instances. Understand how these patterns interact with capacity providers so you can balance performance against cost. Discuss right-sizing tasks, handling traffic spikes, and avoiding over-provisioning. Bring your scaling challenges for an interactive technical discussion.

sessions.abstract: Your telemetry is scattered across tools. Your storage costs keep climbing. Your AI agents are a black box. Ask how our purpose-built log analytics engine reduces cost while boosting query performance. Ask how to unify logs, traces, and metrics into a single OpenTelemetry-native pane of glass with cost efficiency. If you're building AI agents, ask how to trace LLM calls, track per-invocation cost, and debug multi-agent workflows. And for any workload, ask how to stack cost levers like right-sizing, tiered storage, and writeable warm to maximize savings.

sessions.title: Right tool, right layer: Combining ML models and autonomous agents
sessions.abstract: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.

sessions.title: Right workload on the right cloud - multicloud workload placement
sessions.abstract: You operate a multicloud organization, and every new workload raises the same challenge: which cloud should this workload run on? Too often the answer comes down to habit, existing vendor relationships, or whoever argues loudest, and workloads end up somewhere that adds complexity, risk, or complicates compliance. In this session you will learn how to approach multicloud workload placement so that the decisions you make are explainable, repeatable and auditable.

sessions.title: Ring's Security Evolution: From Doorbell to Enterprise Platform (sponsored by Ring LLC)
sessions.abstract: Ring started with a simple mission: make neighborhoods safer with a video doorbell. That mission has scaled — from 100M+ residential cameras to SMB storefronts and jobsites with mobile security towers, to an AI-powered Appstore unlocking entirely new use cases across elder care, workforce analytics, and beyond. Now, Ring is making its boldest leap yet: a cloud-native enterprise platform built on AWS, combining video management, intelligent alerting, third-party camera ingestion, and access control. Join this lightning round to trace Ring's evolution and see what's next for enterprise security. This presentation is brought to you by Ring LLC, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
sessions.abstract: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture behind AWS Specialist Agent: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.

sessions.title: Routing events at scale with Amazon EventBridge
sessions.abstract: Amazon EventBridge simplifies event routing for distributed applications. In this chalk talk, explore how to centralize multi-account event routing without custom infrastructure. We discuss routing policies, event discovery with schema registry, and access controls that let platform teams govern while app teams move independently. We also explore rate limiting and backpressure so your applications gracefully handle traffic spikes and protect downstream systems without losing events.

sessions.title: Running AI agents you can trust on Amazon EKS
sessions.abstract: AI agents are rapidly moving from prototype to production, and running them at scale presents new challenges. Untrusted, AI-generated code executes in your environment. Many agents share the same infrastructure. Workloads spin up, act, and tear down constantly. Join this session to learn how to run agents securely on Amazon EKS with VM-level isolation, wire up the primitives agents need for tools, memory, and orchestration, and manage fleets of short-lived, bursty workloads. You'll also see how the same EKS platform you run your critical workloads on extends into the agentic era and where we're headed next.

sessions.title: Running compute-efficient workloads on Amazon EKS Auto Mode
sessions.abstract: Amazon EKS Auto Mode, powered by open source Karpenter, simplifies infrastructure management while optimizing compute resources. Karpenter provisions Amazon EC2 Instances based on the requirements of your workload. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll gain practical experience in advanced workload scheduling, continually compute optimization with Karpenter consolidation, explore AWS Graviton and AWS spare capacity through Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Whether you’re new to EKS Auto Mode, or an experienced operator you’ll learn best practices for running efficient workloads on Amazon EKS while simplifying Kubernetes cluster management.

sessions.title: Running larger, higher-fidelity quantum experiments on Amazon Braket
sessions.abstract: Amazon Braket offers access to the latest trapped-ion quantum hardware alongside advanced error mitigation techniques, unlocking the largest, highest-fidelity quantum workloads on the platform. In this chalk talk, we demonstrate how error mitigation combines noise-aware transpilation and error suppression to expand usable circuit volume, and how trapped-ion connectivity enables deeper, more complex circuits. We will whiteboard a real workload to estimate cost, runtime, and expected fidelity gains.

sessions.title: Running SAN workloads on Amazon EBS
sessions.abstract: Amazon EBS delivers the performance, durability, and enterprise features that mission-critical SAN workloads depend on. In this session, learn how the latest EBS capabilities map to what you run on premises today, which workloads are the best fit, and how customers are moving databases and enterprise applications off storage arrays and onto EBS. Leave with practical guidance to get started.

sessions.title: Running untrusted code in sandboxes with AWS Lambda MicroVMs
sessions.abstract: AI coding assistants generate code. Customers upload plugins. Third parties submit extensions. All of it needs to run somewhere and that somewhere can't be your production environment. In this builders' session, use AWS Lambda MicroVMs to build secure sandboxes that execute untrusted code at scale with hardware-level tenant isolation. You'll configure sandbox lifecycle management, implement resource limits and permissions boundaries, and test failure modes when code misbehaves. Walk away with a working isolation architecture you can adapt for your own multi-tenant workloads. Bring your laptop.

sessions.title: Running Vercel in Your Own AWS Account (sponsored by Vercel)
sessions.abstract: This session explores how Vercel Enterprise customers can run workloads in their own AWS account while continuing to use the Vercel developer experience. You’ll learn about the separation between the Vercel control plane and customer runtime, and why this model can help organizations meet data privacy, security, and compliance requirements. You’ll see how the setup works through a live walkthrough and demo, and how this architecture can support broader access to tools like v0, Amazon Q, and other coding agents. This presentation is brought to you by Vercel, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Run your largest SAP HANA on AWS: EC2 High Memory deep dive
sessions.abstract: Running SAP HANA at scale requires infrastructure that matches the size and criticality of your Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) workloads. EC2 High Memory instances deliver capacity from 256 GB to 32 TB, backed by the AWS Nitro architecture for consistent performance and hardware-level isolation. In this session, we deep dive into the Nitro design powering these instances and hear how customers are scaling production ERP to 32 TB on AWS. Walk away with architectural guidance and real-world deployment patterns for running your largest HANA workloads in a scale-up configuration.

sessions.title: SaaS Agents Anywhere
sessions.abstract: Customers make deliberate choices about where their workloads run. For SaaS vendors delivering agentic products, that means the runtime has to meet the workload where it is, not the other way around. This chalk talk teaches the everywhere agent pattern for SaaS: keep the control plane on AWS, run the agent runtime and data-plane execution wherever the customer's data lives. Learn three decisions: which destinations to support and when (multi-cloud, on-prem, or both), how to run agent runtimes outside AWS without rewriting your control plane (packaging, model backend selection, dependency portability), and how to manage identity, observability, and lifecycle across environments you don't own. Leave with the decision framework for shipping SaaS agents anywhere the customer's data lives.

sessions.title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
sessions.abstract: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. Once customers have data residency or cost-visibility requirements, deployment topology determines the operational pattern. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

sessions.title: Safer, simpler, faster upgrades with managed blue/green deployments
sessions.abstract: Blue/green deployments for Amazon Aurora and Amazon RDS simplify the process of upgrading and performing maintenance on your databases. In this chalk talk, you will architect a blue/green database upgrade solution to support major or minor engine version upgrades and perform schema changes with minimal and predictable downtime. Active participation is encouraged as you architect a solution to meet your requirements. In open discussion, learn the trade-offs involved in database management when using blue/green deployments and how to design the most effective upgrade solution to meet your needs.

sessions.title: Same code, any compute: Portable architecture on AWS
sessions.abstract: Your business logic shouldn't be coupled to a compute service. In this session, apply Hexagonal Architecture and 12-factor patterns to design workloads where compute is a deployment decision, not an architectural one. Through live code, see the same logic packaged as a Lambda function, a Fargate task, and an EKS pod using AWS Lambda Web Adapter and runtime-neutral handler patterns. You'll learn where portability pays off, where it adds unnecessary abstraction, and how to evaluate the trade-offs between pay-per-request, always-on containers, and orchestrated clusters for your workloads.

sessions.title: Sandboxing AI Agents on EKS: Isolation That Scales
sessions.abstract: AI agents execute untrusted code — one prompt injection away from data exfiltration. This session covers building graduated isolation for autonomous agents on EKS using the agent-sandbox controller. You'll learn why runtime tiers (runc → gVisor → Firecracker) map to different threat models, how SandboxClaim resources manage ephemeral agent lifecycle, and Cilium FQDN egress filtering that prevents exfiltration without blocking legitimate tool use. We'll whiteboard Karpenter NodePool design for gVisor-capable nodes, discuss cost tradeoffs between isolation levels, and share what breaks when you over-isolate. Leave with a production-ready isolation framework.

sessions.title: SAST Is Dead: Program Analysis for AI Agents (sponsored by Semgrep)
sessions.abstract: LLMs didn't kill security testing, they exposed tools that guess at context they don't have. This talk explains what we learned by reinventing program analysis for new end users: builders and agents. We had to develop benchmarks and add determinism with program slicing to better control costs and deliver the optimal price per true vulnerability detected. This presentation is brought to you by Semgrep, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: When adversaries move in seconds, security has to move faster. CrowdStrike shares how they built scalable, real-time LLM inference on Amazon SageMaker to power threat detection at massive scale, where sub-second latency is a hard requirement. Learn how dedicated, configurable endpoints gave them full control over performance, while SageMaker AI's managed infrastructure removed the operational overhead. Walk away with a blueprint for running latency-critical workloads on SageMaker Managed Inference, without running the stack yourself.

sessions.title: Scale AI-powered software development securely with Bedrock
sessions.abstract: Your dev teams are adopting AI coding agents fast: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, open-source agents, and more. Without a shared platform, every team rolls its own auth, its own cost tracking, its own rules. In this builders session, build one platform on Amazon Bedrock that manages all of them. Package your security policies, coding standards, and delivery practices as reusable plugins, agent skills, and MCP servers, then apply consistent identity, sandboxing, observability, and cost controls across every agent. See a team onboard and take an issue from plan to tested change. Leave with a working reference architecture.

sessions.title: Scale data for RAG and AI agents cost-effectively with Amazon S3 Vectors
sessions.abstract: Discover how S3 Vectors transforms retrieval workloads for AI agents and RAG pipelines with native vector storage and query capabilities. This session explores recent enhancements that deliver deeper, more comprehensive search results per query while dramatically reducing costs at scale, reducing the need for multiple round trips while running large-scale RAG, semantic search, and AI workloads. Learn architecture best practices, performance optimization techniques, and diverse vector use cases, from semantic search to large-scale RAG implementations.

sessions.title: Scale financial risk simulations with AWS Batch and Amazon ECS
sessions.abstract: Financial institutions run millions of simulations overnight to price options, stress-test portfolios, and satisfy regulators. Scaling those workloads means balancing queue depth against compute cost. AWS Batch on Amazon ECS eliminates that tradeoff — containers scale elastically, Spot instances cut compute cost, and job orchestration handles retries and memory tuning without custom scripts. In this chalk talk, walk through a production architecture where a quantitative hedge fund runs its entire research compute on AWS Batch. Then open the whiteboard and discuss how to apply these patterns to your own pricing engines, VaR calculations, or scenario analysis workloads.

sessions.title: Scale, optimize and deploy inference with Karpenter and EKS Auto Mode
sessions.abstract: Accelerated workloads make node provisioning challenging. Picking the wrong instance, scheduling constraint, or disruption policy impacts GPU utilization and drives up costs. This deep dive covers how Amazon EKS provisions and scales accelerated compute for real inference workloads, whether you run managed Auto Mode or self-managed Karpenter. See how both select across GPU and accelerator families and honor topology-aware scheduling. Learn the NodePool and disruption settings that keep utilization high without hurting latency-sensitive serving. Discover how Dynamic Resource Allocation and GPU sharing squeeze more inference out of every device, plus accelerator-aware node repair that keeps long-running jobs healthy.

sessions.title: Scale production agents reliably with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: What changes when you go from ten agent sessions to ten thousand? In this chalk talk, whiteboard the architectural and operational patterns that determine whether your agents perform reliably at scale. Discuss microVM isolation for secure multi-tenancy, elastic scaling that handles traffic spikes without capacity planning, and long-running task handling with human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Cover resiliency patterns: what happens when a tool call fails, how to handle model timeouts, and designing for graceful degradation. Walk through the infrastructure decisions you make once and benefit from forever. Bring your scaling scenarios and we architect solutions together.

sessions.title: Scale reinforcement learning globally with sparse weight updates (sponsored by Modal)
sessions.abstract: Reinforcement learning post training usually keeps trainers and rollout workers in one tightly coupled GPU cluster. This talk shows how to keep backpropagation on fast local fabric while moving independent rollout workers to elastic GPU capacity across regions and clouds. The key is to diff weights in the precision actually served, then publish lossless sparse version transitions instead of full checkpoints. Attendees will learn why Adam/Muon updates often disappear under BF16 rounding, how version aware sidecars commit exact weight versions, and how this architecture turns globally available inference capacity into practical reinforcement learning capacity. This presentation is brought to you by Modal, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Scale Through Partners: The Partner-Led SMB Growth Engine
sessions.abstract: SMB is a $1T opportunity—98% of global businesses are small/mid-size, 81% are increasing AI spend, yet fewer than 300 AWS partners hold the SMB Competency. This session unpacks AWS's Indirect Selling engine: new incentives aligned to growth, AI-powered lead generation, SMB solution selling, and a Partnership Maturity Framework turning opportunistic engagement into repeatable business practice. You'll leave with unit economics proving indirect selling reaches SMBs globally, a clear activation timeline from Opportunity through full Business Practice, and specific first moves to build a scalable, profitable SMB practice on AWS—your 20-minute roadmap to outsized growth.

sessions.title: Scale your coding agents beyond the laptop with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Developers want Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro with laptop-like feel but without laptop limits: no parallelism, no persistence, no isolation. In this hands-on workshop, you will deploy a coding agent to AgentCore's runtime in three commands, then build real workflows: a code review agent, PR automation, and a repo consolidation job. You will run agents in parallel across isolated microVMs, persist and share state with BYO S3 and EFS, connect models through Bedrock, and wire an agent to wake on GitHub events and work in the background. Leave with working code you can drop straight into your own repos.

sessions.title: Scaling agent memory with Amazon S3 Vectors and S3 Files
sessions.abstract: Persistent, scalable memory is foundational to production AI agents. In this session, learn how the combination of S3 Vectors and S3 Files provides a unified memory layer for agents by using S3 Vectors for embedding-based semantic recall and S3 Files for low-latency, mutable working memory and shared state across agent sessions. We’ll cover architecture patterns for short-term and long-term memory, multi-agent memory sharing, and managing memory lifecycle and cost as usage grows, including how recent S3 Vectors enhancements improve retrieval economics at scale. Leave with patterns for memory architectures that scale to millions of agent interactions.

sessions.title: Scaling AI Defenses with AWS and CrowdStrike (sponsored by CrowdStrike)
sessions.abstract: AI is accelerating innovation — and accelerating attackers. From prompt injection and data exfiltration to cloud privilege escalation, adversaries are increasingly exploiting AI-powered architectures to move faster than traditional defenses. In this session, AWS and CrowdStrike experts will demonstrate how organizations can securely build and defend modern AI workloads running on AWS. Attendees will explore real-world architectures using Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore and see how attackers move across identity, cloud, and AI services to exploit security gaps. Through live demonstrations and architectural guidance, the session will show how AWS and CrowdStrike help organizations surface shadow AI; visualize attack paths across code and AI services; stop AI-specific attacks; automate protection workflows; and deliver real-time cloud detection and response (CDR) across modern AI environments. This presentation is brought to you by CrowdStrike, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Scaling and securing MCP Servers with AWS Load Balancing and WAF
sessions.abstract: MCP servers are becoming essential infrastructure in enterprise AI environments, and running them in production demands both scalability and security. Join this chalk talk to explore patterns for scaling and securing your MCP servers using AWS native services. We'll cover how to configure Application Load Balancer for MCP traffic characteristics, implement health checks and routing policies, and scale horizontally across availability zones. We'll also cover how to enforce security controls with AWS WAF, including request filtering, rate limiting, and tool-level access policies. Whether you're running a handful of MCP servers or deploying at enterprise scale, you'll leave with actionable architectures for production-ready deployments.

sessions.title: Scaling EC2 Spot with a focus on capacity, GPUs, and allocation
sessions.abstract: Today, organizations run ML training, inference, and large-scale simulations on Spot across CPU and GPU instance families. But scaling Spot successfully requires understanding how capacity actually behaves. In this session, the EC2 Spot product leader shares what the data reveals: which diversification strategies consistently deliver high fill rates, how allocation strategies differ for CPU vs. GPU workloads, and when tools like Spot Placement Score and EC2 Capacity Manager make the difference. You'll leave with a modern playbook covering instance diversification, multi-Region/AZ deployment, checkpointing for long-running jobs, and capacity rebalancing patterns the largest Spot customers use today.

sessions.title: Scaling ElastiCache globally: 400+ clusters & 1.3 trillion ops/day
sessions.abstract: Managing ride-hailing demand across 1,100+ cities and 8+ million daily transactions in real time requires scalable, resilient, sub-millisecond in-memory data operations. In this session, learn how inDrive evolved from a monolithic on-premises Redis OSS cluster to over 400 distributed Amazon ElastiCache clusters spanning 8 AWS Regions, executing 1.3 trillion operations daily. Discover how inDrive eliminated bottlenecks in single-CPU utilization, network saturation, and hotspot shards, and how a zero-downtime migration to the Valkey engine on ElastiCache improved performance and reduced costs. Learn a production-tested blueprint for scaling data-intensive systems across multiple AWS Regions.

sessions.title: Scaling inference compute across clusters (sponsored by Baseten)
sessions.abstract: Your traffic outgrows a single cluster long before you expect it to. Colin McGrath explains how Baseten runs inference across more than 80 GPU clusters and roughly 15 cloud providers as one system: how capacity gets found and claimed, how requests get routed to the right region under real load, how large models get delivered to new clusters quickly, and how autoscaling behaves when traffic is bursty and cold starts are expensive. He covers what happens when a whole region goes down, and the patterns that matter most for teams scaling past one cluster. This presentation is brought to you by Baseten, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Scaling interactive generative AI at Netflix with AWS Local Zones
sessions.abstract: Generative AI VFX and Animation teams at Netflix require the latest GPU hardware for creative workflows, including real-time rendering, VFX editorial, and color correction. These workloads demand low-latency access to high-performance compute close to creative teams. AWS Local Zones make this possible by placing Amazon EC2 G7e instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs in the Los Angeles metro. Netflix's Studio GenAI Infrastructure, including GenAI Sessions and Universal Compute Service, uses Local Zones to serve just-in-time combinations of software and hardware in secure, isolated sandbox environments. Tools like ComfyUI and AI Toolkit with complex dependencies run on task-oriented, elastic GPU assignments, so Netflix scales creative AI workloads efficiently without managing physical infrastructure.

sessions.title: Scaling ISV Revenue: Accelerating Co-Sell with AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: AWS Marketplace has become the fastest path for ISVs to scale co-sell, but unlocking its full potential means going beyond procurement and using it as the backbone of how you sell. This session unpacks how high-performing ISVs combine ISV Accelerate with AWS Marketplace to accelerate co-sell. Three points separate top performers: (1) structuring AWS seller alignment to generate Marketplace-routed pipeline, (2) using private offers and channel-partner workflows to compress enterprise deal cycles by 30-40%, and (3) mining Marketplace buyer signals to drive expansion and proactive renewal. Walk away with a focused playbook for turning Marketplace into a scalable revenue motion.

sessions.abstract: Legacy application modernization is a coordination and code generation problem. A large application must be understood, verified, and integrated without losing fidelity. AWS Transform for mainframe reads legacy code and extracts its business rules into traceable specifications that describe what the application does. Learn how AWS Transform overcomes this modernization challenge, and discover the latest capabilities for scaling modernization that compress delivery from days to hours.

sessions.title: Scaling Multi-Account IAM at Netflix: Access, Visibility and Credentials
sessions.abstract: Managing IAM across a large, fast-growing AWS footprint quickly outgrows manual review — every permission change creates friction for engineers and queue time for operators. We'll cover a control-plane approach that ties together high-level IAM abstractions, automated workflows, and business context to drive the majority of AWS access needs. Developers describe intent against concrete resources instead of hand-writing JSON; Access Analyzer–backed probes auto-approve routine changes; administrators get a single pane of glass over SCPs, identity and resource policies, CloudTrail/S3 errors, and AWS Config history. Credential delivery flows through the same plane, enabling context-aware scoping for human and agentic callers alike.

sessions.title: Scaling Multi-Cluster EKS Without Burning Your Infrastructure Budget
sessions.abstract: Managing hundreds of Amazon EKS clusters breaks standard multi-tenant architectures under the weight of shared control planes, noisy neighbors, and runaway cross-AZ data transfer costs. This interactive chalk talk skips the slides to whiteboard the painful realities of multi-cluster fleet topology at scale. We will dissect the architectural trade-offs between monolithic clusters and localized micro-clusters, mapping out exact blast-radius constraints. Bring your worst infrastructure bottlenecks; we will openly debate cluster life-cycle automation, shared VPC patterns, and cost-allocation frameworks, leaving you with a battle-tested blueprint to optimize fleet operations on Monday morning.

sessions.abstract: Operational complexity doesn't scale linearly but your approach to managing it can. In this chalk talk, we'll use AWS DevOps Agent to explore three protocols shaping how operations teams work at scale: MCP (connecting to operational data and actions), ACP (delegating tasks to purpose-built agents), and A2A (coordinating across autonomous agents). We'll discuss how protocol choice affects decision-making, when to extend capabilities vs. delegate, and how to design architectures that grow with your operational footprint. Leave with a clear mental model for when to reach for each protocol and how they fit together.

Discover how Tech Mahindra helped establish trusted data foundations, harness Agentic AI to enrich product and customer master data, unlock semantic intelligence, and create governed data products that power enterprise-wide insights, including drug demand forecasting. sessions.title: Scaling website delivery with Amazon CloudFront: one configuration, many sites
sessions.abstract: Most enterprises don't run just one website. They run many: a corporate site, regional or sub-brand sites, internal portals, plus full environment tiers (Dev, QA, Staging, Prod) for each. Managing TLS certificates, WAF rules, and cache behavior separately for each creates configuration drift, inconsistent security, and operational overhead that scales with site count. In this workshop, you'll use Amazon CloudFront to define a single reusable baseline configuration and apply it consistently across many website profiles. Whether they represent different brands, business units, or environment tiers, you'll learn how to allow targeted overrides where a site genuinely needs to differ (stricter WAF on production, relaxed caching on QA, a custom origin for a sub-brand). You'll leave with a working reference architecture and a decision framework for what belongs in the baseline vs. the override.

sessions.title: Secrets rotation patterns for agentic pipelines at scale
sessions.abstract: Autonomous agents provision, consume, and rotate credentials without a human in the loop. In this chalk-talk, work through how to build a secrets lifecycle for multi-step agentic workflows: issue dynamic secrets using AWS temporary credentials and leverage AWS Secrets Manager for secrets rotation, Scope each agent with resource policies and VPC endpoint conditions to enforce a data perimeter, and apply AWS KMS envelope encryption so ephemeral secrets never persist in plaintext. Leave with deployable templates for zero-standing-privilege secret delivery across chained agent invocations.

sessions.title: Secure agents at scale on Amazon ECS with VM-level isolation
sessions.abstract: If you run agents, multi-tenant services, or regulated workloads on shared infrastructure, the isolation boundary is an important security consideration. This session shows how to design that boundary using VM-level isolation on Amazon ECS. You will leave knowing how to isolate tenants and untrusted agent workloads from one another, apply least-privilege execution toward compliance obligations, and run it all efficiently at scale. Whether you build agentic AI platforms or sensitive multi-tenant applications, you will walk away with a practical blueprint for strong isolation on ECS.

sessions.title: Secure AI Agent Access with AgentCore Identity
sessions.abstract: Not every caller should have access to your AI agents, and you should verify who is calling them before responding. In this hands-on lab, you deploy an IT help desk agent to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime and configure AgentCore Identity to enforce inbound authentication. You set up an Amazon Cognito user pool as the identity provider, obtain and decode a JSON Web Token (JWT), and test that the agent rejects unauthenticated callers while allowing verified employees through.

sessions.title: Secure AI the same way you secure everything else on AWS
sessions.abstract: You already run security and governance on AWS with IAM, CloudTrail, KMS, and VPC boundaries, and AI workloads on Bedrock inherit all of it. This chalk talk shows how: IAM scoping for model access, data perimeter policies, full prompt and response logging in CloudTrail, and KMS encryption at rest and in transit. There is no separate governance stack to learn and no new tools to onboard. You leave knowing how to extend the security patterns your organization already trusts to cover AI workloads on Bedrock.

sessions.title: Secure and modernize code simultaneously with agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Most modernization teams bolt security on as an afterthought, creating costly late-stage vulnerabilities. In this code talk, you'll follow along as we build a custom agent using Strands Agents SDK on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that takes a security-first approach. We wire up AWS Transform agents for tech debt analysis via MCP integrations, connect AWS Continuum for deep code-level vulnerability scanning, and orchestrate everything through Kiro. The result: an agent that synthesizes a security-hardened modernization plan and autonomously executes it. See AI agents collaborate in real time to transform and secure code simultaneously, eliminating handoffs between teams.

sessions.abstract: A customer runs a support agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that reaches destinations nobody reviewed and takes requests from any caller. sessions.title: Securing applications at machine speed in the frontier model era
sessions.abstract: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. AWS Continuum closes that gap with one continuous workflow: discover risks in your code, prioritize by real exploitability, validate in a sandbox with reproduction steps, and remediate at machine speed within guardrails you define. In this session, we walk through how Continuum operates end-to-end: building a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is reachable, confirming exploitability through sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generating validated fixes. You see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. You leave understanding how to move from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.

sessions.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
sessions.abstract: Multi-agent systems create  a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.

sessions.title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
sessions.abstract: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. sessions.title: Securing software and AI supply chains with Network Firewall at Coupang
sessions.abstract: Coupang, South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, runs millions of daily transactions on AWS. At that volume, each open source library, container base image, and AI model weight pulled from the internet is a supply chain risk. This session goes deep on the AWS Network Firewall architecture and its newer capabilities, including centralized management and container-aware egress inspection. Coupang shows how it built egress control that scales automatically across a container-first fleet, automates allowlist management, and limits exposure to rogue AI dependencies and dynamic payloads without slowing developers down.

sessions.title: Securing the agent loop with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
sessions.abstract: You screen the prompt on the way in and answer on the way out. In between, tool results carry external content straight into the model's context and tool arguments carry the model's decisions out to your systems, without inspection. The middle of the loop is where indirect prompt injection lands. Where you place a guardrail inside the loop is a design decision. In this chalk talk, we place Bedrock Guardrails checks inside the agent loop. We examine ApplyGuardrail and InvokeGuardrailChecks, work through where each one belongs, and look at what risk remains when the checks are in place.

sessions.title: Securing the AI-Native Cloud (sponsored by Upwind)
sessions.abstract: In this session, we will demonstrate how AI is redefining cloud security by moving beyond static posture management to real-time, context-aware protection. The session will showcase how organizations can gain continuous visibility across their environments and respond to threats as they emerge. Attendees will see how AI-driven analysis of runtime behavior enables faster detection of anomalies, prioritization of real risks, and automated response across dynamic, multi-cloud infrastructures. The session will highlight how security teams can reduce noise, strengthen security processes, and proactively respond to threats before they escalate. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong)
sessions.abstract: AI moves fast until it hits production. Then agents that looked solid in a POC start making calls they shouldn't, hammering the vector database, or failing quietly under load, because the API layer underneath wasn't built for it. This session covers what a strong API foundation does for AI at scale: fine-grained authorization keeps context retrieval inside its data privacy boundaries, touching only what it's permitted to touch; rate limiting protects vector databases from resource exhaustion; edge caching cuts query latency without extra engineering; and circuit breaking plus canary deployments let teams ship changes without compromising security or compliance. You'll leave with architectural blueprints and real enterprise examples showing how the right API foundation turns governance from a blocker into what lets AI teams move faster. Presented by Kong an AWS Partner, alongside FanDuel. This presentation is brought to you by Kong, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler)
sessions.abstract: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Securing your AI-accelerated software supply chain with AWS Well-Architected
sessions.abstract: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven. AI assistants pull them into your codebase faster than ever, sometimes suggesting packages that don’t exist or shouldn’t be trusted. Attackers exploit this through “slopsquatting.” Supply chain incidents show registries targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. This workshop builds a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar. You replace long-lived credentials with OIDC, sign artifacts with AWS Signer, and govern dependencies with CodeArtifact package groups. You scan AI-generated and human-written code with Amazon Inspector, then detect threats with GuardDuty and Security Hub. You leave with a defense-in-depth blueprint that scales with AI-accelerated development across your environment.

sessions.title: Security leverage at AI velocity: the operating model shift
sessions.abstract: The speed AI gives your developers is also available to attackers, so AI investment is now a security decision as much as an engineering one. This session covers three changes to how security teams work when engineers pair with frontier agents. Agents carry application context across design, code, and pen testing, so security coverage keeps pace with development. When an agent builds a working proof of exploit for a finding, or shows that an existing control already blocks it, the security team no longer has to argue over whether the finding is real, and the false-positive queue shrinks. Agentic development environments also let you put preventive controls on what agents generate. We cover how to adopt these practices and which signals show they're working.

We'll whiteboard the full identity path: SSO through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection—Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, full SIEM auditability.

sessions.title: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
sessions.abstract: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.

sessions.title: Sell to AI agents through AWS Marketplace
sessions.abstract: Today, buyers are using autonomous AI agents for discovery and digital purchases on their behalf. AWS Marketplace enables buyers' agents to discover partner solutions, transact securely, and meet their enterprise governance controls. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.

sessions.title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
sessions.abstract: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

sessions.title: Serverless compute built for the web
sessions.abstract: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, see how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. We cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

sessions.title: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
sessions.abstract: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session we cover where existing serverless patterns hold up without modification, what actually changes, and how to start with what you have and add only what you need. See how the calls you already run can become tools that describe themselves to the agent that uses them. Learn how coding agents and skills make best practices part of every build, and where doing less with AI pays off.

sessions.title: Serverless Java in 2026
sessions.abstract: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. SnapStart and GraalVM native AOT deliver sub-second startup, and Lambda Managed Instances give steady-state JVM workloads full JIT optimization at EC2 economics. In this chalk talk, we go beyond cold starts: discuss refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to serverless, framework choices that work well on Lambda (and ones that don't), and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture.

sessions.title: Serving World Model at scale with AWS Trainium and Native PyTorch
sessions.abstract: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads at scale. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. You'll leave equipped to take world model inference from eager prototyping to compiled deployment using familiar PyTorch workflows.

sessions.abstract: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. This presentation is brought to you by Notion, an AWS Partner.

You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads on Fargate, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.

sessions.title: Shared judgment: security culture for the agentic era

Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. sessions.abstract: Your AI agent works in demos, but can you trust it enough for production? sessions.abstract: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. Enterprise administrators desire to constrain what agents can do without slowing developers down. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.

sessions.title: Simplify Data Analytics operations with AI-powered Apache Spark agents on AWS
sessions.abstract: Running analytics workloads at scale carries a hidden operational tax: teams commonly lose significant engineering time to debugging failures, leave performance and cost improvements on the table, and spend months on each version upgrade. In this talk, we walk through a family of AI-powered agents for AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Athena. The Spark Troubleshooting Agent finds the root cause of a failure and recommends the code or config fix - cutting debugging time from hours to minutes. The Spark Upgrade Agent plans an upgrade, transforms the code, and validates both runtime and data quality - turning months into hours. We share what worked in production for both agents - the design choices, failure modes, and validation strategies that made them reliable - and distill lessons that generalize to any team applying LLMs to complex infrastructure.

We will examine the trade-offs that come with each design choice, so bring your questions!
