First, deploy a 5G standalone core on Amazon EKS using an agent built with the Strands Agents SDK and Amazon Bedrock. Next, operate a closed-loop remediation agent, inject real failures, and observe how it detects, correlates, and resolves problems.

sessions.title: Tenant-isolated agent memory: one IAM policy for AgentCore Memory
sessions.abstract: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

sessions.title: Testing serverless and event-driven applications
sessions.abstract: You're shipping faster with serverless, but your testing strategy hasn't kept up. Local mocks drift from cloud behavior. Integration tests require full deployments. Contract changes between services break downstream consumers silently. In this chalk talk, whiteboard testing approaches that match how serverless developers actually work: unit testing business logic in isolation, integration testing service interactions without deploying everything, and contract testing event schemas between producers and consumers. We cover local versus cloud testing tradeoffs, when each makes sense, and chaos engineering techniques like injecting message delays, duplicates, and out-of-order delivery to catch failures before your users do.

sessions.title: The Agent Harness You Own on AWS for Regulated Industries
sessions.abstract: In regulated industries the model is easy; the governable, auditable, defensible agent is hard. AgentCore ships primitives, but the governance harness you own on top is the real work. We build the rails it does not give you: a fail-closed, blocklist-first permission gate where deny beats a broad allow; a hash-chained audit verifiable off-cloud; and a RACI gate binding every action to a named human. Each maps onto a managed AWS primitive — Identity, Guardrails, Evaluations, Lambda MicroVMs for isolation — naming where the primitive ends and your code begins. You leave with the rails.

This session teaches a per-flow method: does any component need to own the flow end-to-end, including completion, failure compensation, and ordering? Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.

sessions.title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
sessions.abstract: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

This presentation is brought to you by Oxylabs, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit
sessions.abstract: Checkov, trivy, and Prowler check rules someone already wrote. SOC 2 CC6.1 is a sentence open to interpretation. Between them sits the judgment gap, where AI-generated Terraform for S3, CloudFront, API Gateway, and Lambda often lands. We map the gap on the whiteboard together: take real controls from SOC 2 and PCI DSS, set them against what scanner rules verify, and mark what is left over. Then we discuss what closes the remainder: better authoring-side skills, human review, multi-model review, or accepting the risk. Bring a control your team owns; we trace where its enforcement lives, or does not.

sessions.title: The latest innovations in multicloud agent security
sessions.abstract: AI agents are showing up everywhere your teams work, and security teams also want to keep pace. In this session, explore the latest innovations in securing AI across multicloud environments. See how AWS is thinking about the challenges security teams face as AI is used by teams, and the direction it is taking to help them stay ahead. Walk away with a clearer picture of where AI security is heading and practical ways to get ahead of it in your own organization.

sessions.title: The Mathematics of Backlogs: Why Your Queue Will Never Drain
sessions.abstract: Your consumers are healthy, your pods are green - yet your backlog isn't shrinking. Why? Because systems provisioned for steady-state have zero recovery capacity. In this chalk talk, we'll derive the formulas that govern backlog formation and drain, explore the non-linear utilization cliff where small traffic spikes become catastrophic, and work through the real-world complications: retry amplification, stale-message degradation, and multi-stage cascades. Bring your architectures - we'll whiteboard whether they can actually recover from failure, or just survive it.

sessions.title: The Neuron Stack: Enabling open source ML solutions on AWS Trainium
sessions.abstract: The Neuron software stack has evolved into an open source-first architecture. Developers can read, modify, and contribute to the components that compile, optimize, and execute ML workloads on Trainium. This session covers how Neuron enables open source ML solutions on Trainium. We show what's open source, how it integrates with upstream projects like PyTorch and distributed training frameworks, and how developers use these tools without modifications. Attendees leave understanding the Neuron stack, which parts are open source, and how to use and contribute to them.

sessions.abstract: AI for SRE isn’t just a speed or accuracy problem; it’s a problem of deeper understanding. This session explores how team members across different domains in an enterprise can use a shared AI reasoning layer to operate production systems and collaborate effectively to increase reliability. We’ll show how this AI reasoning layer handles the extremes of alert storms and alert silence, catching deployment-triggered anomalies before they cause production impact. Learn how teams are moving beyond reactive dashboards, using state-of-the-art techniques to instantly correlate cross-domain telemetry, execute complex investigations, and achieve proactive reliability in dynamic cloud and hybrid environments. This presentation is brought to you by Ciroos, an AWS Partner.

sessions.abstract: Get hands-on building a complete Physical AI pipeline using the AWS and NVIDIA toolchain. This workshop walks you through each stage—synthetic data generation with Isaac Sim, foundation model training with GR00T and Cosmos, digital twin simulation in Omniverse, edge deployment via IoT Greengrass, multi-robot orchestration with AgentCore, and continuous learning with SageMaker using NVIDIA OSMO. sessions.title: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
sessions.abstract: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.

sessions.title: The Trade Desk's Cloud Journey: AI-Assisted Optimization to AI Agents
sessions.abstract: The Trade Desk operates a real-time advertising platform on AWS, where infrastructure must handle massive scale while making bidding decisions in milliseconds. At that volume, cloud cost optimization is a continuous discipline, not a one-time audit. In this breakout, The Trade Desk shares how it moved from manual cost audits to an AI-assisted approach: an internal MCP server that lets AI agents investigate cost and usage data, surface savings across services like S3, NAT Gateway, EBS, and Graviton, and apply a repeatable method for optimizing workloads over time. You'll see how the team structured the agents, what they found, and where the approach is headed.

sessions.abstract: As AI speeds up releases, continuous security control assurance and detecting threats in millions of telemetry signals get harder. We transformed AWS DevOps Agent into one agent for SRE, SOC and compliance, effectively addressing AI-era cloud security challenges in production. With AWS Config Conformance Packs for compliance-as-code and security MCP for finding triage, it produces point-in-time compliance and well-architected assessments, and drives alarm-triggered agentic SOC investigations within a controlled agent space, automating responses and keeping human-in-the-loop on high-risk mitigations only. You'll learn the methodology to design an agentic compliance and SOC solution that ports seamlessly into your own environment.

sessions.title: Thinking agentic: What developers using Serverless need to know
sessions.abstract: You've been building event-driven, async systems for years. Agents are a new type of consumer in your existing architecture. In this chalk talk, we discuss what actually changes: reframing functions as tools with schema-first interfaces, managing agent state with storage and checkpoints, and handling non-deterministic failures from LLM calls. We walk through a practical path from "I have a serverless app" to "my app has agent capabilities," adding capabilities incrementally without rewriting what already works. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard where agents fit in what you've already built.

sessions.title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB)
sessions.abstract: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with three architectural changes on AWS: Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Threat detection and IR in AgentCore workloads
sessions.abstract: Step into an AWS environment where command-and-control callbacks from agent tools, exfiltrated credentials, and disabled safety guardrails occurred across AgentCore workloads. Your mission: detect, investigate, and respond. Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You'll leave with practical skills to secure AgentCore systems you can trust.

sessions.title: Threat modeling the agentic SDLC: from user story to deployment
sessions.abstract:
"Threat modeling the agentic SDLC with ThreatForest	
Agentic development is speeding up, and traditional threat modeling assumes a person makes the decisions. In this code talk, you follow one process end to end. You threat model a user story with the autonomous threat modeling built into AWS Continuum, carry it through the developer workflow, and take it to deployment. You see how ThreatForest, an agentic tool built on the Strands framework, generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings on its own, and how to build a mitigations catalog your organization can reuse. We also show where traditional threat modeling can be used for agentic systems."

sessions.title: Threat technique catalog for AWS: practical controls for real TTPs
sessions.abstract: Threat actors are evolving faster than ever, leveraging AI-generated exploits and automated attack tooling to move at machine speed. AWS CIRT sees these techniques firsthand across customer incidents of all sizes. The Threat Technique Catalog for AWS (TTC), extending the MITRE ATT&CK framework, documents these recurring TTPs with detection and mitigation guidance specific to AWS. This session covers how to turn observed attacker patterns into an advantage: build actionable detections and mitigations into your security operations before the next incident hits.

sessions.title: Token Counts to Business Impact: Measurable AI Architectures at Scale
sessions.abstract: As AI workloads scale, the question shifts from "what does this cost?" to "is this delivering real value?" The answer depends on your workload, architecture, and adoption maturity. We present progressive architecture patterns using agentic software development — from vibe-coding to cloud agents to self-hosted inference to custom models — with a live demo across the AWS AI Stack, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker HyperPod, and Trainium, showing how the right metrics evolve with your architecture. You'll leave with cost-per-outcome comparisons, spend controls that work at scale, and an ROI measurement framework with architecture patterns to implement across any AI workload.

sessions.title: Token-efficient retrieval for production AI agents (sponsored by Exa)
sessions.abstract: Most agent bills aren't driven by the model,  they're driven by the context it's given. Raw web pages, HTML boilerplate, and 10 blue links padded with irrelevant text quietly multiply token spend and degrade answer quality. This lightning talk walks through how Exa engineered retrieval to hand LLMs exactly the text they need: neural search that returns precise passages instead of whole pages, highlight extraction tuned to the query, and context-budgeting techniques that cut input tokens dramatically without hurting accuracy. Using real production traces, we'll show how token-efficient retrieval changes the economics of agents at scale on AWS, and give you a practical checklist you can apply to any RAG or agent pipeline this week. This presentation is brought to you by Exa, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Tokenomics for AI on AWS: Local inference plus Amazon Bedrock (sponsored by Spectro Cloud)
sessions.abstract: Power users in AI teams building on AWS face the challenge of frontier models delivering the best answers and token costs scaling with adoption. Not every prompt requires frontier models. The ones that do, belong on the best endpoint. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. We will show how routing, quotas, and per-team attribution keep tokenomics predictable, so platform teams can enable AI adoption without inheriting the bill. This presentation is brought to you by Spectro Cloud, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Tokenomics of attacks: how AWS defends you from AI-powered threats
sessions.abstract: AI isn't just transforming how we build, it's transforming how attackers exploit. In this session, AWS threat researchers share the intelligence they observe in real time: the prompts adversaries feed into AI systems, the tokenomics that make AI-powered attacks devastatingly scalable, and the shrinking window between vulnerability disclosure and weaponized exploitation. We'll share first-hand threat intel from MadPot, AWS's globally distributed honeypot network, and show how AWS protects AI-based workloads. You'll learn how AWS Active Threat Defense capabilities proactively block malicious infrastructure before it reaches your workloads, so you can innovate with AI confidently while staying ahead of emerging threats.

sessions.title: Tokenomics: Understanding What Your AI Actually Costs (sponsored by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company)
sessions.abstract: Your AI pilot ran smoothly and stayed on budget. Then you launched, and the invoice was much higher than the estimate. We'll walk through where AI spend actually goes once a system leaves the demo stage, why agentic AI costs differently than a simple chatbot, and how choosing the right model for each task, not just the flagship model for everything, can cut spend dramatically without hurting quality. You'll leave with a practical framework for tracking cost, avoiding common budgeting traps, and having a more confident conversation with finance the next time AI spend comes up. This presentation is brought to you by Mission Cloud, a CDW Company, an AWS Partner.

Leave with a plan for building software with AI, not just a tool list.

In this hands-on builders' session, work alongside a team of consulting agents that guide a human consultant through structured discovery — asking the right questions and validating assumptions — then build out business requirements, generate agent designs and AWS architectures, calculate ROI-backed financial models, and export ready-to-use Statement of Work — all in a single, AI-accelerated workflow you can take straight back to your practice.

sessions.title: Turn autonomous agents into accountable ones
sessions.abstract: Your AI agents pass the demo but struggle in production because of limited accountability and controls. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard a governance framework that closes the loop. You get governed agent accounts with AWS Control Tower, hard API boundaries with AWS Organizations policies, and runtime tool-access controls and behavior scoring in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AWS Config detects drift from policy and triggers automated rollback. You leave with a repeatable, observe-score-remediate pattern for keeping AI agents operating within your policies."

sessions.title: Turn AWS Marketplace listings into self-service buyer journeys
sessions.abstract: Make it easier for customers to find, subscribe and deploy your software in by providing a self-service path from evaluation to purchase. In this session, explore how to transform your AWS Marketplace listing using demos, free trials, AI-guided evaluation and usage-based pricing. Learn the repeatable patterns for reducing procurement delays, measuring buyer progression, activating listings, and directing qualified buyers.

The solution automates the ingestion, transformation, validation, schema mapping, and PII redaction of client actuarial datasets that arrive in different formats, languages, and quality levels. sessions.title: Turn log storage into log intelligence
sessions.abstract: Give your operations teams the full picture without jumping between tools. Learn how to bring logs, metrics, and traces into a unified data store for analytics and improved troubleshooting. Instead of just storing logs and treating logs as text to grep during an outage, use centralization rules that bring telemetry together across accounts and regions, telemetry pipelines that enrich and route data in flight, intelligence tiering that matches storage cost to query value, and AI-assisted log analytics that surface answers instead of waiting for you to ask the right question. This is about making logs work for you — not the other way around. You'll leave with a clear architecture for unified log analytics you can take back to your org and put into production.

sessions.title: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs
sessions.abstract: Organizations planning post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migrations face the same three questions: where do I start my migration plan, which workloads do I prioritize, and how do I get buy-in from leadership? With NIST PQC standards finalized, the algorithm question is settled, the open question is how to plan and fund the transition. In this chalk talk we whiteboard the PQC Readiness Maturity Model: five levels from discovery to quantum-ready, each with measurable milestones. You leave with a practical framework to scope your inventory, prioritize transitions, modernize how you protect data, and build the board narrative that funds your migration program.

sessions.title: Turn your coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore
sessions.abstract: Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex are impressive individually, but in an enterprise they run stateless, isolated from team context, and invisible to governance. AgentCore turns any coding agent into a production system: shared memory so the agent understands your architecture across sessions, microVM isolation so jobs run in parallel without interference, identity propagation so agents access only what they should, and full trace observability so you know what every agent did and why. This session shows what changes when you pair popular coding agents with a production platform, and how our customer deployed this across hundreds of developers.

sessions.title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
sessions.abstract: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?

Cover the key logs and metrics that actually matter, how to read them, and how to set up simple dashboards and alerts that tell you something is wrong before your users do. sessions.title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
sessions.abstract: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

sessions.title: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
sessions.abstract: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.

sessions.title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
sessions.abstract: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.

sessions.title: Unified Commerce Intelligence for Amazon Sellers on Amazon Quick
sessions.abstract: Brands selling on Amazon generate rich signals across commerce and advertising — order trends, catalog performance, competitive pricing, campaign metrics, and customer engagement. The opportunity lies in connecting these signals into a unified view that drives faster, smarter decisions. In this chalk talk, we design an architecture that composes two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — the SP-API MCP Server for Selling Partner operations and the Amazon Ads MCP Server for campaigns and reporting — behind Amazon Qucik as a conversational layer. We'll whiteboard how brands can build cross-domain queries, like correlating ad spend with order velocity or surfacing catalog insights that inform campaign strategy. Leave with production-grade patterns for building agentic commerce workflows tailored to your brand's data

sessions.title: Unified observability with Amazon OpenSearch Service
sessions.abstract: Most teams run observability across fragmented tools: one for metrics, another for logs and traces, each with its own cost model and blind spots. In this session, you work hands-on to consolidate your observability stack on Amazon OpenSearch Service. You integrate Amazon Managed Prometheus for metrics, configure native OpenTelemetry ingestion for traces and logs, and see how a single pane of glass eliminates the context-switching that slows down investigations. Then you optimize for cost and scale: warm tiering, direct query for infrequently accessed data, and O-series instances for log-heavy workloads. Finally, you use AI-powered investigation to perform natural-language root-cause analysis across your unified telemetry and monitor your agents' behavior in production. You leave with a working observability setup that scales, costs less, and investigates faster.

In this chalk talk, we walk through a modern Lakehouse architecture on AWS that combines the cost benefits of data lakes with the governance and performance of data warehouses. We explain how Amazon S3 Tables with managed Apache Iceberg and AWS Glue Catalog semantic search deliver a single governed data foundation supporting agentic AI, traditional AI/ML, and analytics workloads. sessions.title: Unlock cost efficiency with Graviton savings tools
sessions.abstract: While AWS Graviton delivers up to 40% better price-performance, uncovering those savings across your fleet shouldn't take weeks of manual analysis. Building a concrete migration plan for a specific environment is where teams get stuck. The Graviton Savings Dashboard is an Amazon Quick visualization of your Graviton usage, realized savings, and migration opportunities over time. The Graviton Savings Assessment is an open-source skill that any AI coding agent can run against your accounts to produce a prioritized migration roadmap on demand. This lightning talk demonstrates both tools against a real-world scenario, showing how to analyze compute usage, visualize potential savings, and turn efficiency insights into actionable migration plans you can use to accelerate your Graviton adoption.

sessions.title: Vector search, agents, and image matching with Amazon DynamoDB
sessions.abstract: Amazon DynamoDB supports native vector search, enabling semantic queries, agentic recommendations, and image-based matching without additional infrastructure. In this session, explore how to design a single-table data model for a recipe database, bulk-load thousands of items with embeddings, and build three vector-powered features: semantic search, a smart recommendation agent, and image-based meal matching. Learn how to configure vector indexes, composite keys, and global secondary indexes on a fully serverless stack, and leave with reusable patterns to add vector search to your own DynamoDB workloads. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
sessions.abstract: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.

sessions.title: Vertiv’s Amazon Quick Journey: Scaling Agentic AI Globally with Deloitte & AWS (sponsored by Deloitte)
sessions.abstract: Vertiv, a global digital infrastructure company, faced fragmented AI experimentation, limited accessibility, and complex enterprise integrational barriers preventing consistent scaling. Vertiv's AI journey began with VeGA, a GenAI platform turned agentic with their recent release of VeGA 3.0. Powered by Amazon Quick, it enables employees to generate content, automate workflows, and create custom applications. In one year, nearly one-third of the workforce was registered in VeGA, spanning functions across all functions and regions. Attendees will learn the architectural blueprint for evolving from basic AI assistants to intelligent agentic systems, including connectors used, data streamlining strategies, and practical implementation steps. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Virtualization Architecture Behind AgentCore's Runtime Security Model
sessions.abstract: Journey into the sophisticated virtualization architecture that powers AgentCore's runtime security model. This session examines the intricate mechanics of session isolation at the virtualization layer, exploring advanced techniques in compute and memory virtualization, virtual machine snapshot optimization, and virtual memory deduplication. Drawing from operating systems research and systems security principles, we'll demonstrate how these components work together to create robust security boundaries for agent workloads. Attendees will gain deep technical insights into the mathematical and systems-level concepts that position AWS at the forefront of secure agent runtime architectures, showcasing our industry-leading approach to securing code execution in agent environments.

sessions.title: Visa: Building autonomous defense for payments security in the agentic AI era
sessions.abstract: Visa secures one of the world's largest payment ecosystems, processing over $14 trillion across 300+ billion transactions annually. As AI-powered threats evolve, Visa is reimagining cybersecurity through hybrid-cloud architecture with 70+ controls framework, AI-driven operations, and an agentic control plane designed for autonomous defense. Built on an Agentic harness with Zero-Trust principles and AWS capabilities, such as Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Nitro Enclaves, and cloud-agnostic security controls, Visa continuously detects and mitigates risk across its cloud environment. Discover how Visa is building a security foundation for the agentic AI era, protecting today's payments ecosystem while enabling AI-powered applications and autonomous workloads.

sessions.title: Visualize and interpret domain knowledge graphs using AI
sessions.abstract: Complex systems like supply chains, energy grids, and decarbonization efforts are difficult to model because relationships between actors are hidden across siloed data. A knowledge graph can surface these connections, helping organizations simulate what-if scenarios and act on high impact opportunities. In this builder session, use Amazon Neptune to construct an ontology-typed knowledge graph that maps stakeholder dependencies and sustainability regulatory impacts. Then simulate competing interventions and use an Amazon Bedrock agent to interpret which action drives the broadest impact. Leave with a reusable pattern for modeling complex systems and identifying high-leverage intervention points.

sessions.title: Visualizing agent identity privileges to monitor multi-agent behavior
sessions.abstract: If one of your AI agents quietly gained admin-level access right now, would you know? In multi-agent systems, each handoff between agents can widen permissions, and traditional monitoring won't catch it. In this code talk, we build a real-time graph answering three questions: who are my agents, what can each one do, and what can they reach through each other? We connect IAM roles, Cedar policies, and CloudWatch data into one visual map, then add alerts that fire the instant any permission chain exceeds what you defined. You leave with the tool that catches it first.

sessions.title: Visualizing multi-tenant isolation: Catch your noisy neighbors
sessions.abstract: Managing multi-tenant platforms forces trade-offs between cost, complexity, and performance. This session tackles two common challenges: tenant data isolation and the noisy-neighbor problem. Starting from a single-tenant architecture, you consolidate into a shared Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, building isolation through Cognito-issued JWTs, Lambda-based dynamic policy generation, IAM authentication, and RDS Proxy connection pooling. Then you implement queuing tiers with Amazon SQS to manage load. Visualize real-time request flows, data isolation, and noisy-neighbor effects on your own dynamic architecture simulation and a central 16,000-LED display. Bring your laptop to participate.

sessions.title: VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts with AWS Transform
sessions.abstract: Many organizations struggle to migrate VMware workloads due to complex dependencies, network translation challenges, and the need to support both cloud and on-premises targets. In this workshop, you use AWS Transform MGN, an agentic AI service, to execute an end-to-end VMware migration to Amazon EC2 and AWS Outposts. You work through AI-driven discovery, dependency mapping, intelligent wave planning, automated network conversion, and orchestrated execution. See how Trianz's Concierto platform also integrates with AWS Transform to streamline migration to AWS Outposts with automated orchestration and operational governance.

sessions.title: Warehouse Alchemy: How Eni's AI agents cut days of sourcing to minutes
sessions.abstract: Eni operates one of the world's most complex upstream supply chains, managing exploration and production materials across warehouses on multiple continents. Tubular items alone represent €1.5 billion out of a €2.5 billion inventory — scattered across dozens of facilities with fragmented visibility. Engineers searching for available spare parts faced a manual, days-long process of cross-referencing spreadsheets, navigating import restrictions, certifications, third-party stock, and delivery schedules — often resulting in unnecessary new purchases while surplus materials sat idle in distant warehouses. With Eni's expansion into fast-track development, biofuel production, and CCUS, the traditional material management approach couldn't keep pace with the speed and complexity of global operations.

sessions.abstract: Modernizing SQL Server and its dependent .NET applications to Aurora PostgreSQL typically requires months of manual effort across schema conversion, stored procedure rewriting, and application code changes. In this code talk, see how AWS Transform uses agentic AI to automate this journey end-to-end. Through a live walkthrough, we'll showcase complex schema transformations, T-SQL to PL/pgSQL stored procedure conversions, Entity Framework provider updates, and wave-based orchestration of multi-database estates with human-in-the-loop validation checkpoints. Ask questions throughout. Leave with patterns for modernizing SQL Server at scale.

sessions.title: What AI agents need from an application backend
sessions.abstract: AI agents build applications differently than people do. They work from code, call APIs, run in parallel, and keep working after you close your laptop. In this session, learn what a backend has to provide for an agent to carry an application from first prompt to production: schema and configuration as code the agent can read and change, serverless infrastructure with nothing to size or provision, data APIs and authentication that work on the first call, isolated environments for every experiment the agent runs, logs the agent can query when something breaks, and approval steps that keep destructive changes in your hands.

sessions.title: What Breaks First: Detection Engineering Lessons at AWS Scale (sponsored by Datadog)
sessions.abstract: Tighten the detection rule and you miss the variant. Loosen them and you drown the on-call. Deviate too far either way and you risk missing attackers and getting compromised. FanDuel handled adjustments by hand for years, until attackers started moving faster than the tuning backlog. Join FanDuel and Datadog to see detection rebuilt around automation: SIEM logic as code, orchestrated enrichment and triage, vulnerability workflows in the same pipeline. Attendees will leave with practical patterns for scaling detection engineering, reducing analyst toil, and knowing where AI helps and where it creates new work. This presentation is brought to you by Datadog, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: What Building an SRE Agent Taught Us About Agents at Scale
sessions.abstract: Anyone can wire up an agent, but operating one safely and cheaply across thousands of sessions is where developer craft begins. Grounded in a production SRE agent we built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents SDK, this session dissects engineering around agentic models: session isolation, context management, and least privilege identity. What broke, and how we fixed it: an agent with too much access, context bloat that wrecked cost, a crash during a tool call that forced durable recovery. You will see where architectures leak, how to evaluate on production traces, and tradeoffs behind resilient agent infrastructure.

sessions.title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
sessions.abstract: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

sessions.title: What FanDuel learned running containers on hundreds of AWS Outposts
sessions.abstract: Running containerized workloads across dozens of AWS Local Zones and hundreds of AWS Outposts demands operational patterns that hold up at fleet scale. In this session, learn how FanDuel operates Amazon EKS across a huge hybrid edge fleet with a focus on high availability, patching, observability, service disruption handling, and autoscaling. The session digs into how workloads respond gracefully to service link and hardware disruptions, and how autoscaling behaves when compute is fixed and on-rack. Discover the operational model that keeps a large edge fleet healthy without growing the platform team at the same rate.

sessions.abstract: Organizations are deploying copilots, AI agents, and LLM-driven workflows faster than governance and security can adapt. Non-deterministic AI creates a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data, and runtime behavior, and acts as both defensive force multiplier and adversarial accelerant. Static guardrails are necessary but insufficient: they miss novel behavior, unsafe tool use, and risk that only surfaces when AI interacts with identities and downstream systems. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI at runtime, using NIST's Secure/Defend/Thwart framing: an identity control plane for agents, least-privilege and JIT access, runtime observability, behavior detection, and autonomous investigation and containment. We'll share a blueprint for a minimum viable AI security baseline, and why behavioral oversight is the decisive layer for securing AI at scale. sessions.title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
sessions.abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

sessions.title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
sessions.abstract: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

sessions.title: When security, speed, and trust all matter: Lessons from Project Glasswing
sessions.abstract: In 2026, a frontier AI model demonstrated it could discover and chain software exploits at machine speed. This new reality forced the industry to confront an entirely new class of offensive capability. In this session, learn how AWS Security's Office of the CISO engaged executive customers and partners to build playbooks to help assess AI-era vulnerability management and remediation. We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

sessions.title: When Software Builds and Improves Itself (sponsored by Factory)
sessions.abstract: Software is becoming more than something companies build. It is becoming the system through which they improve. The next generation of software factories will turn business signals into production software, measure the outcomes, and use those outcomes to improve each cycle of development. Engineers set the goals, architecture, policies, and approval gates, while the system handles execution and continuously improves itself. Factory cofounder Eno Reyes will share what this future looks like, what has to be true to build it, and why self-improving software will fundamentally change how every company operates. This presentation is brought to you by Factory, an AWS Partner.

times.room: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

sessions.title: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT)
sessions.abstract: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Not every workflow needs an agent, and applying agentic AI where it doesn’t fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. We’ll ideate on a scoring framework that assesses the inherent nature of the work to reveal where agentic approaches thrive. You’ll apply the PERCEIVE-REASON-ACT pattern for isolating AI reasoning from orchestration, and walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately.

sessions.title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
sessions.abstract: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

You decide what to trace and build the dashboards that connect a symptom to its root cause. Leave with skills to trace any slowdown across layers in a single pane.

sessions.abstract: Off the shelf models work for prototyping, but production forces a choice, which technique, which service, which tradeoffs. In this chalk talk, we work through the decision framework live. When Supervised Fine Tuning is enough, when DPO or RLAIF earns its added cost, and when RLVR or multi-turn RL is the right call, and what data each demands. We will learn how to choose across SageMaker Serverless Customization, Training Jobs, HyperPod, and Bedrock Custom Model Import based on traffic, budget, and control needs. sessions.title: Who Checks the Agents? Quality and Governance for the Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Qodo)
sessions.abstract: Agents now plan work, write code, generate tests and open PRs—sometimes without human review before production. Yet most teams rely on a trust model built for a slower SDLC: one reviewer, one merge gate and one chance to catch what went wrong. That model fails when agents operate at every stage and final review can’t reveal what happened upstream. This session treats trust as a property of the pipeline, not a final checkpoint. We’ll explore why the system generating code shouldn’t also verify it, how to turn tribal standards into enforceable, auditable controls, and where independent review belongs between spec and deploy. Key takeaways: Why end-stage review fails in an agent-driven SDLC. How to enforce and trace standards across teams, repos and AI tools. How to decide what can merge automatically, what needs human review and how to document that decision for auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Qodo, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Who’s Pulling the Strings? Securing GitHub from Rogue AI Agents (sponsored by Zscaler)
sessions.abstract: With the rise of autonomous AI agents like Devin, Cursor, and Amazon Q, the security boundary has shifted from the network perimeter directly to the developer's workspace. These AI tools and automated integration pipelines establish dynamic, encrypted connections straight to GitHub, third-party repositories, and cloud workloads—creating blind spots that legacy firewalls cannot see. Join us as we map out this highly interconnected AI developer ecosystem and showcase why traditional security fails. We will share a unified, proxy-based Zero Trust architecture that inspects encrypted developer traffic, secures access to critical repositories, and isolates untrusted AI actions. You’ll leave with an actionable blueprint to protect your code, APIs, and AI integrations while maintaining peak developer velocity. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Who's Your Security MVP? Here's How AI Ranks Them (sponsored by Trellix)
sessions.abstract: Yeah, yeah, AI SOC, we get it. But what really goes into getting wins out of AI in security vs saving a couple of clicks? This talk will show the importance of small (dumb) LLM's and how they create opportunities for secops by allowing you to use more tokens, anywhere you want. It will demo how you can go beyond enriching a few alerts to stack rank your most valuable security tools in an ROI thunderdome. You'll learn the AI confidence guardrail framework you need so you to actually start taking actions on your behalf without accidentally deleting all your VM's when you asked it to "eliminate all vulnerabilities." Seeing is believing, so there will be real-world demos of where AI works, where it doesn't, and why--bring your 3D glasses. This presentation is brought to you by Trellix, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and  Ontology Patterns on AWS
sessions.abstract: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.

sessions.title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB)
sessions.abstract: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Winning the DDoS Game: defend your app under real-time attack
sessions.abstract: Compete in a team-based environment where you face real-time threats aimed at your web application. Use the latest capabilities in AWS WAF and AWS Shield to mitigate HTTP floods, web exploits, and malicious bots that disrupt your customers. This risk-free event puts teamwork to the test as you work under pressure. Watch a real-time scoreboard as your team works through each level. Whether it's volumetric attacks or the new wave of AI-driven traffic hitting your APIs, you'll leave prepared to defend against what's coming next. The most effective team earns a prize!

sessions.title: Winning the War on Fraud with Network-Powered Intelligence (sponsored by Vonage, Part of Ericsson)
sessions.abstract: Fraud is winning. SIM swaps have surged over 1,000%; synthetic identity cases are up 60% year-over-year, legacy OTP defenses are structurally broken — and fraudsters know it. Every industry feels it. Banks, healthcare providers, retailers, rideshare and delivery platforms, all fighting the same battle, all demanding the same answer: security that doesn't sacrifice the customer experience. As the first and only communications and Network API provider to achieve the AWS Financial Services Industry Competency, Vonage is changing the equation. Discover how enterprises are moving to a model where identity is verified silently at the network layer, before fraud happens. Built on AWS, powered by direct carrier intelligence. This presentation is brought to you by Vonage, Part of Ericsson, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
sessions.abstract: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: leveraging native OIDC providers from Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries, and using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters. We walk through architecture decisions, trust policy design, and security best practices for each approach - covering GCP Workload Identity, Microsoft Entra ID federation, and cross-cluster OIDC. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.

sessions.title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
sessions.abstract: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

sessions.title: World Models & Physical AI: The Next Frontier in Intelligent Systems
sessions.abstract: World models—AI systems that simulate and predict complex environments—are emerging with new modalities including Video, Vision, Language, Action to power physical AI, autonomous systems, and real-time video generation. From humanoid robotics to immersive entertainment, these models are transforming how machines perceive, think, and interact with the physical world. In this panel, hear from researchers and customers on how they're building and deploying world models in production, the business opportunities they unlock, and the unique technical challenges they present. Learn how AWS AI infrastructure powers these use cases at scale with speed, efficiency, and automatic fault recovery.

sessions.abstract: Agentic applications need different access patterns and tooling than traditional apps. Teams often stitch together several tools and act as the human orchestrator just to answer a basic question: is my agent doing what the business needs? That gets harder when the agent runs on one cloud and calls models or APIs on another. In this session, we show how CloudWatch Omni brings AI agents and applications across clouds into one view, accelerating root cause whether its due to performance, availability or response quality.

sessions.title: You cannot write the eval for a failure you have not seen yet (sponsored by Arize AI)
sessions.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge works beautifully when you already know what you're looking for. You write the rubric, validate it against human labels, and it catches the failure you designed it to catch. But agents in production don't fail the way you anticipated. They fail as they meet new tools, new users, and environments that shifted underneath them, and every new failure arrives after the rubric was written. This talk argues the evaluation layer itself must become agentic. Instead of specifying a metric, you describe the behavior you want, and a judge with tool access inspects the trace, finds the spans that matter, classifies what went wrong, and generates labels you can monitor against. We'll cover why this became viable only recently, where it fails, and how to keep an agentic judge honest against human labels, so you know when to reach for one and how to validate it. This presentation is brought to you by Arize AI, an AWS Partner.

sessions.title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
sessions.abstract: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

sessions.abstract: Stockouts and overstocks quietly erode margin for retail and CPG brands, driving lost sales, markdowns, and working capital tied up in the wrong inventory. Traditional forecasting models take months to train and tune, and struggle with the cold-start problem for new products and locations. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to architect zero-shot demand forecasting pipelines using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio with the Chronos 2 time-series foundation model, developed by the Amazon Science team and proven on Amazon's own retail and CPG demand at scale, requiring no historical model training. We walk through the end-to-end design: SMUS notebooks for rapid experimentation, Chronos 2 for multi-variate time series prediction, and Amazon Quick Suite for conversational analytics that let planners explore forecasts in natural language..

sessions.title: Zero to multimodal in 60 mins: Building Live Sync on Connect Customer
sessions.abstract: What does it take to synchronize a live voice conversation with a real-time visual interface — and make it feel like magic? In this chalk talk, we'll answer that question by building one from scratch. Starting from first principles, we'll construct a fully functional voice AI agent that leverages the patented Live Sync on Amazon Connect Customer: the signaling that keeps voice and visual in lock-step, the state machine that drives bi-directional interaction, and the rendering layer that turns conversational intent into on-screen UI in real time. No slides, no hand-waving — just building, live, from zero to a working multimodal agent in 60 minutes. At the end, we'll deploy what we built and every phone in the room becomes a live demo.

sessions.title: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
sessions.abstract: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier; devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.

sessions.title: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
sessions.abstract: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.
